jobs.title: Manager, Internal Controls
jobs.excerpt: Job Description: The Manager, Internal Controls will be based in India.
jobs.description:
Job Description:

The Manager, Internal Controls will be based in India. In this position, you will report to the Head of Internal Controls.Nextpower is seeking a Manager, Internal Control to lead the company’s SOX and internal controls work across assigned business processes. This role manages and develops a team of internal controls professionals while partnering with Finance, Accounting, IT, Operations, Legal, and external auditors. The manager sets team priorities, oversees routine operating plans and costs, and guides risk assessments, control design and testing, remediation, and readiness efforts. The role requires sound judgment, strong knowledge of business processes and financial reporting, and the ability to turn control requirements into practical solutions.

Watch “Culture is our Passion” to learn more about us

We are looking for someone who demonstrates:

  • Passionate drive to innovate and create

· Integrity to the core

· Enthusiastic customer focus

  • Consistent interactive teamwork
  • Desire for continuous improvement and top performance.

Here is a glimpse of what you will do:

People leadership and team operations

  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of internal controls professionals; set clear goals, assign work, review quality and timeliness, provide ongoing feedback, and support performance and career development.
  • Plan and allocate team capacity against monthly and routine operating plans; monitor milestones, workload, and costs, and raise resource or schedule risks with leadership.
  • Apply company policies consistently, address routine team matters, and recommend improvements to procedures and practices within the function.

SOX program and control environment

  • Lead and contribute to SOX risk assessments, annual planning and scoping, readiness activities, and the ongoing maturity of the SOX program.
  • Oversee assigned process areas and ensure the team understands related business activities, risks, controls, company policies, and applicable accounting and reporting requirements.
  • Guide process walkthroughs, tests of design, and tests of operating effectiveness; review workpapers and documentation for accuracy, completeness, and consistency.
  • Partner with process owners to evaluate existing processes, identify control gaps and improvement opportunities, and design practical controls that address risk and exposure.
  • Assess new projects, systems, and process changes for SOX impact; coordinate with cross-functional partners to define and complete readiness actions.
  • Maintain accurate SOX documentation, including process narratives, flowcharts, risk-control matrices, and evidence of control performance.

Issues, remediation, and partnership

  • Evaluate audit findings and control deficiencies; analyze relevant facts, assess potential impact, and develop and track remediation plans with SOX leadership and accountable stakeholders.
  • Coordinate with internal and external auditors and support requests related to SOX, internal controls, and financial reporting.
  • Explain control requirements, findings, and recommendations to process owners, peer groups, and leaders; build cooperation and influence timely action across functions.
  • Monitor progress against commitments, resolve routine execution issues, and escalate significant risks, delays, or resource needs.

Governance and continuous improvement

  • Stay current on relevant SOX, PCAOB, COSO, U.S. GAAP, and public-company reporting requirements and emerging practices.
  • Recommend updates to team procedures and control practices based on changes in the business, systems, risks, and applicable requirements.

Here is some of what you will need (required):

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • (10-12) years of related experience in accounting, external or internal audit, SOX, or internal controls, preferably across public accounting and corporate environments.
  • Experience directly managing or formally leading employees, including assigning work, coaching, providing feedback, and supporting performance and development.
  • Working knowledge of SOX 404, internal control frameworks such as COSO, audit requirements including PCAOB standards, and U.S. GAAP.
  • Experience assessing business process risks, designing or evaluating controls, leading walkthroughs and control testing, documenting results, and driving remediation.
  • Ability to analyze complex or incomplete information, exercise sound judgment, and interpret requirements to recommend appropriate procedures and actions.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain technical control matters and gain cooperation from cross-functional partners.
  • Demonstrated ability to organize team work, manage multiple timelines, and deliver against recurring plans

Here are a few of our preferred experiences:

  • CPA, CIA, or other relevant professional certification.
  • Experience supporting a public company’s SOX program through growth, system implementation, acquisition, or process transformation.
  • Experience with internal controls over financial reporting across finance, accounting, IT, or operational processes.

At Nextpower, we are driving the global energy transition with an integrated clean energy technology platform that combines intelligent structural, electrical, and digital solutions for utility-scale power plants. Our comprehensive portfolio enables faster project delivery, higher performance, and greater reliability, helping our customers capture the full value of solar power. Our talented worldwide teams are redefining how solar power plants are designed, built, and operated every day with smart technology, data-driven insights, and advanced automation. Together, we’re building the foundation for the world’s next generation of clean energy infrastructure.

We are Nextpower

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States. This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Windchill Technical Developer
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)

Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $130,000–$180,000 Annually (based on experience)
Experience Required:10+ Years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary

Bright Vision Technologies is seeking a highly experienced Windchill Technical Developer with 10+ years of experience in designing, developing, and supporting enterprise Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) solutions using PTC Windchill. The ideal candidate will possess deep expertise in Java, Windchill Java APIs, PTC customization frameworks, workflows, lifecycle management, and platform extensions, with a proven ability to build scalable, upgrade-friendly, and high-performance PLM solutions. This role combines hands-on development with technical leadership, architecture guidance, and mentorship across enterprise Windchill implementations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain advanced Java customizations within PTC Windchill, including custom services, listeners, processors, validators, helpers, and business logic extensions.
  • Extend the Windchill data model by implementing custom object types, attributes, relationships, and metadata using Type and Attribute Management (TAM).
  • Develop custom user interface components including JSP, HTML, JavaScript, custom actions, tables, wizard pages, dashboards, and UI extensions.
  • Build asynchronous processing solutions using Windchill queues, background processors, scheduled tasks, and event-driven components.
  • Design and implement complex workflow expressions, robot delegates, lifecycle automation, and approval processes using Java and Windchill workflow frameworks.
  • Optimize application performance through Java profiling, query optimization, caching strategies, JVM tuning, and efficient API utilization.
  • Ensure all customizations follow PTC-supported development practices, minimizing technical debt and enabling seamless future upgrades.
  • Lead modernization initiatives by migrating legacy customizations to supported PTC frameworks while maintaining backward compatibility and minimizing business disruption.
  • Perform architecture reviews, code reviews, and technical assessments to maintain engineering quality, scalability, security, and maintainability.
  • Collaborate with functional consultants, solution architects, PLM administrators, and business stakeholders to translate complex business requirements into robust technical solutions.
  • Provide production support, troubleshoot complex issues, perform root cause analysis, and drive long-term platform stability.
  • Create and maintain comprehensive technical documentation, architecture diagrams, operational runbooks, coding standards, and design specifications.
  • Mentor development teams through code reviews, technical workshops, design sessions, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related technical discipline.
  • 10+ years of professional Java development experience, including extensive hands-on experience with PTC Windchill customization and platform development.
  • Expert-level proficiency with Windchill Java API, PTC customization frameworks, and Windchill extension mechanisms.
  • Deep understanding of Windchill architecture, data model, lifecycle management, workflow engine, access control, and object model.
  • Strong expertise in Java, object-oriented design, multithreading, performance tuning, and enterprise software development.
  • Extensive experience with JSP, HTML, JavaScript, and Windchill client-side customization.
  • Hands-on experience with Type and Attribute Management (TAM), Object Initialization Rules (OIRs), lifecycle templates, and workflow customization.
  • Strong SQL skills with experience supporting Oracle or Microsoft SQL Server databases.
  • Proven experience supporting Windchill upgrades, migrations, performance optimization, and enterprise production environments.
  • Excellent troubleshooting, communication, documentation, collaboration, and technical leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • PTC Windchill Certified Professional or equivalent certification.
  • Experience with PTC ThingWorx, Windchill RV&S (Integrity), Creo, Arbortext, or other PTC product integrations.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, Git, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Actions for Windchill development.
  • Experience deploying or supporting Windchill in AWS, Microsoft Azure, or other cloud environments.
  • Knowledge of enterprise integration patterns, REST APIs, messaging technologies, and PLM-to-ERP integrations.
  • Experience supporting regulated industries such as Aerospace, Automotive, Medical Devices, Industrial Manufacturing, or Defense.
How to Apply

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend are seeking a dedicated Health & Safety Senior Analyst to join our construction management consultancy. The ideal candidate will be responsible for ensuring that all health and safety regulations are adhered to across our construction projects. This role involves developing and implementing safety policies, conducting site inspections, and providing guidance to project teams to maintain a safe working environment.

What you’ll do

  • Proactive Safety in Design Review: Read, interpret, and perform meticulous safety reviews of architectural drawing sets, technical design specifications, engineering drawings, floor layouts, elevations, and Life Safety Plans across all project phases (Concept & Schematic, Design Development, and Construction Documents).

  • Lifecycle Hazard Mitigation: Apply Safety in Design (Safety in Design) principles and the Hierarchy of Controls to eliminate or substitute hazards at the design stage, prioritizing physical engineering solutions over administrative controls and personal protective equipment (PPE). Evaluate designs to ensure safety across all lifecycle phases: construction, installation, commissioning, operation, maintenance, and eventual demolition.

  • Hazard Identification & Workshops: Lead or actively participate in systematic, multidisciplinary hazard identification exercises. Facilitate collaborative sessions with architects, engineers, construction managers, maintenance technicians, and operational end-users to ensure designed systems are highly practical and error-proof.

  • Regulatory & Code Verification: Verify that all facility and equipment designs strictly adhere to applicable local, regional, national, and international standards, codes, and legislation, including but not limited to OSHA, NFPA, IBC, and ADA regulations.

  • Operational Program Administration: Ability to manage regional HSE programs, initiatives, plans, playbooks, and standardized procedures to satisfy regulatory requirements and meet the evolving safety needs of CBRE client accounts across the market area.

  • Performance Monitoring & Analytics: Oversee Safety in Design performance monitoring, capturing project lessons to refine client design guides and safety standards for continuous improvement. Track and analyze injury, illness, and incident data to provide leadership and regional management with actionable guidance on compliance, trends, and improvement strategies.

  • Operational Leadership & Coordination: Establish work schedules and assign specific safety-related tasks to team members. Coordinate work efforts and impact the quality of both individual output and the wider team's performance, ensuring objectives are met within standardized procedures and established timelines.

  • Multi-disciplinary Knowledge Synthesis: Synthesize complex technical data and safety insights spanning multiple professional disciplines—such as mechanical/electrical engineering, occupational hygiene, and materials chemistry—to engineer cohesive, inherently safer facility solutions.

  • Risk Transfer & Safety Handover: Provide robust safety oversight during commissioning and handover processes. Ensure that critical risk control information developed during the design phase is successfully documented and transferred to operational end-users and facility maintenance teams.

  • RISE Values & Communication: Lead by example and consistently model professional behaviors aligned with CBRE RISE Values (Respect, Integrity, Service, Excellence). Translate complex technical HSE details and risk parameters into clear, straightforward communication for non-technical stakeholders and client teams in routine and challenging situations.

  • Education & Experience: A Bachelor's Degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Engineering, Construction Management, Science, or a related technical discipline is preferred. An equivalent blend of formal education and professional experience will be considered. Candidates must demonstrate 2-5 years of relevant experience. In lieu of a degree, a combination of experience and education will be considered.

  • Technical Drawing Literacy: Demonstrate ability to read, interpret, and perform safety-focused reviews of complex multi-disciplinary architectural drawing sets, structural/mechanical elevations, design instructions, scope of works documents, and technical construction specifications.

Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Senior Travel & Purchasing Coordinator to manage travel-authorization and purchasing-request documentation for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This role prepares and performs quality-control reviews of Travel Authorization Requests, Requests to Initiate Purchase, and Consent to Purchase requests while tracking Government concurrence, purchasing activity, travel status, costs, and supporting documentation.

The Senior Travel & Purchasing Coordinator will work closely with program leadership, travelers, task leads, finance, procurement, subcontractors, and Government stakeholders to ensure requests are complete, accurate, timely, and compliant with applicable task order requirements. The successful candidate will maintain organized records, monitor approval workflows, support trip reporting, and provide accurate data for program reports and Task Order Management Portal dashboards.

This position is remote, with preference given to candidates located in or near Chicago.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Senior Travel & Purchasing Coordinator will:

  • Prepare, review, and process Travel Authorization Requests, Requests to Initiate Purchase, and Consent to Purchase requests.
  • Perform quality-control reviews to verify that requests are complete, accurate, adequately supported, and submitted using the required templates.
  • Coordinate request development and correction with travelers, task leads, program leadership, finance, procurement, and subcontractors.
  • Route requests through established approval workflows and track Government review and concurrence.
  • Confirm that travel and purchases do not proceed before required Government concurrence is received.
  • Maintain current logs of submitted, pending, approved, returned, rejected, completed, and closed requests.
  • Monitor request dates, approval status, funding information, costs, vendors, travelers, destinations, and other required data.
  • Support timely submission of travel and purchasing requests to allow adequate Government review.
  • Track whether requested purchases involve commercial or non-commercial products or services.
  • Maintain documentation supporting commerciality determinations, purchase approvals, and associated cost tracking.
  • Track tools and other direct-cost purchases from initial request through approval, acquisition, invoicing, and closeout.
  • Maintain travel records, including traveler name, location, trip duration, purpose, approval authority, estimated cost, actual cost, and destination point of contact.
  • Prepare, coordinate, consolidate, and track trip reports requested by the Government.
  • Reconcile travel and purchasing records with financial reports, invoices, approval documentation, and Task Order Management Portal data.
  • Provide travel and purchasing information for Monthly Status Reports, Program Management Reviews, spend plans, forecasts, and other program-management products.
  • Maintain accurate portal content, dashboards, approval records, supporting documents, and audit-ready files.
  • Identify incomplete documentation, approaching deadlines, delayed approvals, cost discrepancies, and other workflow risks.
  • Communicate request status, required corrections, approval decisions, and outstanding actions to relevant stakeholders.
  • Develop and maintain travel and purchasing procedures, checklists, templates, trackers, and document-control standards.
  • Support the transfer of travel and purchasing records, procedures, and open actions during transition-in and transition-out activities.
  • Protect sensitive Government, financial, procurement, travel, and personnel information.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Minimum of 8 years of relevant professional experience.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Administration, Logistics, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience coordinating Government travel, purchasing, procurement, logistics, document management, or administrative workflows.
  • Experience preparing or processing Travel Authorization Requests, Requests to Initiate Purchase, Consent to Purchase requests, or comparable approval packages.
  • Experience performing quality-control reviews of travel, purchasing, or financial documentation.
  • Experience supporting Department of Defense, federal civilian, or other Government contracts.
  • Knowledge of Government concurrence and approval requirements for contractor travel and purchases.
  • Familiarity with the Federal Travel Regulation, Joint Travel Regulations, Department of State Standardized Regulations, or comparable Government travel guidance.
  • Experience tracking tools, travel, other direct costs, vendors, approvals, and expenditures by CLIN or contract period.
  • Experience preparing, consolidating, or maintaining formal trip reports.
  • Experience distinguishing and tracking commercial and non-commercial products or services.
  • Experience maintaining audit-ready records, approval histories, and supporting documentation.
  • Experience supporting firm-fixed-price, fixed-price-award-fee, travel, tools, or other direct-cost CLINs.
  • Experience maintaining content in document repositories, program portals, dashboards, or automated approval workflows.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams.
  • Experience with SharePoint, Power BI, Adobe Acrobat, workflow-management tools, or comparable collaboration platforms.
  • Strong document-control, records-management, and quality-assurance capabilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong organizational, coordination, and time-management skills.
  • High attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, completeness, and regulatory compliance.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent requests, deadlines, approvals, and follow-up actions.
  • Ability to identify documentation gaps and communicate required corrections clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with travelers, program leadership, finance, procurement, subcontractors, and Government stakeholders.
  • Ability to work independently while maintaining accountability, discretion, and consistent follow-through.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.

However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.

jobs.description:
Our world is transforming, and PTC is leading the way. Our software brings the physical and digital worlds together, enabling companies to improve operations, create better products, and empower people in all aspects of their business.

Our people make all the difference in our success. Today, we are a global team of nearly 7,000 and our main objective is to create opportunities for our team members to explore, learn, and grow – all while seeing their ideas come to life and celebrating the differences that make us who we are and the work we do possible.

PTC is seeking an experienced Test Manager to join our Professional Services organization. In this role, you will lead quality assurance, test strategy, validation planning, and test execution for customers implementing PTC solutions.

You will work closely with customers, project managers, and delivery teams to ensure solutions are validated against business, regulatory, and technical requirements. You will help customers improve product quality, reduce delivery risk, accelerate time-to-value, and establish scalable testing and quality management practices.


Key Responsibilities

Test Strategy & Governance

  • Define and govern end-to-end test strategies for customer implementations.
  • Establish testing frameworks, methodologies, standards, tooling, and best practices.
  • Develop risk-based testing approaches aligned with customer objectives and compliance requirements.
  • Ensure traceability among requirements, risks, test cases, defects, and validation evidence.

Quality Planning & Delivery

  • Support project delivery teams in developing comprehensive test plans covering functional, integration, system, user acceptance, performance, and regression testing.
  • Monitor testing progress and communicate quality status to stakeholders.

Test & Quality Consulting

  • Advise customers and partners on test management best practices.
  • Help customers design and implement test management processes.
  • Guide customers on validation approaches for regulated and safety-critical environments.
  • Support customer adoption of quality engineering and continuous testing practices.

Defect & Risk Management

  • Establish defect management processes and reporting standards.
  • Facilitate defect triage and prioritization.
  • Track quality metrics and project risks throughout implementation.
  • Recommend mitigation strategies to improve product and project quality.

Continuous Improvement

  • Contribute to the development of test service offerings, accelerators, and best practices.
  • Capture lessons learned from customer engagements and apply them to future delivery approaches.
  • Support field readiness initiatives and cross-functional quality improvement efforts.

Customer Escalation Support

  • Serve as a quality advisor during critical customer situations and escalations.
  • Support root cause analysis and corrective action planning.
  • Partner with engineering, support, and delivery teams to resolve complex quality issues.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in test management, quality assurance, or a related role.

Skills and Knowledge

  • Strong understanding of software testing methodologies and quality assurance practices.
  • Experience with requirements management, traceability, and validation processes.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Proven stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • Confident presentation and facilitation skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with customers, partners, and cross-functional teams.
  • Customer-first mindset focused on successful business outcomes.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with at least one programming language (e.g., Java, C++, JavaScript).
  • Experience with at least one relational database technology (e.g., Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL).
  • Previous software consulting experience as a solution, technical, or application architect.

Job Description

For over 130 years, we have pioneered groundbreaking science.  Today, we are driven by continuous innovation to develop breakthrough medicines, vaccines and technology.  Rooted in direct experience on the farm and in the clinic, we work hand in hand with our customers every step of the way.

Our singular focus is to empower those who care for animals, helping them manage their vital responsibility with confidence.  Because when it comes to animal health, no one sees it like we do.


Our company is a global healthcare leader with a diversified portfolio of prescription medicines, vaccines, and animal health products. Our ability to excel depends on the integrity, knowledge, imagination, skill, diversity, and teamwork of our people. We strive to create an environment of mutual respect, encouragement, and collaboration. As part of our global team, colleagues in this role work cross-functionally with talented and dedicated partners while developing and expanding their skills and careers.

This role ensures timely, compliant handling of technical service inquiries, product complaints, and adverse events for the companion animal portfolio. Responsibilities include triaging incoming inquiries, managing technician level complaint processing end-to-end, supporting pharmacovigilance veterinarians, and serving as a liaison for product quality investigations and customer follow-up. The role supports accurate case documentation, quality assurance coordination, and clear communication with veterinarians, pet owners, sales representatives, and distributors.

Technical Support, Triage, and Complaint Handling (some combination of the below)


  • Serve as a first point of contact via phone, email, fax, written correspondence, and web inquiries (Technical Services 800-line).
  • Triage technical service inquiries, determining when to escalate to veterinarians and handling those that do not require veterinarian attention.
  • Address questions related to product usage and competitor product comparisons.
  • Processing and documenting complaints (may include but not limited to, call handling, data entry and/or releasing).
  • Identify trends and initiate product testing procedures; track testing through Global Quality and follow up with customers.
  • Retrieve, process, and follow up on after-hours product complaints.
  • Support PV veterinarians with:
    • Customer correspondence and follow-up.
    • Uploading correspondence/medical records into the complaint database.
    • Reviewing medical records for accuracy and forwarding to PV veterinarians.
    • Reviewing compensation requests and processing reimbursements.
    • Keeping the complaint database updated in real time.

Quality Assurance for Product Complaints:


  • Serve as primary contact for product quality issues, testing procedures, and warranty questions.
  • Initiate product sample returns from the field; ensure timely receipt, coordinate with Global Quality, and manage destruction when appropriate.
  • Upload QA testing results into the complaint database and close the loop with complainants

.

Cross-Functional and Commercial Support:


  • Share relevant information and trends in the veterinary marketplace with internal stakeholders.
  • Support special projects (e.g., diagnostic testing programs).
  • Assist with sales training and provide administrative/training support at meetings or national sales meetings.
  • Provide pharmacovigilance data and reports upon request.
  • Support the Equine PV team as needed by triaging incoming calls; addressing customer concerns and questions; handling product quality complaints (PQCs), product replacements, and reimbursement requests; and performing case entry when required.

  • BA/BS with at least 1 year of experience in the veterinary field; or
  • Associate’s degree (biological sciences preferred) with 3 years of veterinary-related experience; or
  • RVT/CVT/LVT with 2 years of related experience; or
  • 5 years of pharmacovigilance and/or animal science and/or companion animal customer care experience.

Core Requirements:


  • Minimum 1 year of pharmacovigilance experience and/or experience in animal science/companion animal customer care.
  • Strong computer skills: Word, Excel, Outlook; comfort with databases and data entry accuracy.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills; able to interact effectively with internal stakeholders and external customers.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications:


  • Experience with product knowledge management, database fundamentals, and internal/external compliance regulations.
  • Knowledge of parasiticide products in the animal health industry.
  • Prior call center or customer service experience.

  • Customer focus: Empathetic, responsive, and clear in communications with veterinarians, pet owners, and partners.

Especialista em Capital e Liquidez terá papel-chave na gestão de riscos e do capital regulatório da RecargaPay e na correta parametrização das contas COSIF nos sistemas de risco, garantindo aderência plena às normas prudenciais vigentes. Atuará como responsável técnico pelos reportes regulatórios ao Bacen — com ênfase em DLO, DDR, DLI, DRM, DRL, assegurando a consistência entre dados contábeis, financeiros, gerenciais e regulatórios.


RESPONSABILIDADES

  • Responder tecnicamente pelos reportes regulatórios ao Bacen — elaborar, revisar e transmitir DLO, DDR, DLI, DRM, DRL, assegurando prazos, qualidade e consistência entre dados contábeis, financeiros, gerenciais e regulatórios.
  • Conduzir a parametrização e a manutenção das contas COSIF nos sistemas de risco, garantindo classificação correta das exposições (crédito, mercado e operacional), atribuição adequada dos Fatores de Ponderação de Risco (FPRs) e aderência às Resoluções CMN nº 4.955 e 4.966 e normativos correlatos.
  • Calcular e monitorar os requerimentos de capital — risco de crédito (RWACPAD), mercado (RWAMPAD) e operacional (RWAOPAD) — e acompanhar Índices de Basileia, capital mínimo, buffers e razão de alavancagem, antecipando pressões de capital e de liquidez.
  • Acompanhar mudanças regulatórias do CMN, BCB, CVM e Receita Federal, avaliando impactos em capital, liquidez e processos e conduzindo a implementação das adequações
  • Atuar como referência técnica da área: orientar analistas, disseminar boas práticas de cálculo e reporte e elevar a automação e o controle dos processos regulatórios.

Requirements

  • Graduação em Economia, Administração, Engenharia, Estatística, Matemática, Finanças ou áreas correlatas.
  • Experiência sólida (referência: 7+ anos) em risco de capital, regulatório e/ou liquidez em instituição financeira, instituição de pagamento ou fintech regulada.
  • Domínio da regulamentação prudencial do Bacen/CMN: cálculo de RWA (crédito, mercado e operacional), Índice de Basileia, buffers e razão de alavancagem.
  • Experiência em planos de capital, testes de estresse e apoio a inspeções do Bacen e auditorias. Habilidade para construir apresentações executivas e indicadores de risco para comitês e alta liderança.
  • Diferencial: pós-graduação em Riscos, Regulação Bancária ou Finanças.
  • Diferencial: Conhecimento no sistema de Riscos Matera Diferencial: Python e SQL para automação de cálculos e relatórios regulatórios.

COMPETÊNCIAS

  • Rigor técnico e atenção a detalhes: garante consistência entre contabilidade, risco e regulatório e identifica inconsistências antes que cheguem ao regulador.
  • Pensamento analítico e visão sistêmica: conecta capital, liquidez, estratégia de negócio e regulação para apoiar decisões.
  • Comunicação executiva: sintetiza temas complexos para Comitê de Risco e liderança de forma clara e objetiva.

jobs.description:
Department:

104275 FILSPARI Global Strategy

Location:

San Diego, USA- Remote

Be a part of a global team that is inspired to make a difference in the lives of people living with rare disease.

At Travere Therapeutics, we recognize that our exceptional employees are vital to our success. We are a dedicated team focused on meeting the unique needs of rare patients. Our work is rewarding – both professionally and personally – because we are making a difference. We are passionate about what we do.

We are seeking talented individuals who will thrive in our collaborative, diverse, fast-paced environment and share in our mission – to identify, develop and deliver life-changing therapies to people living with rare disease. We stick by our values centered on patients, courage, community, and collaboration to pursue our vision of becoming a leading biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the delivery of innovation and hope to patients in the global rare disease community.

At Travere Therapeutics, we are in rare for life. We continue to courageously forge new paths as we move toward a common goal of elevating science and service for rare patients.

Position Summary


The Executive Director, Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) will provide strategic leadership for the development and execution of health economics, outcomes research, real-world evidence, patient-reported outcomes and evidence synthesis strategies across Travere Therapeutics’ nephrology portfolio, including FILSPARI® (sparsentan), civorebrutinib, and future pipeline assets.

This individual will be responsible for developing an integrated evidence strategy that demonstrates the clinical, humanistic, and economic value of Travere’s therapies throughout the product lifecycle. The Executive Director will partner closely with Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, Market Access, Commercial, Regulatory Affairs, Biostatistics, and other cross-functional partners to identify evidence needs and ensure generation of high-quality data that supports scientific exchange, patient access, clinical development, and future value demonstration.

The Executive Director will serve as the senior HEOR expert for the Nephrology Franchise and will help shape the long-range evidence strategy for marketed and development-stage assets.

Responsibilities:


  • Develop and lead the HEOR and value evidence strategy across Travere’s nephrology portfolio, including FILSPARI, civorebrutinib, and future pipeline assets.
  • Develop integrated evidence-generation plans that address clinical, economic, humanistic, and healthcare decision-maker evidence needs across the product lifecycle.
  • Partner closely with Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Market Access, Regulatory, and Biostatistics to identify evidence gaps and ensure HEOR priorities are incorporated into broader asset and franchise strategies.
  • Lead health economic research, including cost-effectiveness, budget impact, cost-of-illness, healthcare resource utilization, and other analyses that support understanding of the value of Travere therapies.
  • Develop and execute real-world evidence studies leveraging existing data sources, including administrative claims, electronic medical records, registries, and other healthcare databases, to characterize disease burden, treatment patterns, patient journeys, healthcare resource utilization, and clinical outcomes.
  • Lead the patient-reported outcomes strategy, including selection, development, validation, and incorporation of fit-for-purpose PRO measures into clinical development and evidence-generation programs where appropriate.
  • Partner with Clinical Development to incorporate HEOR and outcomes research considerations early in development, including study design, endpoint strategy, evidence gaps, and future access needs.
  • Identify opportunities to complement clinical trial evidence with epidemiology, real-world data, health economics, and patient-centered outcomes research.
  • Develop evidence that supports payer and health technology assessment needs and contributes to value dossiers, reimbursement submissions, and other access-related evidence requirements.
  • Anticipate future evidence needs and establish research plans that support new indications, lifecycle opportunities, and future nephrology assets.
  • Partner with external research collaborations, data partners, research organizations, and other external experts.
  • Develop and oversee HEOR publication plans and ensure timely dissemination of research through peer-reviewed publications, scientific congresses, and other appropriate scientific channels.
  • Represent Travere externally with HEOR researchers, nephrology experts, academic collaborators, and other scientific stakeholders.
  • Serve as an internal subject matter expert on health economics, outcomes research, real-world evidence, and patient-centered outcomes, providing strategic guidance to senior leadership and cross-functional teams.
  • Manage external vendors, research partners, budgets, timelines, and project execution to ensure high-quality and timely delivery of HEOR initiatives.
  • Ensure all activities are conducted in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, industry standards, company policies, and Travere compliance requirements.

Education/Experience Requirements:


  • Advanced degree in health economics, outcomes research, epidemiology, public health, health services research, pharmacy, medicine, biostatistics, or a related discipline required; PhD, PharmD, MD, ScD, DrPH, or equivalent advanced degree strongly preferred.
  • 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in HEOR, real-world evidence, outcomes research, market access evidence, or related disciplines within the biopharmaceutical industry, consulting, academia, or a combination thereof.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and executing HEOR and evidence-generation strategies for marketed and/or development-stage assets.
  • Strong experience using real-world healthcare data, including claims, EMR/EHR, registries, and other large healthcare databases.
  • Experience with health economic modeling, burden-of-illness research, healthcare resource utilization, epidemiology, and observational research.
  • Experience with patient-reported outcomes and clinical outcomes assessments, including instrument selection, development, validation, and implementation.
  • Experience developing evidence to support payer, reimbursement, and health technology assessment needs.
  • Experience in nephrology, rare disease, specialty therapeutics, or progressive chronic diseases strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated record of scientific publications and presentations in HEOR, outcomes research, epidemiology, real-world evidence, or related fields.

Additional Skills/Experience/Requirements:


  • Strong understanding of payer and healthcare decision-maker evidence needs.
  • Ability to translate clinical and business questions into rigorous, decision-relevant evidence-generation programs.
  • Strong strategic thinking with the ability to anticipate evidence needs and connect research priorities to clinical development and product strategy.
  • Ability to work effectively across functions and influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners without direct authority.
  • Strong scientific judgment, analytical skills, and commitment to research quality and scientific integrity.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex evidence clearly to scientific and non-scientific audiences.
  • Strong leadership, organizational, budget management, and vendor management capabilities.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and evolving organization.

Total Rewards Offerings:
Travere provides comprehensive total rewards offerings that demonstrate our commitment as a diverse, equitable, people-centric, and pay-for-performance organization.

Benefits: Our benefits include premium health, financial, work-life and well-being offerings for eligible employees and dependents, wellness and employee support programs, life insurance, disability, retirement plans with employer match and generous paid time off.

Compensation: Our competitive compensation package includes a combination of both cash compensation (base pay and short-term incentive) and long-term incentive compensation (company stock), designed to recognize, retain, and reward employees.

Target Base Pay Range:

$246,000.00 - $332,000.00

*This information is current as of the date of this posting and may be modified in the future. Actual pay offered to a candidate will depend on a variety of factors including the candidate’s experience, education, skills, and location.

Job Description

Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University’s Worldwide campus is currently hiring adjunct faculty to teach SYSE 505 – System Safety and Certification

Course Description

Safety engineering considerations when designing, testing, and certifying airborne safety-critical systems in regulated industries. Fundamentals of system safety engineering and the regulatory framework for initial airworthiness certification; system hazard and risk analysis and safety assessment; safety requirements validation and verification; fault models and failure analysis techniques such as fault trees, FEMA, event tree analysis, common cause/mode analysis, dependence diagrams, and Markov analysis. Industry standards for aircraft development (SAE ARP4754B and ARP4761A) and for airborne hardware and software development (RTCA DO-178C and DO-254).


Please note that ERAU policy requires that all adjuncts be physically located within the United States while working for the University, including during training. Presently, we are able to support work for new adjuncts from all U.S. states except California. ERAU does not support work from international locations with some limited exceptions for individuals who are residing and working from U.S. military bases.

If selected for this role, the candidate will be required to provide proof of stated qualifications. This includes, but is not limited to, official transcripts, copies of professional licenses/certifications, documentation of military experience, and/or verified professional industry related experience.

Experience at a Military and Civilian organization designing, developing, testing, operating, or analyzing application of unmanned systems (robotics), including the components, tools, methods, and processes associated with system control and interaction and Active membership in professional organizations in engineering, i.e., National Academy of Engineering, National Society of Professional Engineers, Society of Flight Test Engineers, Society of Experimental Test Pilots, Aircraft Designer, Human Factors and Ergonomics Society, or other field related to the research, design, development, test, evaluation, operation, or application of unmanned systems

jobs.description:
We are seeking a Senior QA Automation Engineer to join our Quality Engineering team and help ensure the reliability, security, and overall quality of our cybersecurity products. You will play a key role in defining, leading, and scaling quality assurance across our platform, with a strong emphasis on test automation.

This is a hands-on senior individual contributor role. You will lead our web application test automation efforts, designing and evolving automated testing solutions with Playwright and JavaScript, and integrating automated testing throughout the software development lifecycle. You will also mentor junior QA and automation engineers and influence engineering practices across teams.

Requirements

QA Strategy & Leadership

  • Lead the design and execution of QA strategies, frameworks, and automated test plans across multiple products
  • Identify high-value opportunities for automation and help define the team's automation strategy and roadmap
  • Participate in requirements and design reviews to identify quality risks and testability concerns early in the development lifecycle
  • Define meaningful quality metrics and provide visibility into automation coverage, reliability, and product quality
  • Continuously evaluate testing tools, techniques, and approaches, and drive improvement of QA processes aligned with engineering goals

Test Automation & Infrastructure

  • Lead the design, development, and ongoing improvement of our automated testing framework using Playwright and JavaScript
  • Develop reliable, maintainable, and reusable automated tests for browser-based cybersecurity applications, with coverage across backend, frontend, and infrastructure components
  • Establish and promote automation architecture, coding standards, design patterns, and testing best practices
  • Own and enhance CI/CD-integrated testing infrastructure, including quality gates and feedback mechanisms, for consistent validation across environments
  • Review existing automation and improve its reliability, maintainability, execution speed, and coverage
  • Diagnose and resolve flaky tests, automation failures, and complex application or environment issues
  • Analyze test results to distinguish product defects from automation, environment, and test-data issues
  • Contribute to our growing suite of automated security checks (e.g., SAST/DAST and dependency scanning) in CI/CD pipelines

Team Enablement & Collaboration

  • Mentor junior QA and automation engineers, conduct code reviews, and provide technical guidance
  • Partner with software engineers, product managers, security teams, and QA engineers to develop effective test strategies for new features and releases
  • Advocate for quality engineering practices and help shift testing earlier in the development lifecycle
  • Promote a culture of quality and accountability

What You Bring

Required:

  • 5+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance, Quality Engineering, Software Development Engineering in Test (SDET), or a similar role
  • Strong experience designing and developing automated tests for modern web applications
  • Hands-on experience with Playwright, preferably using JavaScript or TypeScript, with emphasis on designing scalable automation frameworks rather than solely creating individual test cases (experience with Cypress, Selenium, Jest, or similar is a plus)
  • Strong understanding of software testing methodologies, including functional, integration, regression, end-to-end, and negative testing
  • Strong experience integrating automated tests with CI/CD pipelines (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI) and source-control workflows
  • Experience testing complex applications involving role-based access controls, permissions, multi-tenant environments, or security policies
  • Experience mentoring junior engineers and providing constructive technical feedback through code reviews
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work cross-functionally

Preferred:

  • Familiarity with Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, Azure, or similar technologies
  • Experience in security-critical, high-availability, or infrastructure-heavy systems
  • Familiarity with API security, authentication flows, and data protection practices
  • Experience leading QA initiatives in Agile environments
  • Familiarity with security testing tools (e.g., OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite, SAST/DAST)

What Success Looks Like:

Success means moving beyond simply increasing the number of automated tests. You will build an automation ecosystem that engineers trust: tests that are reliable, maintainable, appropriately scoped, and give rapid feedback when something goes wrong. You will become a technical leader within the QA organization, helping decide what to automate, how to automate it, and how automation fits into the broader development process, while growing the engineers around you.

You as a Person

  • Knowledge: Deep expertise in QA automation and CI/CD workflows
  • Skill: Builds scalable testing systems and mentors others in quality practices
  • Ability: Influences teams and drives improvements in product quality

You in the Role

  • Autonomy: Owns and evolves QA and test automation across multiple products
  • Complexity: Solves complex quality challenges across the full stack
  • Impact: Ensures consistent, high-quality product releases

Extra Credit

  • QA certifications such as ISTQB, or security certifications such as OSCP, CEH, or CSSLP
  • Experience with SaaS platforms or networking-intensive solutions
  • Hands-on experience with cloud security and compliance (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001)

Benefits

Why Dispel/Benefits

At Dispel you’ll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

  • Base salary: $90,000 – $120,000
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Generous paid time off and holidays
  • Performance bonus and equity eligible
  • Remote work
  • Medical, vision, dental insurance

Position Title: Intern

Location: Remote, but must be a college student/recent graduate residing in the U.S.

About the Active Minds Internship Program

Active Minds is the nation’s leading nonprofit organization changing the culture around mental health. Through our presence at more than 800 high school and college campuses, in corporate settings, and with a wide-reaching public audience, Active Minds is creating communities of support and saving lives. Founded in 2003 by Alison Malmon after the tragic suicide of her brother Brian, Active Minds is dedicated to supporting a new generation in ending the silence, helping to make mental health as highly valued as physical health. Through our many programs – including the emotionally gripping Send Silence Packing® traveling exhibit and our compelling Active Minds Speakers – we are changing culture and behaviors related to mental health across the country.

Our internships are geared towards current college students and recent college graduates. As a small nonprofit, Active Minds relies on the help of our interns tremendously. They work directly on important initiatives and projects and assist staff on a variety of administrative tasks. Interns have the opportunity to do substantive work, gain experience in the nonprofit sector, and help change the culture around mental health.

All Spring 2027 internships will be remote, with an anticipated start date of February 1st, 2027, and an anticipated end date of April 23rd, 2027. We expect interns to work a minimum of 20 hours a week, set a consistent work schedule between 9:00am and 5:00pm EST Monday through Friday, and commit to staying on board for the entire semester (February-April).

Active Minds pays interns $18 per hour.

As part of the Marketing and Communications team, the Digital Media intern will support the Social Media and Digital Marketing team in developing content across platforms, with a particular focus on short and long-form video content capturing, editing, and producing. They will work with the rest of the team to create engaging, shareable content to help increase awareness of Active Minds programming.

This role will provide interns with the opportunity to be creative, learn how nonprofits manage and develop their social media, collaborate with various Active Minds staffers to learn more about mental health advocacy, and interact with thousands of enthusiastic audience members on a daily basis.

  • Support community engagement efforts by helping manage comments, messages, and audience interactions.

  • Hands-on experience creating content for a nationally recognized nonprofit organization.
  • Exposure to digital marketing, social media strategy, brand storytelling, and audience engagement.

  • Experience developing content that advances mental health awareness and social impact initiatives.

The application cycle for the Spring 2027 Internship Program will be open from Wednesday, October 21st, 2026 through Wednesday, November 4th, 2026. When completing the application, please thoughtfully answer each application question in complete, authentic sentences, as we thoroughly review every application.

Applicants selected for an interview will be contacted by late November/early December 2026 regarding scheduling next steps. We are looking for a Lead Data Scientist – Virtual Models to take ownership of this programme from the start.

This is a hands-on role for an experienced data scientist who wants to build something new. You will assess existing datasets across QIMA’s Business Units, identify the most promising opportunities, develop proof-of-concept models and prepare them for use by internal teams and, ultimately, by clients.

Initial applications may include models related to:

  • skin;
  • hair follicles;
  • longevity;
  • prostate cancer;
  • immunology.

You will work closely with Managing Directors, laboratory scientists and QIMA’s IT and AI experts. Scientific validation will be carried out in collaboration with independent laboratory teams.

Key responsibilities

  • Review and assess proposals from QIMA’s Business Units.
  • Examine the underlying data in detail, including its quality, structure, consistency, depth and breadth.
  • Recommend one or two models with the strongest potential for development, subject to approval by the CEO of QIMA Life Sciences.
  • Build and manage the required data pipelines.
  • Clean, structure, integrate and analyse complex biological datasets.
  • Develop machine learning models and proof of concepts.
  • Identify data gaps and recommend additional experiments where needed. Work with laboratory scientists to help define these experiments, including the required data, measurements and quality criteria.
  • Establish clear validation criteria and prepare models for independent scientific validation.
  • Improve the models through repeated testing and iteration.
  • Ensure that code, data and models are reproducible, traceable and properly documented.
  • Present results clearly to scientific, technical, commercial and non-specialist audiences.
  • Support the preparation of a model for future commercialisation, either as a SaaS product or as a service supporting, replacing or complementing wet-lab assays.
  • Contribute to the documentation and protection of intellectual property related to the models, pipelines and methods.

This role will initially be an individual contributor position. As the programme grows, you may help build and lead a team of additional data scientists.

First objectives

Within the first six months, you will be expected to:

  • assess the main model proposals and their underlying datasets;
  • recommend the one or two strongest projects;
  • establish a proof of concept for one or two models.

Within 12 to 15 months, the objective will be to prepare at least one model for potential commercialisation. This should include sufficient scientific validation, an interface usable internally, and complete documentation or detailed operator training.

You have:

  • a PhD in data science, biostatistics, bioinformatics, machine learning or a related field;
  • 8–10 years of experience in data science, biostatistics and machine learning;
  • a proven track record of delivering complex machine learning projects using complex biological datasets;
  • strong experience building data pipelines, assessing data quality, identifying limitations and defining what additional data is needed;
  • experience working with scientists and translating scientific questions into data and modelling approaches;
  • excellent communication skills and the ability to explain complex concepts clearly to non-specialists;
  • ideally, experience presenting work to clients, partners or other external stakeholders;
  • a practical, entrepreneurial and hands-on approach;
  • the ability to work independently and take ownership of an ambiguous, new project.

Experience in a specific therapeutic area is not essential. The most important requirements are strong technical expertise, experience with biological data and the ability to turn complex datasets into useful, validated models.

Strong Python or R skills, including production-quality, version-controlled code. Experience with cloud data platforms (we use Snowflake) and MLOps practices.

Why join QIMA?

This is an opportunity to build a new capability from the ground up and shape how QIMA uses its biological data. You will have direct access to senior leadership, laboratory experts and technical teams, with the autonomy to define the approach and deliver tangible results.

The role will be based in Europe and will require travel, depending on project needs, to QIMA laboratories in France, Northern Ireland and Germany.

Does this describe you? Then we want to hear from you as soon as possible! Apply now with your CV in Englishand we can write the next chapter of the QIMA story together!

At QIMA, we are on a mission to help our clients make products consumers can trust. We have developed compliance solutions for testing, inspection and certification (TIC) that enable supply chain agility, sustainability and product innovation. Our services are used by 30,000 businesses globally in the consumer products, agri-food and life sciences industries. Backed by 6,000+ dedicated Qimates worldwide, we bring local expertise and tailored support to every client. Our passion for service has made QIMA an industry leader for customer satisfaction, as highlighted by our exceptional Net Promoter Score (NPS).

Through our Life Sciences activities, we develop and deliver scientific testing and research services for our clients.

We are now launching a new programme to develop virtual pharmacology models. These models will use the data generated through years of laboratory work to help assess the efficacy of molecules and support future screening activities.

The role serves as a senior technical resource for complex initiatives involving interoperability, integration architecture, and emerging technologies while supporting the organization's long-term technology strategy.

  • Mentors technical team members and promotes best practices related to enterprise integration and solution architecture.
  • Adheres to University and unit-level policies and procedures and safeguards University assets.

Epic Technical Architecture

  • Serve as the technical lead for Epic interoperability and integration solutions involving Epic and third-party applications.

  • Design enterprise interoperability solutions connecting Epic with clinical, operational, research, and digital health platforms.

  • Lead the architecture, implementation, administration, and support of interoperability solutions utilizing healthcare integration platforms such as InterSystems IRIS for Health, Rhapsody, Corepoint, and other enterprise integration technologies.
  • Translate business and clinical requirements into secure, scalable, and supportable architectures.
  • Establish reusable integration patterns, technical standards, and architecture guidelines.
  • Ensure solutions align with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity, data governance, and operational requirements.

Vendor and Startup Engagement

  • Lead technical discussions, architecture reviews, and solution assessments with healthcare vendors, startups, and implementation partners.
  • Evaluate vendor products for interoperability, scalability, security, operational supportability, and alignment with organizational standards.
  • Provide technical due diligence, architecture guidance, and build-versus-buy recommendations.
  • Review vendor APIs, implementation guides, security models, and integration designs.
  • Facilitate architecture workshops and drive practical solutions for complex business and technical challenges.

Software Engineering and Technical Prototyping

  • Develop or guide prototypes, proofs of concept, web services, APIs, and custom integration components.

  • Mentor engineers and participate in the design and development of complex interoperability solutions.

  • Partner with cybersecurity and infrastructure teams to ensure HIPAA-compliant and secure interoperability solutions.

AI-Enabled and Agentic Solutions

jobs.title: Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst (Journeyman)
jobs.excerpt: OverviewDecisionPoint seeks a Journeyman Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst to support vulnerability tracking, remediation coordination, and cybersecurity compliance reporting for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.
jobs.description:
Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Journeyman Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst to support vulnerability tracking, remediation coordination, and cybersecurity compliance reporting for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program.

The Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst will review ACAS findings provided by Government personnel, reconcile affected systems and devices with inventory records, and coordinate corrective actions with responsible administrators. The analyst will track remediation tickets, dependencies, deadlines, POA&M updates, and supporting evidence through resolution.

This role will also coordinate Government rescans, review the resulting data to verify remediation, and maintain accurate vulnerability status information for operational reporting, compliance reviews, and cybersecurity inspections.

This position is remote, with a preference for candidates located in the Chicago area.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The Vulnerability Management / ACAS Analyst will:

  • Review ACAS vulnerability findings provided by Government personnel.
  • Analyze findings to identify affected assets, systems, applications, devices, and responsible support teams.
  • Reconcile affected assets against configuration-management, inventory, and asset-management records.
  • Research discrepancies between ACAS results and authoritative asset inventories.
  • Support prioritization of vulnerabilities based on severity, asset criticality, mission impact, remediation deadlines, and Government direction.
  • Coordinate corrective actions with system administrators, infrastructure teams, application teams, engineers, and other remediation owners.
  • Create, update, and monitor vulnerability-remediation tickets in the designated workflow system.
  • Track assigned owners, corrective actions, technical dependencies, target completion dates, and current remediation status.
  • Follow up with responsible personnel to obtain status updates and identify issues that could delay remediation.
  • Collect technical documentation, screenshots, configuration results, ticket records, and other evidence supporting remediation completion.
  • Review supporting evidence for completeness before requesting validation or rescanning.
  • Coordinate Government rescan requests for vulnerabilities reported as remediated.
  • Review Government-provided rescan results to verify that corrective actions successfully resolved identified vulnerabilities.
  • Document validated closures and retain supporting evidence in the designated Government repository.
  • Track compliance with applicable Information Assurance Vulnerability Alerts and Information Assurance Vulnerability Management requirements.
  • Create and update POA&M entries for vulnerabilities requiring formal corrective-action tracking.
  • Maintain accurate vulnerability status information for recurring reports, dashboards, compliance reviews, and cybersecurity inspections.
  • Identify overdue, high-risk, recurring, or unresolved findings and escalate them to the Senior Vulnerability Management / ACAS Response Analyst or cybersecurity leadership.
  • Track remediation dependencies involving patch availability, configuration changes, application testing, maintenance windows, or operational constraints.
  • Assist with documenting false positives, mitigating controls, operational dependencies, and Government-approved risk decisions.
  • Support review of Endpoint Security Solutions reports and tracking of applicable endpoint-security findings.
  • Develop vulnerability aging reports, remediation status summaries, compliance metrics, and supporting briefing materials.
  • Help identify recurring vulnerabilities, process gaps, inaccurate asset records, and opportunities to improve remediation workflows.
  • Support maintenance of vulnerability-management procedures, standard operating procedures, tracking tools, and reporting templates.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 7 years of relevant cybersecurity, information assurance, vulnerability-management, or information-security experience.
  • Current CompTIA Security+ certification.

Preferred Qualifications

  • CompTIA Cybersecurity Analyst (CySA+) certification.
  • Experience reviewing ACAS or Tenable vulnerability-scan results in a Department of Defense environment.
  • Experience reconciling vulnerability findings against hardware, software, configuration-management, or asset-inventory records.
  • Experience coordinating vulnerability remediation with system administrators, infrastructure teams, and application support teams.
  • Knowledge of Information Assurance Vulnerability Alerts and Information Assurance Vulnerability Management requirements.
  • Experience creating and maintaining cybersecurity POA&Ms.
  • Experience using ServiceNow or another ticketing and workflow-management platform to track remediation activities.
  • Familiarity with Endpoint Security Solutions, STIG Viewer, SCAP tools, eMASS, or comparable DoD cybersecurity technologies.
  • Knowledge of the DoD Risk Management Framework, NIST SP 800-53 controls, DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides, and applicable DoD cybersecurity directives.
  • Experience collecting, reviewing, and maintaining technical evidence supporting vulnerability remediation and closure.
  • Experience coordinating rescans and reviewing results to verify successful remediation.
  • Experience preparing vulnerability reports, remediation metrics, aging summaries, dashboards, or inspection-support materials.
  • Familiarity with current DoD 8140 cybersecurity workforce qualification requirements.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, documentation, communication, and follow-through skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple findings, owners, dependencies, and deadlines in a structured compliance environment.

Our Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

  • EEO and Affirmative Action Policy: DecisionPoint Corporation is an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. It is the policy of DecisionPoint Corporation to provide equal employment opportunity in accordance with all applicable Equal Employment Opportunity/Affirmative Action laws, directives and regulations to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, disability status, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other protected status under Federal, State or Local laws.
  • Pay Transparency Policy: In accordance with Presidential Executive Order 13665, DecisionPoint Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor's legal duty to furnish information.
  • Authorization to Share Resume and Personal Information: By expressing your interest and submitting your resume for this position, you authorize DecisionPoint Corporation to share your resume, as well as personal information included on the resume, with its subsidiaries, affiliates and teaming partners for the purpose of considering you for this position and other available positions requiring comparable skills, education and experience.
