jobs.title: Software Engineer II, Engineering
jobs.excerpt: As a Software Engineer II on an engineering squad at Ellevation, you'll build and operate features that directly shape how educators manage English Learner programs across thousands of school districts.
jobs.description:
As a Software Engineer II on an engineering squad at Ellevation, you'll build and operate features that directly shape how educators manage English Learner programs across thousands of school districts. You'll work across a full-stack environment — React on the frontend, C#/.NET Core or Python on the backend — and you'll own your work end-to-end: design, build, ship, and keep it running.

At this level, you're not just executing tickets. You're expected to bring a proposed path when you surface a problem, close open questions by building rather than debating, and leave the systems you touch in better shape than you found them. You'll be a real contributor to how the squad works — in design discussions, in code review, and in the day-to-day quality bar the team holds together.

About You:

    You might be a great fit if you:

  • You bring a proposed path along with the problem — you've found that framing a solution, even a rough one, moves things forward faster than waiting for the perfect answer.

  • When something is blocking the team, your instinct is to build the smallest thing that answers the question rather than debate it — a spike, a script, a quick prototype.

  • You share real opinions in design discussions — on tradeoffs, complexity, and risk — because you believe teams make better decisions when people actually weigh in.

  • You take code review seriously in both directions: you ask until you understand before approving, and you welcome the same rigor on your own work.

  • You stay engaged past the merge — on cleanup, follow-up bugs, and alerts that trace back to what you shipped — because you care about the full lifecycle, not just the delivery moment.

  • You use AI tools to move faster, and you read and own everything that goes out under your name.

What You’ll Do:

  • Build and ship product features across React, .NET Core/Python, and supporting infrastructure — from design through operation.

  • Bring concrete tradeoffs to design discussions — performance, complexity, blast radius, time-to-ship — so the squad is making decisions based on real costs.

  • Close open questions by spiking, scripting, or prototyping, keeping the team moving rather than waiting on answers that could be found by building.

  • Operate what you build: instrument it, respond to alerts, and close the loop on issues that surface after release.

  • Review code thoughtfully — ask questions, push for improvements when they matter, and welcome the same on your own PRs.

  • Pick up improvements you notice along the way — tech debt, alerting gaps, missing tests — without waiting to be asked.

What You’ll Bring:

  • 2–4 years shipping production software, with enough end-to-end ownership to know what "done" actually means.

  • Fluency in at least one frontend JS framework (React/Vue/Angular), and a strongly typed language (C#/.NET/Python/Go) — and comfort learning across the stack where the work takes you.

  • Experience naming tradeoffs concretely rather than just expressing preferences — you've been in design discussions where your perspective shaped the outcome.

  • Engineering habits — testing, observability, careful review — that reflect care for the long term, not just the current ticket.

  • Some experience operating what you've built: you've debugged production, you know what good instrumentation looks like.

  • Some experience with how code gets deployed and runs in production — you understand the path from commit to live, and you know what good instrumentation looks like.

Why Ellevation?

    At Ellevation, we believe in the power of education and the educators who make it possible. Joining our team means:

  • Working on meaningful challenges that directly impact English Learners.

  • Helping define and build the future of internal platforms and developer experience at a mission-driven company.

  • Collaborating in a supportive, cross-functional environment.

  • Growing personally and professionally as part of a high-performing team.

  • Leveraging AI responsibly to accelerate how we build, test, and operate systems.

Our Tech Stack

    Frontend: React (with ongoing migration from legacy systems)
    Backend: C#/.NET Core (and some .NET Framework legacy) or Python
    Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, CI/CD with Jenkins, Docker
    Developer Experience: Internal tooling, repo templates, CI/CD workflows, container-based dev

    We don’t expect you to know everything on day one — what matters most is your ability to learn, collaborate, and lead through change.

Are you passionate about growth and eager to learn? Do you possess a drive to excel and make a difference? Ellevation values diversity, creativity, and a hunger for new perspectives. While our job postings outline preferred qualifications, we believe that talent comes in various forms. If you're motivated, adaptable, and ready to contribute, we encourage you to apply. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences, recognizing that unique skills and fresh outlooks are invaluable assets to our team. Don't let a checklist of requirements deter you – take the leap, and let's explore the possibilities together!

About Us:

At Ellevation, we develop world-class software to help educators serve the fastest growing population of K-12 students: English Learners (ELs). Ellevation helps school districts transform their Multilingual Learner programs and ensure all students can achieve their highest aspirations. Our product suite includes a best-in-class data and instructional planning platform, resources to build teacher capacity, and student-facing programs to teach academic language.
We are a fast-growing, mission-driven technology company partnering with over 2,000 school districts and more than 2 million current and former English Learners. Over the next five years, we plan to double the number of ELs we serve and drive measurable outcomes for students. Ellevation merged with Curriculum Associates in 2021 to accelerate impact for Multilingual Learners. Our company continues to operate independently and is well-capitalized to support our ambitious social and financial objectives.

Why Ellevation?

In addition to our great benefits and competitive salaries, here are some things that make us unique:
+ Mission-driven organization where team members are empowered to make a significant impact
+ Opportunities to join Employee Resource Groups and support building a culture of belonging
+ Professional development and growth opportunities
+ Company and team offsites in various cities across the United States
+ Collaborative workspace in the heart of Boston - a stone's throw from many central T stops (Downtown Crossing, Government Center, and Aquarium). Free snacks, beverages, and local organic fruit provided
+ Remote and in-person engagement opportunities, including happy hours, themed events, and competitions
+ Remote and in-person wellness programming to support team’s mental and physical wellbeing
Here at Ellevation, we champion diversity, inclusion, equity, and belonging. We strive to build a team that reflects the diverse communities we serve. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values a range of ideas and opinions.
We believe in building a culture where productivity can flourish, one that is empathetic, respectful, and inclusive. We are proud to have been recognized in prior years as “Best Tech Workplace for Diversity” by the Timmy Awards for investing in training around inclusive behaviors, microaggressions, unconscious bias, and fostering a culture of continuous learning and feedback across the company. We are encouraged by our progress, but there’s more work to be done.

What We Can Achieve Together:


The Associate Director of Development I (ADoD I) works closely with the development team to implement and coordinate effective multi-year strategies and plans for gift prospects, including corporate, foundation, and/or individual donors.


The Associate Director of Development I is responsible for building a portfolio of qualified donors and developing relationships. They understand and apply the principles of developing donor strategies. They will be responsible for direct asks to both global and local priorities to meet funding needs. They listen for opportunities for gifts of assets or other non-cash gifts, such as planned gifts and trade lands. The ADoD I provides opportunities for donors to receive recognition and increase future giving. They involve appropriate partners in the field and staff at the Worldwide Office, keeping them apprised of interactions, issues or concerns, and direct questions as appropriate. They can feature the programs of the Conservancy in broad terms. They may be responsible for volunteer engagement within formal and/or informal networks. The ADoD I will be required to use the Conservancy’s donor database and may participate in the development of proposals. They will travel frequently and on short notice, work long and flexible hours as needed. The work environment may involve infrequent exposure to disagreeable elements and minor physical exertion and/or strain.


We’re Looking for You:

Have you ever asked yourself, “How can I make a difference?”, but you don’t know where to go or have the time to do it? Welcome to The Nature Conservancy.


You have found the solution and now you can pointedly make a difference every day! By joining our Oceania team, you will become part of a group that is a force for nature and people. Our team consists of a dedicated group who are leading the conservation effort on multiple fronts and who expertly bring strategy and action together. We’re looking for an individual with fundraising or business development experience who wants to make a difference. The Conservancy is a global conservation leader and one of the top fundraising charities in the United States.


What You’ll Bring:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 5 years related experience or an equivalent combination.
  • Experience building and maintaining long-term relationships with fundraising constituents.
  • Experience in asking for and closing gifts of $25,000 or more.
  • Experience in managing and tracking multiple prospects and donors.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams.
  • Experience, coursework, or other training in fundraising principles and practices.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience appreciated.
  • Ability to determine an individual’s interests, capacity, and potential for helping the Conservancy meet its goals, and act appropriately to tie those interests with the Conservancy’s work.
  • Ability to educate and inform prospective and existing donors about appropriate giving vehicles.
  • Ability to implement and manage fundraising plans, including individualized cultivation, solicitation, and recognition plans.
  • Knowledge of current trends in the charitable giving in the areas of capital campaigns, major gifts or planned giving.
  • Demonstrated experience using listening, diplomacy, and tact to build strong relationships and motivate donors and volunteers.
  • Proven ability to negotiate high profile or sensitive agreements.
  • Working knowledge of the basics of charitable gift planning.

This position requires a valid driver's license and compliance with TNC’s Auto Safety Program. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Employment in this position will be contingent upon completion of a Vehicle Use Agreement, which may include a review of the prospective employee's motor vehicle record.

Who We Are:

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

Description:
Structural Integrity Associates, Inc. (SIA) is seeking an experienced Consultant specializing in turbomachinery structural design and analysis, with a strong background in gas or steam turbines. Previous experience within the power generation, aerospace, or energy industries, particularly with an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) or independent service provider, is preferred.

The successful candidate will provide advanced technical expertise in thermal and structural analysis to lead the support and execution of engineering projects involving rotating equipment, reverse engineering, fitness-for-service evaluations, and remaining life assessments. This position will lead the development of analytical digital twin models using computer-aided design (CAD) and finite element analysis (FEA) tools to evaluate equipment performance under transient and steady-state operating conditions. These analyses will support the assessment of potential failure mechanisms, remaining service life, and appropriate inspection intervals.

This position requires collaboration with clients, multidisciplinary engineering teams, and senior technical personnel to support equipment condition assessments, reverse engineering, and lifecycle evaluations of rotating and stationary components.

Primary Responsibilities:
  • Perform advanced finite element thermal and structural stress analyses of turbomachinery components using engineering software, including ANSYS and Abaqus, as required.
  • Develop detailed 2D and 3D models of turbomachinery components and assemblies, including gas and steam turbine rotors and blades, to support engineering analysis and reverse engineering activities.
  • Conduct applicable ASME Code evaluations and ensure engineering analyses comply with relevant industry standards and design criteria.
  • Develop, maintain, and utilize analytical digital twin models of gas and steam turbines to support equipment performance evaluations, predictive analytics, and lifecycle management.
  • Utilize thermodynamic and fluid dynamics software, including AxStream, Fluent, and STAR-CCM+, as required, to support performance and flow analyses.
  • Integrate thermal and fluid simulation results, including boundary conditions developed using AxStream, into structural FEA models.
  • Evaluate equipment operating conditions, including temperature distributions, stresses, strains, and material behavior, to assess potential failure mechanisms and remaining service life.
  • Support the evaluation of nondestructive examination (NDE) results and equipment condition assessments, including metallurgical replication, hardness testing, and ultrasonic inspection techniques.
  • Prepare and present detailed technical reports, engineering calculations, and recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders.
  • Contribute to internal research and development initiatives focused on process automation, artificial intelligence applications, and improvements in engineering analysis methods and accuracy.

Leadership & Client-Facing Responsibilities:
  • Provide technical leadership, guidance, and mentorship to junior engineers and analysts to support professional development and knowledge transfer.
  • Serve as a primary technical point of contact for clients, ensuring effective communication of project objectives, deliverables, and engineering recommendations.
  • Lead technical discussions, client meetings, and presentations to communicate project findings and support long-term client relationships.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and other SIA business units to develop engineering solutions that align with client needs and operational requirements.
  • Provide technical oversight and support throughout project execution to ensure quality, accuracy, and timely delivery of engineering services.

Required Skills/Qualifications:
  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or a related engineering discipline.
  • Minimum of 10 years of relevant professional engineering experience, including significant experience in turbomachinery structural design, analysis, or field service engineering support.
  • Demonstrated technical expertise in gas or steam turbine design, structural analysis, and equipment evaluation.
  • Proficiency in 2D and 3D modeling of turbomachinery components, including rotors and blades, using SolidWorks or comparable CAD software.
  • Proficiency in finite element analysis software, including ANSYS or Abaqus, and experience with thermodynamic or fluid simulation software, including AxStream.
  • Strong understanding of creep, fatigue, fracture mechanics, and finite element methods as they relate to equipment failure mechanisms and remaining life assessments.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead complex engineering analyses, interpret technical results, and develop practical engineering recommendations.
  • Advanced computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Excel and ability to automate/optimize processes via the use of AI tools.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.
  • Ability to provide technical leadership and collaborate effectively with clients, multidisciplinary engineering teams, and other technical professionals.

Preferred Qualifications:
  • Master's degree or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
  • Previous experience within the power generation, aerospace, or energy industries.
  • Experience working with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) or independent service providers.
  • Familiarity with gas and steam turbine operations, maintenance, and inspection practices.
  • Experience with fitness-for-service evaluations, remaining life assessments, reverse engineering, and equipment condition assessments.
  • Experience with Microsoft Access, SQL, and programming or scripting languages such as Python or VBA.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or willingness to pursue professional licensure.

Travel & Work Conditions:
  • Less than 10% annual travel, primarily involving occasional visits to power generation facilities during scheduled outage seasons or to client sites and maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) facilities in support of engineering and reverse engineering activities.
  • Occasional fieldwork in power plants, industrial facilities, or MRO facilities may involve exposure to elevated temperatures, noise, and confined spaces.
  • Compliance with applicable company and client safety requirements, including annual drug testing requirements.

Pay Range:
The expected salary range for this position is $100,000 – $160,000. Compensation will be based on experience, qualifications, and location. Leveling may be adjusted based on candidate experience.

Who We Are

Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms.

We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes.

We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact.

What We Build

Our products—Eureka Math and Eureka Math², Wit & Wisdom, Geodes, and the newly launched Arts & Letters ELA—are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide.

  • Eureka Math is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application.

  • Wit & Wisdom® and Arts & Letters ELA™ anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. Geodes® complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy.

These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students.

Where We’re Headed

Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support.

Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale.


Job Purpose

Reporting to the Vice President, Corporate Communications, the Director, Enterprise Communicationswill act as a senior leader responsible for the strategy, execution, and continuous evolution of Great Minds’ internal communications and employer brand functions. Internally, this role will shape how the organization communicates at an enterprise level, ensuring employees are informed, connected to strategy and values, and inspired by the mission and impact that drive Great Minds’ work. Externally, this role will curate, monitor, and disseminate content that tells the story of Great Minds’ mission, culture and values to support recruiting, retention, and sales. The Director will serve as the company’s chief architect of enterprise communication, setting the vision for how the company reaches, engages, and retains a dispersed, impact-driven workforce; positioning Great Minds as an employer of choice; and ensuring internal stories reach external audiences where they can reinforce our brand and reputation.


Responsibilities

  • Strategic Leadership and Team Management:

    • Lead and develop the Internal Communications function, providing strategic direction, coaching, and clear accountability for goals and quality standards.

    • Set the enterprise communications vision and annual strategy, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, culture, and the 2030 student outcomes commitment.

    • Serve as a senior strategic advisor to executive leadership and the VP, Corporate Communications, translating organizational priorities into communications approaches that build clarity, trust, and engagement.

    • Partner deeply across functions to drive alignment, inform communications, and source stories—including HR and Strategy to convey operating values and organizational direction; Research, Product, Sales, and Customer Success to surface impact data and field stories that connect employees to the difference Great Minds makes for students and educators; and Brand, Marketing, and Legal to ensure consistency, accuracy, and voice across all enterprise communications.

  • Enterprise Communications:

    • Own the enterprise-wide internal communications framework—including editorial calendar, governance, channel strategy, and content standards—that keeps employees informed and connected to what matters most.

    • Lead communications for high-stakes, organization-wide moments: executive announcements, leadership transitions, strategic initiatives, transformation efforts, and town halls.

    • Ensure employees have consistent access to need-to-know operational information while also deepening their connection to Great Minds’ strategy, culture, values, and impact.

    • Build and steward a center of excellence model, equipping communications liaisons and cross-functional partners with tools, frameworks, and best practices to strengthen the quality of communications across the organization.

    • Build and operate an employee storytelling engine—partnering with teams that include Product, Research, Sales, and Customer Success to identify, develop, and distribute compelling stories of student and educator impact that connect Great Minds employees to the purpose behind their work.

    • Work closely with HR and Strategy to develop communications that actively convey Great Minds’ operating values, culture commitments, and strategic direction—ensuring employees understand not just what the organization is doing, but why it matters and how they contribute.

    • Develop and implement measurement frameworks (KPIs, engagement data, feedback loops) to continuously assess and improve internal communications effectiveness.

    • Lead the embedding of Great Minds’ refreshed enterprise brand across internal channels and communications—partnering with Brand to ensure voice, visual identity, and messaging standards are consistently reflected in all employee-facing content and experiences.

  • Platform and Channel Evolution:

    • Partner with IT on Great Minds’ internal communications technology roadmap—evaluating, selecting, and optimizing platforms, tools, and formats to enhance reach, usability, and employee experience.

    • Bring technical fluency to channel strategy decisions, including intranet architecture, email platforms, video tools, and emerging collaboration and communications technologies.

    • Drive adoption and governance of communication platforms, ensuring tools are used effectively and equitably across a distributed workforce.

    • Identify gaps in current channel infrastructure and develop phased recommendations for platform evolution that serve both near-term needs and long-term scalability.

  • Employer Brand and Internal Storytelling:

    • Build and lead Great Minds’ employer brand strategy, positioning the organization as a destination for mission-aligned talent and amplifying the employee experience externally.

    • Identify compelling internal stories—from educator impact to employee milestones to culture moments—and develop them into external-facing content in partnership with Media Relations and Brand.

    • Create and sustain an employee storytelling engine that amplifies authentic stories from across the organization to showcase mission impact internally and externally.

    • Collaborate with Media Relations to pitch employee and culture stories to relevant media and talent-focused outlets, expanding the reach of Great Minds’ employer brand.

    • Own Great Minds’ employer reputation strategy—including active management of Glassdoor, LinkedIn employer presence, and other third-party platforms—monitoring sentiment, responding to reviews, and developing proactive strategies to strengthen how the organization is perceived as a place to work.

    • Ensure employer brand messaging is consistent and compelling across internal and external channels, including LinkedIn, Glassdoor, and recruiting materials.

    • Partner with HR and Talent Acquisition to develop communications that support the full employee lifecycle—attraction, onboarding, engagement, and retention.

Requirements

Requirements

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in communications or marketing, with demonstrated ownership of enterprise-wide strategy

  • 5+ years of management experience

  • Experience managing or mentoring direct reports, with a track record of developing talent and building high-functioning teams

  • Experience developing or contributing to employer brand strategy, with an understanding of how internal culture stories translate to external reputation

  • Demonstrated experience managing employer reputation on platforms such as Glassdoor and LinkedIn, including proactive review strategy, sentiment monitoring, and response frameworks

  • Experience building employee or customer storytelling programs that surface and amplify narratives of impact across internal and external channels

  • Experience partnering with brand or creative teams to embed refreshed brand identities into internal communications—including voice, visual standards, and messaging frameworks

  • Proven ability to advise and influence senior executives, translating complex organizational priorities into compelling, accessible messaging

  • Deep expertise in executive communications, change and transformation communications, and large-scale organizational initiatives

  • Strong technical knowledge of internal communications platforms and channel ecosystems—including intranets, email platforms, video tools, and collaboration technology—with the ability to evaluate and recommend platform investments

  • Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills with the ability to adapt voice and tone across formats, audiences, and channels

  • Strong project management skills and the ability to lead multiple complex initiatives

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in a communications function at an education or mission-driven entity

  • Familiarity with media relations related to employer brand and culture storytelling

  • Experience building or transforming an internal communications function, including platform migrations or channel strategy overhauls

  • Track record of using data and analytics to measure communications effectiveness and drive continuous improvement

About Us

Flourish and Thrive Labs is a woman-owned and led consulting firm specializing in public health solutions. Our team, composed of former public health officials, works with state and local health departments across the country, building resilient public health operating systems. We pride ourselves on being different, holding ourselves to high ethical standards, and taking care of each other.

We view our company as an urban neighborhood—a diverse group of individuals coming together to live and work, embracing the beauty in that diversity. We are a wacky bunch who are intent on spreading joy! (We just mailed out stickers to over 200 local health health professionals because we felt they could use more joy!)

As Salesforce, Microsoft, Snowflake, and AWS partners, we specialize in technology implementation with a strong people focus. We combine this with strategic planning, data analysis, coaching, and facilitation to effectively support local public health department staff.

Our core values are:

  • People First
  • Focus on Capacity Building
  • Belief in Continuous Experimentation
  • By Public Heath; For Public Health
  • We Do What Is Right. Always.

We're seeking passionate, joyful individuals who align with our ethos of being different and making a difference.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A TEAM MEMBER WITH PUBLIC HEALTH EXPERIENCE (LOCAL/ TRIBAL/ STATE/ FEDERAL).

About Consulting at F&T Labs

If you're new to consulting, we want to help you understand what makes F&T Labs different and why our approach might be perfect for you. We know transitioning from government and non-profit to consulting can be a big step, but we've designed our work environment to blend the best of both worlds.

First, let's talk about how we work. Unlike traditional consulting firms, we hire you for a role, not a specific project. This means you can contribute to various initiatives that match your expertise and interests. Think of it as bringing your public health superpowers to different challenges where they're needed most.

We believe in measuring what matters. While many consulting firms focus on billable hours, we care about the quality and impact of your work. Time sheets don't measure your success with us – it's measured by the meaningful solutions you help create for our clients and their communities.

Yes, we have utilization targets (consulting speak for how much of your time is spent on client work), but we view these as guideposts rather than strict rules. They help us ensure we're making a sustainable impact while maintaining a healthy business. These targets are meant to motivate, not to create stress.

One of the most dynamic aspects of consulting is its natural rhythm. Some weeks might be bustling with activity, while others might be quieter. We embrace these ebbs and flows because they create space for both intense, focused work and time for learning, reflection, and personal growth. This is part of our philosophy that work and life shouldn't be at odds – they should be integrated in a sustainable and energizing way.

At our core, we're built on a simple belief: when our team members flourish, our clients flourish, and ultimately, communities thrive. That's why we've created an environment that supports your growth, values your expertise, and understands that the best solutions come from people who feel empowered and energized by their work.

If you're passionate about public health and excited about the possibility of expanding your impact through consulting, we'd love to talk with you. Your experience in public health is valuable, and we're here to help you apply it in new and meaningful ways.

Notice

No 3rd Party Recruiters. No Phone Calls. We are unable to do informational interviews at this moment. Candidates who call or schedule a "coffee chat" will be considered disqualified.

Junior Salesforce Developer

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A TEAM MEMBER WITH GOVERNMENTAL PUBLIC HEALTH EXPERIENCE (LOCAL / TRIBAL / STATE / FEDERAL). IF YOU HAVE THAT EXPERIENCE IN ADDITION TO SALESFORCE SKILLS, PLEASE ENSURE IT IS CLEAR ON YOUR RESUME.

What do we mean by governmental public health? We're looking for people who have worked directly for a public health agency: a local health department, tribal health organization, state health department, or federal public health agency like CDC or HRSA. We require this because there's no substitute for the lived experience of navigating government systems, understanding the constraints public health staff face, and developing genuine empathy for the people doing this work. That empathy shapes how we build solutions.

SALESFORCE EXPERIENCE IS REQUIRED FOR THIS ROLE. We are looking for candidates who have hands-on experience with the Salesforce platform, not those looking to learn Salesforce from scratch.

Compensation Note: If a salary range is listed for this position, please note that we will be offering at the starting point of the band. We cover 100% of your health insurance!

Role Overview

We're seeking a Junior Salesforce Developer who brings more than technical skills. We need someone who understands public health and can translate that understanding into solutions that actually work for health department staff.

This role is about building technology that fits how public health actually operates. Your background in public health means you'll understand why a disease investigator needs to access data a certain way, or why a reporting workflow has to account for multiple jurisdictions. You won't just write code to spec. You'll build solutions that make sense because you've lived the work.

You'll be part of a collaborative team working on our PH360 platform and client implementations. You'll learn from senior developers and architects who are invested in your growth, while contributing your own public health expertise to help the team build better solutions. This isn't a role where you'll be coding alone in a corner. You'll be pairing with teammates, participating in design discussions, and helping ensure what we build truly serves our clients.

If you've ever looked at a public health technology system and thought "I could build something better," this is your opportunity.

How You'll Work

You'll be part of an Agile Release Train (ART) that follows SAFe principles. This means:

  • Program Increment (PI) Planning: You'll participate in quarterly planning sessions, learning how technical roadmaps come together and contributing your public health perspective
  • Sprint Collaboration: You'll work in two-week sprints with daily standups, regular backlog refinement, and sprint retrospectives
  • Pair Programming: You'll work alongside senior developers who will help you grow your technical skills
  • Team Problem-Solving: You'll be part of discussions where your understanding of public health workflows helps the team build better solutions

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and maintain Salesforce applications using Apex, Lightning Web Components, and Flow
  • Collaborate with senior developers and architects on solution design
  • Bring your public health perspective to technical discussions and design decisions
  • Participate actively in Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, daily standups, and retrospectives
  • Write clean, well-documented, testable code that follows team standards
  • Learn and apply Salesforce best practices through code reviews and mentorship
  • Help translate public health requirements into technical implementations
  • Ask questions, seek feedback, and continuously improve your craft

Experience Required

  • 1-2 years of hands-on Salesforce development or administration experience (required)
  • 1+ years working for a governmental public health agency (local, state, federal, or tribal)
  • Salesforce Administrator certification required (Platform Developer I preferred, or willingness to obtain within 6 months)
  • Demonstrated ability to learn new technologies quickly
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills

Technical Requirements

  • Hands-on experience with the Salesforce platform (required)
  • Basic understanding of Apex, SOQL, or similar programming languages
  • Familiarity with Salesforce declarative tools (Flow, Process Builder, validation rules)
  • Understanding of relational databases and data modeling concepts
  • Exposure to version control (Git) or willingness to learn

Preferred Qualifications

  • Salesforce Platform Developer I certification
  • Experience with Lightning Web Components or other JavaScript frameworks
  • Familiarity with Agile or SAFe methodology
  • Background in public health data systems, case management, or epidemiology workflows
  • Trailhead Ranger status or significant Trailhead completion

What We Offer for Your Growth

  • Mentorship: You'll be paired with senior developers who are genuinely invested in helping you succeed
  • Certification Support: We'll support your journey to additional Salesforce certifications
  • Learning Time: Our natural consulting rhythm includes quieter periods that create space for training and professional development
  • Meaningful Work: You'll contribute to projects that directly impact public health communities from day one

Notice

Must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship. Willingness to adhere to our no-drug workplace policy. You must agree to undergo eVerify for employment status at hiring.

No 3rd Party Recruiters.

We value initiative. If you're genuinely interested in this role, show us. (However, please do not use the "Schedule a Meeting" feature on our website. You will be disqualified.) We notice candidates who take the extra step to express real interest. Demonstrate the value that you will add to F&T Labs.

At Flourish and Thrive Labs, we believe in the unique value each candidate brings. We encourage applications from diverse backgrounds and experiences, even if you don't meet all listed qualifications

Job Description

  • The Data Builder is the hands-on builder responsible for turning architectural design and business requirements into trusted, reusable data products through MVP that are production grade. Reporting to the Senior Director, Data Operations & Data Management, this role builds to the enterprise-agnostic Silver foundation designed by Data Architecture and co-designs and builds Gold data products where business logic, metrics, and functional knowledge live.
  • This is a hands-on individual contributor role — the build authority that blends business fluency and data engineering discipline in equal measure, authoring Gold data products that answer the question the first time and building them to production standard.
  • This role is a critical execution counterpart to Data Architecture and Data Analysis, Products & Integration, building faithfully against their designs and requirements and compressing the path from new data to a production-grade, reusable asset. It is an exciting opportunity to join the team transforming how Cigna builds and reuses data — delivered through MVP.

Key Responsibilities

Rapid Build & Delivery

  • Build architecture’s designs and analysis’s requirements into production-ready solutions through MVP.
  • Work new and unfamiliar data quickly into a working solution that answers the business question at hand.
  • Refactor learning-stage and bespoke work into durable, reusable, production-ready assets.

Silver — Build to Architecture’s Design

  • Build the physical Silver structures to the enterprise-agnostic Silver model and reference patterns designed by Data Architecture.
  • Implement the design faithfully and promote it to production through governed CI/CD pipelines.
  • Capture business context and metadata at build, and hand off to trusted partner teams as readiness allows.

Gold — Democratized, Delivered Through MVP

  • Treat the Gold layer as democratized — Data Operations may own specific Gold assets and assists other teams in building theirs.
  • Deliver Gold solutions through build-through-MVP, promoted to production-grade through governed CI/CD pipelines regardless of owner.
  • Uphold the build standards and guardrails any Gold solution must meet, so a federated Gold layer stays stable and production-grade across owning teams.

Engineering Discipline & Production Readiness

  • Build to production standards from day one so the lift from MVP to production is simple, not a rebuild.
  • Apply consistent development patterns, naming conventions, and build standards with specific focus on the connectivity across all data products to create a more connected data ecosystem.
  • Move work through the CI/CD pipeline — develop, test, and productionize — clearing quality, security, and cost checks on first pass.
  • Apply AI and automation to accelerate build and testing without bypassing governance, security, or quality expectations.

Partnership & Collaboration

  • Partner with Data Architecture — building to their Silver design and co-designing Gold within the standards they set.
  • Partner with Data Analysis, Products & Integration — who bring the requirements, business rules, and acceptance criteria this role builds against.
  • Partner with Platform Engineering / IT and DevOps & AI Enablement — who own ingestion, pipelines, and the automation frameworks this role builds on.
  • Partner with data science and business analytics teams so Gold data products serve their models, analyses, and decisions.
  • Set the design and hold Data Operations standards across the Hyderabad Data Operations team and outside service partners as part of a global delivery model.

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a pure data engineering or platform role.
  • Not the owner of the enterprise Silver model.
  • Not the primary business-engagement or requirements role.
  • Not the owner of the Gold layer, which is democratized across teams.
  • Not a governance policy, stewardship, or BI reporting role.
  • This role exists to build real data solutions that get used — designed for the business, engineered to last, delivered through MVP.

Required Experience & Capabilities

  • 3+ years building production-grade data solutions, with demonstrated depth in analytics engineering or equivalent business-plus-build work.
  • A genuine 50/50 blend of business fluency and hands-on engineering discipline.
  • Hands-on experience with Databricks, Spark, Unity Catalog, SQL, and Python.
  • Familiarity with Snowflake and Teradata in addition to a Databricks-first stack.
  • Expert knowledge of dimensional and medallion (Silver / Gold) modeling within an enterprise-agnostic data model.
  • Working knowledge of CI/CD pipelines, automated code evaluation, and controlled promotion to production.
  • Strong software-engineering discipline — version control (Git), code review, and efficient, reusable code.
  • Performance-tuning and cost-optimizing Spark and SQL transformations at scale.
  • Familiarity with data governance and cataloging tooling such as Collibra.
  • Automated data-quality testing and validation built into every solution.
  • Demonstrated ability to learn a new data domain fast and turn business logic into reusable data products.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply AI and automation to accelerate build while preserving quality and governance.
  • Experience in complex, regulated enterprises preferred; healthcare or PBM data a plus.

Measures of Success

  • New data reaches a trusted, production-grade asset in a short cycle time.

jobs.description:
À titre de Chercheur et Designer UX/UI chez Intelerad, vous jouerez un rôle clé dans l’évolution de l’expérience utilisateur de nos solutions d’imagerie médicale. Vous serez responsable, de façon autonome, de la recherche utilisateur et de la conception pour un ou plusieurs secteurs de produits, en collaborant étroitement avec les gestionnaires de produits, les développeurs et les utilisateurs finaux afin de transformer des besoins cliniques complexes et des objectifs d’affaires en expériences intuitives et de grande qualité, de la découverte initiale jusqu’au lancement.

Vous apporterez un ensemble de compétences équilibré, en appuyant vos décisions de conception sur des recherches utilisateurs rigoureuses, en transformant les insights en interfaces efficaces et attrayantes, et en contribuant à l’amélioration continue des pratiques UX au sein de l’équipe.

Principales responsabilités

Recherche utilisateur

  • Planifier et diriger de façon autonome des activités de recherche UX qualitatives et quantitatives tout au long du cycle de vie du produit. Utiliser des études terrain, l’observation directe, des entrevues, l’analyse des tâches et des flux de travail, les tests d’utilisabilité et les sondages afin d’identifier des opportunités, valider des hypothèses et orienter les décisions produit.
  • Définir les priorités et les méthodologies de recherche pour votre secteur de produit en collaboration avec l’équipe de gestion de produit; recruter des participants et animer des séances avec des cliniciens et d’autres utilisateurs finaux.
  • Synthétiser les données de recherche sous forme de personas, de cartes de parcours utilisateur (journey maps) et d’informations exploitables, puis transformer les résultats en recommandations de conception et de produit influençant les décisions de feuille de route.
  • Assurer la gestion et l’évolution du dépôt de recherche afin que les résultats demeurent accessibles et continuent d’alimenter les travaux actuels et futurs.

Conception

  • Diriger la conception d’interfaces intuitives de l’idéation jusqu’au lancement, en s’appuyant sur une compréhension approfondie des objectifs utilisateurs, des flux de travail cliniques et des exigences produit. Créer des maquettes d’écran, des modèles d’interaction et des éléments d’interface répondant aux normes d’utilisabilité et aux objectifs d’affaires.
  • Prendre en charge l’ensemble du processus de conception : produire des esquisses fonctionnelles (wireframes), des scénarimages (storyboards), des prototypes interactifs et des spécifications détaillées permettant aux développeurs, analystes en assurance qualité et rédacteurs techniques de comprendre clairement les intentions de conception.
  • Favoriser la création et l’adoption de normes de conception afin d’assurer la cohérence à travers l’ensemble de la suite de produits et accompagner les développeurs dans les décisions et compromis liés au design de l’interface utilisateur.

Communication et collaboration

  • Établir une relation de confiance avec les utilisateurs grâce à l’empathie, à l’écoute active et à de solides compétences d’animation, afin de bien comprendre leurs objectifs, leurs flux de travail et leurs défis.
  • Présenter clairement les résultats de recherche et les concepts de design à différents publics, allant des équipes d’ingénierie jusqu’aux dirigeants produit, et animer des séances de révision critique afin d’assurer l’alignement et la qualité des livrables.
  • Encadrer et conseiller les designers et chercheurs UX moins expérimentés en partageant méthodes, outils et meilleures pratiques.

Qualifications et expérience

  • Baccalauréat en interaction humain-ordinateur (IHO/HCI), en expérience utilisateur (UX), en design d’interaction, en facteurs humains/ergonomie, en psychologie, en design graphique ou expérience équivalente.
  • Minimum de 4 ans d’expérience en design UX/UI et en recherche UX, avec un portfolio démontrant à la fois de solides compétences de conception Web et mobile ainsi qu’une expérience complète en recherche utilisateur.
  • Maîtrise des outils de conception standards de l’industrie, notamment Figma et/ou la suite Adobe Creative Cloud (Photoshop, Illustrator, XD ou équivalent).
  • Expertise démontrée en création de wireframes, de prototypes et de spécifications de conception détaillées.
  • Expérience démontrée dans la planification et la réalisation autonome d’activités de recherche utilisateur utilisant des méthodes qualitatives et quantitatives, ainsi que dans la synthèse des résultats sous forme de personas, de parcours utilisateurs et d’insights exploitables.
  • Familiarité avec des outils et référentiels de recherche UX tels que Dovetail, UserZoom, Optimal Workshop ou des solutions similaires.
  • Excellente connaissance des principes de l’interaction humain-ordinateur (HCI) et des meilleures pratiques en conception centrée sur l’utilisateur.
  • Capacité démontrée à communiquer efficacement les décisions de conception et les conclusions de recherche à des publics techniques et non techniques, y compris à des intervenants de niveau exécutif.
  • Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale en anglais ou équivalent.

Qualifications privilégiées et exigences particulières

  • Expérience en prototypage avec HTML, CSS ou des outils front-end similaires.
  • Expérience dans le domaine des technologies de l’information en santé ou des logiciels d’entreprise complexes; expérience de recherche auprès de cliniciens ou d’utilisateurs du secteur de la santé.
  • Familiarité avec les normes d’accessibilité (WCAG) et les principes de conception inclusive.
  • Connaissance de la conception de sondages et des notions de base en analyse statistique.
  • Expérience dans des environnements de développement Agile.
  • Expérience en mentorat ou en accompagnement informel de designers ou chercheurs UX.
  • Aucune responsabilité de supervision directe.

Exigences relatives aux déplacements

  • Aucun déplacement requis.

Job Title: Compliance Analyst

Location: Remote

Position Type: Full-time


About Us: Solera Holdings is a leading provider of software solutions for the automotive aftermarket industry. We specialize in offering innovative, subscription-based tools and services to help businesses streamline operations, enhance customer experience, and drive profitability. As we continue to grow, we are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Account Compliance Specialist to join our team and help ensure the integrity of our subscription-based accounts.


Job Summary:

The Compliance Analyst will analyze usage reports and abuse trends, identify fraudulent activity, enhance security workflows, and work with teams to mitigate risks. Key duties include data analysis, developing abuse prevention strategies.


The Compliance Analyst will play a critical role in detecting, preventing, and addressing illegal and unauthorized usage of subscription-based accounts. This position involves identifying abuse patterns, setting account limits, and resetting accounts to mitigate fraud or unauthorized access. The role also requires direct communication with legitimate customers and unauthorized users, ensuring account security and resolving issues through re-contracting and upselling initiatives. The ideal candidate will possess strong communication skills, the ability to work collaboratively within a team, and proficiency in Microsoft Office products.


Key Responsibilities:

Account Monitoring & Detection:

  • Detect and address instances of illegal and unauthorized usage on subscription-based accounts. Implement account limits and resets as necessary to maintain compliance and prevent abuse.

Account Management:

  • Reset compromised accounts and issue new temporary credentials to ensure customers’ access is restored securely.
    Promote upselling opportunities where applicable. using our Compliance sales model.

Customer & Unauthorized User Communication:

  • Communicate effectively with legitimate customers to resolve issues and manage account status. Proactively reach out to legitimate customers and explain the situation regarding the unauthorized use.
  • Communicate with unauthorized users to inform them of their violation and direct them to cease their access.

Online Monitoring & Reporting:

  • Conduct regular checks on online marketplaces and forums for illegal sales or distribution of the company's software.
  • Collect evidence of illegal distribution and report findings to appropriate authorities, and legal teams.

Collaboration & Team Support:

  • Collaborate with internal teams to identify trends and refine strategies for abuse detection and prevention.
  • Support the compliance team with ongoing investigations and report escalations. Uncover lead opportunities through resets.

Documentation & Record Keeping:

  • Maintain clear and accurate documentation of interactions and resolutions related to account abuse and unauthorized sales.
  • Ensure all actions are compliant with company policies and legal requirements.

Skills & Qualifications:

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, Information Technology, or a related field preferred
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in account management, compliance, or a similar role, ideally within the software or automotive aftermarket industries.

Technical Skills:

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook) is required.
  • Experience using our sales of subscription management or CRM software is a plus.
  • Working knowledge of the internet and basic IT/account limit setting a plus.

Communication Skills:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to articulate complex issues clearly and professionally to both customers and unauthorized users.
  • Experience in conflict resolution and customer service is an advantage.

Analytical Abilities:

  • Detail-oriented with strong problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to conduct investigations and analyze data to identify trends in illegal or unauthorized account usage.
  • Monitor market trends, attend trade shows, and communicate future compliance needs to management.

Legal & Compliance Knowledge:

  • Understanding of basic internet security practices and compliance regulations in the software industry.
  • Experience with reporting illegal online activities to authorities is a plus.

Key Competencies:

  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to ensuring the integrity of subscription-based services.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Professional demeanor and discretion when dealing with sensitive customer information and compliance issues.

Be part of a fast-growing company in a dynamic and exciting industry.

Work in a supportive, team-oriented environment that encourages professional growth.

Competitive salary and benefits package.

Opportunities for career advancement as the company continues to expand.

Job Posting Closing Date: Open until Filled

Where do you belong?

Your career is more than just a job, it's part of your life. Whether you’re a clinician, or non-clinical professional, at USACS you'll feel a sense of connection working with clinicians and office staff who share your interests and values. We want you to love coming to work each day because you believe in what you do and the people with whom you work. We care about your success.

USACS also understands that location is important. We offer career opportunities for clinicians and non-clinical support staff from New York to Hawaii and numerous points in between. Our supportive culture, outstanding benefits and competitive compensation package is best in class.

Job Description

The Clinician Scheduler develops and manages schedules for clinicians at hospital locations to ensure that all shifts are fully staffed for the expected patient volume. This role will work with Clinicians, Leadership, and Site Directors to ensure appropriate clinician coverage is in place to treat expected patient volumes. The clinician scheduler contributes to the corporation’s financial performance by managing schedules based on tiered prioritization of clinician utilization, optimizing clinician availability, assisting in requesting and planning future over/under staffing needs, and adjusting as needed on a continual basis.

Location: Remote


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:

  • Creates and maintains schedules for multiple hospital locations 45 days before the start of the month.
  • Works independently utilizing scheduling software (Shift Admin) to auto-generate schedules based on customizations, rules, and weightings.
  • Establish relationships with all providers to learn their scheduling preferences and hard stops. Use discretion to determine reasonable asks and when medical director approval/denial is necessary.
  • Analyze requests, identify potential conflict areas, and determine the best solution. If unsuccessful in resolving independently, implement an escalation process.
  • Compile standard reports based on historical data to determine future staffing needs.
  • Collaborate with credentialing, RDO, Directors, or others to ensure available staffing.
  • Work with other clinician schedulers to ensure coordination of the utilization of cross-credentialed providers and days of availability.
  • Work with Scheduling Optimization to schedule traveling physicians and to optimize the site allocation process.
  • Ensure distributed days of availability allow for complete staffing of all shifts. Optimize trades and shift blocking to minimize costs of traveling physician expenses.
  • Responsible for ensuring continuity of care, shift equity, and distribution in accordance with site-specific scheduling policies.
  • Schedule providers based on budgeting tiers. Maximize the use of local FT clinicians based on contractual obligations, followed by PT, STAT, and locums in descending priority.
  • Responsible for coordinating and securing the use of outside clinician resources through locum companies within budgeted goals as necessary to complete the schedule.
  • Modification of shift maps as directed by site leadership
  • Work with the President/VP/Site Directors/RDOs to adjust the schedule for service/budget under immediate deadlines.
  • Work directly with site Physician/APP leaders to ensure optimal schedules before publication.
  • Responsible for ensuring anticipated and last-minute open shifts are filled. Responsible for communicating changes to schedule and providing all necessary parties are aware and in agreement.
  • Responsible for maintaining provider satisfaction regarding the monthly schedule. Ensures expectations are clear of clinician scheduling requirements and expectations from scheduling.
  • Ability to investigate the source of any complaints, analyze the underlying reasons, and resolve them as appropriate.
  • Responsible for setting up Shift Admin and properly applying shifts with pay codes to automate payroll through Workday integration.
  • Utilize strong judgment when deviations from established policies and procedures are necessary to complete schedules based on established deadlines.
  • Communicates terms and premium rates with providers to ensure all shifts are covered after the provider is scheduled to contract max by site leadership.
  • On Call responsibilities may be required.
  • Discretion in the escalation process when clinician leadership support is necessary to create a schedule effectively.
  • Responsible for ensuring all parties agree with scheduling policies and decisions surrounding specific issues, including local and support clinician leadership.
  • Analyze metrics and reporting, able to communicate results

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

  • Ability to navigate and function under a dual and remote reporting structure
  • Strong organization and problem-solving skills
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to prioritize competing needs
  • Uses critical thinking skills to make decisions
  • Professional presentation/phone savvy
  • High-level analytics skills
  • Ability to effectively perform in a multi-task work environment
  • Ability to maintain patience and composure in difficult situations
  • Ability to identify and communicate emerging issues to management
  • Knowledge and skills in using personal computers (Windows) with a strong emphasis on Microsoft Office
  • Programs- Outlook, Word, Excel and Adobe Acrobat
  • Technical ability with scheduling software

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred
  • Experience creating/managing complex fluid schedules
  • Shift admin scheduling experience preferred
  • Previous experience working with clinicians preferred

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:

  • This position requires long periods of sitting and reviewing data on computer monitors
  • Required to have close visual acuity to perform the job

Hourly Rate: $21.59-$39.94

Hourly rate may be determined on several factors including but not limited to knowledge, skills, experience, education, geographical location and requirements stated in job description.

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance options

Additional compensation may include bonus eligibility, equity, or other incentive programs, depending on the role.

Specific benefit offerings and eligibility will be provided during the hiring process and may be subject to change in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.

Overview

DecisionPoint seeks a Senior ITSM / Service Management Lead to own the Information Technology Service Management Plan and Service Management System for the USMEPCOM ENLIST program. This role provides enterprise-wide leadership for IT service-management governance, process integration, service-quality improvement, performance management, and ITIL best-practice adoption across all required service-management processes.

The ITSM / Service Management Lead will establish the operating model for consistent service delivery across ENLIST tasks, define process ownership and accountability, oversee SLA/SLO performance, and lead the program’s service-management maturity evolution. The successful candidate will work closely with program leadership, service owners, process owners, technical teams, quality personnel, tool administrators, subcontractors, and Government stakeholders to improve service outcomes and advance the program toward ITIL Version 5 practices.

This position is remote, with preference given to candidates located in or near Chicago.

Note: By applying to this position, you acknowledge and consent to having your resume included in an active competitive government contract bid.

Duties & Responsibilities

The ITSM / Service Management Lead will:

  • Own the development, implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the program ITSM Plan.
  • Establish and govern the Service Management System, including its policies, processes, controls, roles, responsibilities, technologies, and reporting structure.
  • Lead implementation and integration of the 21 required service-management processes across ENLIST tasks and technical service areas.
  • Define process ownership, accountability, governance forums, escalation paths, interfaces, and decision authorities.
  • Develop and maintain an ITSM maturity roadmap aligned with program priorities, Government requirements, and recognized industry practices.
  • Lead the adoption and practical application of ITIL best practices and the program’s progression toward ITIL Version 5.
  • Promote consistent, efficient, effective, measurable, and well-documented service delivery throughout the service lifecycle.
  • Govern service strategy, service design, service transition, service operations, and continual-improvement activities.
  • Oversee service portfolio, technology strategy, cost control, service catalog, service-level, availability, capacity, continuity, and information-security management.
  • Oversee project transition, service asset and transition, change, release and deployment, knowledge, and service-validation processes.
  • Oversee event, incident, request, problem, and access-management processes.
  • Define, negotiate, document, monitor, and improve Service Level Agreements, Service Level Objectives, key performance indicators, and operating-level expectations.
  • Establish performance thresholds, measurement methods, reporting requirements, service-review procedures, and escalation criteria.
  • Analyze performance trends, service risks, recurring failures, bottlenecks, customer-impacting issues, and systemic process gaps.
  • Lead continual-improvement planning and maintain a prioritized register of improvement initiatives, owners, benefits, milestones, and outcomes.
  • Coordinate corrective and preventive actions and verify that implemented solutions address root causes.
  • Ensure that service-management processes respond effectively to changing mission requirements, priorities, technologies, and user needs.
  • Identify opportunities to improve service quality, reduce disruption, increase automation, strengthen integration, and realize cost efficiencies.
  • Govern development and quality review of Daily System Status Reports and other operational service reports.
  • Ensure timely communication of system performance, upcoming events, outages, maintenance, risks, and activities affecting user access to services.
  • Provide ITSM status, performance metrics, risks, decisions, and improvement updates for Monthly Status Reports, project status meetings, Program Management Reviews, and executive briefings.
  • Coordinate with the Quality Manager and QA personnel on process audits, service-quality reviews, findings, corrective actions, and improvement opportunities.
  • Guide configuration and use of ITSM platforms, workflows, service catalogs, dashboards, knowledge bases, automation, and reporting capabilities.
  • Establish and maintain ITSM policies, standard operating procedures, process maps, knowledge articles, templates, control matrices, and governance records.
  • Facilitate service reviews, governance meetings, process-owner forums, maturity assessments, and continual-improvement workshops.
  • Provide coaching and guidance to service owners, process owners, task leads, and technical teams on ITSM responsibilities and practices.
  • Support transition-in and transition-out activities by ensuring that service-management processes, records, tools, responsibilities, and knowledge are transferred effectively.
  • Protect sensitive Government, program, operational, performance, and personnel information.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Active Secret clearance or higher.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Business Management, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 8 years of relevant professional experience.
  • Current ITIL Foundation certification or higher.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading enterprise IT service management, service delivery, IT operations, or Service Management System implementation.
  • Experience owning or leading an ITSM Plan in a complex, multi-team technology environment.
  • Experience supporting Department of Defense, federal civilian, or other large Government IT programs.
  • Experience leading ITIL adoption, process integration, maturity improvement, or service-management transformation.
  • Experience establishing process-owner governance, responsibility matrices, decision authorities, escalation procedures, and cross-process interfaces.
  • Experience implementing and governing service strategy, design, transition, operations, and continual-improvement processes.
  • Experience defining, negotiating, monitoring, and reporting SLAs, SLOs, key performance indicators, and operating-level expectations.
  • Experience leading service-performance reviews, maturity assessments, process audits, root-cause analyses, and continual-improvement initiatives.
  • Experience managing service portfolios, service catalogs, knowledge bases, process repositories, and improvement registers.
  • Experience with incident, problem, change, release, deployment, request, event, access, knowledge, configuration, availability, capacity, continuity, and service-level management.
  • Experience integrating ITSM processes across infrastructure, cloud, cybersecurity, software engineering, service desk, data, and mission-support teams.
