jobs.description:
ORDERYOYO

Lead Software Engineer – Payments

Remote · Quarterly team gatherings in one of our global offices · Competitive salary

About the Role

At OrderYOYO, payments sit at the heart of everything we do. Every order placed, every restaurant paid, and every dispute resolved runs through the systems this team owns and operates.

We're looking for a Lead Software Engineer – Payments to own the next stage of our payments platform's evolution — as a hands-on technical leader who can grow and manage a team of payments engineers, set the technical direction for a business-critical domain, and support our transition to a more scalable operating model across online ordering and in-store platforms (POS, Kiosk, and payment terminals).

You'll play a central role in shaping how OrderYOYO handles money — from authorisation and settlement to disputes and merchant invoicing — while building and developing the people who make that possible.

Role Mission

Lead the people, architecture, and delivery behind OrderYOYO's payments platform — enabling KYC onboarding, deductions, settlement/payout timing, dispute flows, and merchant invoicing — while growing a high-performing engineering team and raising the bar on reliability, security, and engineering quality in one of our most business-critical domains.

Core Responsibilities

People Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead, mentor, and grow a team of payments engineers — providing hands-on technical guidance, regular feedback, and clear paths for career development.
  • Own hiring and team-building for the payments engineering function, partnering with recruiting to define role profiles, run interviews, and bring in strong talent.
  • Run day-to-day people management: 1:1s, goal-setting, performance reviews, and career progression conversations for direct reports.
  • Build a team culture where payments knowledge is documented and shared, not tribal — through design reviews, standards, and mentoring.
  • Represent the payments engineering team in leadership and cross-functional conversations, translating business needs into technical strategy and team priorities.
  • Balance hands-on technical contribution with people-management responsibilities, staying close enough to the codebase to lead by example and unblock the team.

Technical & Domain Ownership

  • Set the technical direction and long-term architecture strategy for payment-domain services, including gateway integrations, payment intent/authorisation/capture/refund flows, payout orchestration, and reconciliation.
  • Oversee marketplace capabilities: onboarding/KYC integration, merchant configuration, settlement instructions, deductions, and invoicing/merchant-statement alignment.
  • Ensure robust “flow-of-funds” primitives across the team's systems — idempotency, ledgers/events, and audit trails that are fully supportable for finance and compliance.
  • Own the strategy for PSP and partner integrations, with close attention to tri-party / sub-merchant implications where applicable.
  • Oversee dispute/chargeback and fraud-handling touchpoints across internal workflows and PSP tooling, and drive collaboration with Ops on runbooks and escalation paths.
  • Partner closely with Product, Legal/Compliance, Finance, and Support to convert requirements into safe, testable production behaviour.
  • Raise engineering quality in a high-change domain: automated testing, safe rollouts/canaries, observability, and incident-response improvements, with accountability for outcomes across the team.

Must-Have Requirements

  • Proven experience leading, mentoring, or people-managing a team of software engineers — including hiring, performance management, and career development.
  • Strong backend engineering background in distributed systems — microservices, async processing, resilient APIs, and eventual consistency.
  • Production experience with payment flows (auth/capture/refund, webhooks, reconciliation) and “money correctness” patterns such as idempotency keys, double-entry thinking, and auditability.
  • A solid security mindset: PCI compliance, PII protection, secrets management, least privilege, and secure coding practices.
  • Comfort working in an Azure-first environment (APIs, queues/eventing, monitoring), with strong CI/CD and automated testing practices.
  • Clear, confident communication with both engineers and non-technical stakeholders in high-stakes scenarios — incidents, financial breaks, and compliance requests.
  • Strong judgement on when to move fast, when to standardise, and when to say “not yet” with evidence — balancing team capacity, technical debt, and business priorities.

Strong-to-Have Experience

  • Experience scaling or restructuring an engineering team through periods of growth or organisational change.
  • Experience with sub-merchant, marketplace, or Payfac-like operating models (KYC, underwriting, settlements, fee deductions).
  • Familiarity with dispute tooling, card scheme rules, 3DS/risk rules, or fraud platforms.
  • Experience partnering with Legal, Compliance, or Finance leadership on regulatory or audit requirements.

Who We Are

At OrderYOYO, company culture comes first. We create a positive, inclusive environment where people are trusted to do their best work and take ownership of what they build. Personal development is central to how we work — engineers are encouraged to grow technically, take responsibility, and help shape how our products and platforms evolve.

We help restaurants succeed online by providing branded websites, mobile apps, and tailored marketing solutions, giving them full control of their business. By removing high commission fees charged by third-party platforms, we empower restaurants to grow sustainably.

Through our partnership with AppSmart, the market leader in POS and in-store systems, we've become the largest restaurant-focused platform in Europe.

What We Offer

• Competitive salary.

  • A remote role — work from wherever you do your best work, with quarterly in-person gatherings at one of our global offices.
  • High ownership and autonomy, with a direct hand in shaping the team you lead.
  • A clear leadership mandate, with scope to grow further into broader engineering management responsibilities.
  • The opportunity to lead work on revenue-critical production systems.
  • A strong focus on security, reliability, and engineering best practices.
  • A collaborative, international engineering team.
  • Real emphasis on learning, mentoring, and long-term growth — for you and for the people you lead.

FICO (NYSE: FICO)is a leading global analytics software company, helping businesses in 100+ countries make better decisions. Join our world-class team today and fulfill your career potential!

The Opportunity


This position is a great opportunity for a strategic, creative, and AI-savvy marketer with a proven track record of designing and executing multi-channel enterprise B2B marketing programs that start conversations and drive and accelerate pipeline at scale.

This director owns solution campaign marketing for North American growth accounts— the broad base of prospect and early-stage accounts across FICO's target industries. The mandate is to build interest, awareness, and qualified pipeline across that account universe so that accounts land, generate initial ARR, and earn a place in our Pod-based ABM program. This role is the engine that feeds the Pods, which are responsible for expansion of our FICO® Platform solution across our existing customer accounts.


What You’ll Contribute


  • Serve as the strategic solution campaign marketing lead for all NorAm growth accounts. You’ll set priorities and orchestrate execution, collaborating with FICO’s digital, value messaging team, events, and SDR teams without direct management authority — requiring strong influence and coalition-building skills.
  • Design and execute well-orchestrated, scalable multi-channel campaigns incorporating email, webinars, advertising, tradeshows, and other 1:Many tactics to create awareness and interest across account base and convert it into qualified pipeline.   • Define and run the account journey from first touch to "Pod-ready": build and manage a consistent set of criteria and handoff process, in partnership with sales and Pod leadership, for when a landed account with initial ARR graduates from campaign-based coverage into a Pod for ongoing ABM.
  • Own marketing-sourced pipeline, new-logo, and initial-ARR targets across assigned account base, and manage the allocated marketing budget against those targets.

  • Develop messaging strategies and content for emails, webinars, and events, collaborating closely with product marketing and other stakeholders.

  • Deep knowledge of complex selling environments in the B2B technology world and what it takes to build brand and product awareness and pipeline.

  • Creative skills in both communications and problem solving.
  • Expertise in using metrics and marketing performance measurement to optimize results and ROI in a corporate marketing environment.
  • Strong experience using GenAI to develop demand generation and event content and personalize content to specific personas and accounts, and — ideally — broader experience exploring AI-driven approaches to pipeline generation beyond content creation (see above).
  • Outstanding writing and presentation skills.
  • A passion for technology, learning, and creativity.
  • Knowledge and experience building demand marketing plans, and a clear point of view on how campaign-based demand generation and Pod-based ABM should hand off to one another as accounts mature.
  • Bachelor’s degree, preferably in marketing or a related field.

Our Offer to You


  • An inclusive culture strongly reflecting our core values: Act Like an Owner, Delight Our Customers, and Earn the Respect of Others.

  • Highly competitive compensation, benefits, and rewards programs that encourage you to bring your best every day and be recognized for doing so.

At FICO, you can develop your career with a leading organization in one of the fastest-growing fields in technology today – Big Data analytics. Who You Are

jobs.description:
Position Title: Senior Consultant or Principal Consultant - Microsoft Modern Work Solutions

Position Location: Remote in the Contiguous United States

Job Summary:

As a Senior Consultant or Principal Consultant (depending on experience level) within our Digital Workplace Practice, you will lead the design and delivery of Microsoft Modern Work solutions, with a focus on mergers and acquisitions (M&A), divestitures, Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migrations, and endpoint solutions with Microsoft Intune. You will guide clients through discovery, architecture, migration planning, execution, and post-migration stabilization across identity, messaging, collaboration, and endpoints. This hands-on consulting role combines technical delivery, client advisory, and team mentorship to help organizations integrate or separate workplaces while protecting data, maintaining business continuity, and minimizing disruption to users.

Essential Functions:

  • Assist with statement of work development and validation as needed.
  • Lead client discovery, workshops, and readiness assessments across Microsoft 365, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and endpoint management to define Modern Work requirements, M&A objectives, migration scope, dependencies, integration or separation timelines, and business continuity needs.
  • Develop migration strategies, effort estimates, workload sequencing, migration waves, cutover runbooks, and rollback or recovery plans with clear assumptions, exclusions, and acceptance criteria. Evaluate migration tools against workload coverage, limitations, client constraints, and cost.
  • Develop target-state recommendations and architecture diagrams for Microsoft 365 tenant consolidation and separation, including identity alignment, hybrid dependencies, coexistence, domain transitions, access controls, and endpoint integration, in partnership with security and infrastructure teams.
  • Lead hands-on migrations of mailboxes, OneDrive accounts, SharePoint sites, and Teams content, coordinating engineering teams and vendors while managing permissions, data integrity, and workload-specific limitations.
  • Configure Microsoft 365 services and coordinate identity transitions, including Microsoft Entra ID, directory synchronization, and application access.
  • Design and implement endpoint solutions with Microsoft Intune, including Windows Autopilot provisioning, device configuration and compliance policies, application deployment and protection, endpoint security policies, and Windows update management. Plan device enrollment and management transitions for M&A integrations and tenant migrations, minimizing disruption to users.
  • Execute pilots, migration testing, cutover validation, and troubleshooting to verify data, mail flow, sign-in, collaboration, device access, and security controls; provide post-migration stabilization and operational handoff.
  • Partner with project managers to define workstreams, resource needs, milestones, and cutover schedules, aligning technical delivery with client communications, service desk readiness, and user adoption activities.
  • Manage technical risks, dependencies, and scope changes, including licensing, administrative access, application integrations, data retention requirements, and transition service agreement deadlines where applicable.
  • Communicate decisions, progress, risks, and user impacts to technical and executive stakeholders. Mentor consultants.
  • Develop and improve reusable migration playbooks, automation, packaged solutions, standardized templates, methodologies, and delivery standards.

Required Skills/Abilities/Competencies:

  • Excellent customer service skills.
  • Strong technical leadership skills with the ability to mentor other team members and develop their skillsets.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills, with attention to detail and the ability to prioritize tasks, delegate appropriately, and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to function well in a high-paced and at times stressful environment, handling multiple simultaneous engagements.
  • Strong hands-on expertise in Microsoft 365 administration, design, implementation, and migration across Exchange Online, OneDrive, and Teams, including Microsoft 365 licensing dependencies.
  • Hands-on experience delivering Microsoft Intune solutions for Windows endpoints, including Windows Autopilot, device enrollment, configuration profiles, compliance policies, application packaging and deployment, endpoint security, update policies, PKI, and Cloud PKI. Ability to assess existing device management environments and troubleshoot provisioning, policy, application, and access issues during endpoint modernization and tenant transitions.
  • Proficiency with PowerShell for Microsoft 365 administration, reporting, and migration automation, and familiarity with Microsoft Graph.
  • Hands-on proficiency with Quest and AvePoint is required as the primary migration toolset; familiarity with ForensIT, BitTitan, and PowerSync Pro is preferred for use as secondary tools as project and client needs dictate.
  • Strong understanding of Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, hybrid identity, directory synchronization, UPN and domain changes, authentication, Conditional Access, and their impact on migration sequencing and user access.
  • Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to analyze complex technical issues and develop effective solutions.
  • Strong communication, interpersonal, and presentation skills, with the ability to interact effectively with clients and internal stakeholders.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in Microsoft Modern Work consulting, Microsoft 365 engineering, or enterprise migrations, including technical leadership of complex client engagements.
  • Demonstrated delivery of Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migrations supporting mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, or enterprise consolidation, including discovery, coexistence, workload and identity sequencing, cutover, and post-migration support.
  • Relevant Microsoft certifications in Microsoft 365 administration, identity and access, endpoint management, or collaboration.

Physical Requirements:

  • Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

Belong to Something Beautiful

At Sephora, beauty is about feeling seen, valued, and empowered, individually and collectively. It is connecting deeply with others, celebrating diversity and inclusivity, unlocking your potential, and making a difference every day. Together, we belong to something beautiful. 

Your Role at Sephora

Ready for a career glow up? As Retail Communications Manager, Translation and Localization, you’ll lead the development and delivery of accurate, inclusive, and contextually relevant Spanish-language content for Sephora’s retail organization. The work you do will impact beauty, as you help ensure store teams receive clear, consistent, and culturally relevant information that supports seamless execution and an exceptional client experience. You’ll be part of the Retail Communications team, which supports more than 650 Sephora stores, 1,000 Sephora at Kohl’s locations, retail leadership, brand partners, and Asset Protection. You’ll collaborate with partners who are equally passionate about delivering the right information at the right time, while establishing translation standards, managing workflows, and preserving Sephora’s business intent and store-centered voice across languages.

What You’ll Do

Translation & Localization

  • Manage end-to-end Spanish translation and localization across the department using translation technology for key deliverables, including policies, guidelines, communications, eLearnings, PDFs, videos, and audio.
  • Translate, edit, proofread, and adapt content into Spanish while preserving business intent, tone, terminology, clarity, and cultural and contextual relevance.
  • Establish and maintain quality-assurance practices for Spanish-language content, including version control, accessibility, and publishing accuracy.
  • Monitor published Spanish-language content and coordinate corrections, updates, or retirement when source content changes.
  • Identify and implement improvements to translation processes, tools, and workflows to increase speed, consistency, and quality.
  • Maintain and consistently apply translation glossaries, style guides, and terminology standards for Spanish-language content.
  • Manage translation request prioritization by evaluating content readiness, business priority, timing, effort, audience impact, and localization risks.

Collaboration (or Cross-Functional Partnership)

  • Collaborate across the organization, including with Retail Communications, Instructional Design, Retail Training, HR, Legal, and subject-matter experts, to confirm business intent, resolve source-content questions, and validate specialized terminology.
  • Partner with the Retail Communications and Design teams to ensure translated materials follow established content, brand, design, and store-voice standards.
  • Provide translation and localization expertise to cross-functional partners, identifying risks and recommending solutions when content cannot be translated directly without affecting clarity, meaning, or audience relevance.

Retail Communication Optimizations

  • Embrace a continuous improvement mindset, driving excellence across communications responsibilities.
  • Continually evaluate, lead, and participate in improvements to Retail Communications processes and tools to ensure they remain effective and relevant.
  • Travel to Sephora stores as needed to monitor project progress and adoption, gather feedback and insights, and develop new or improved procedures.
  • Support and own special projects, leveraging your expertise to ensure successful execution and alignment with broader business goals.

Retail Communications Support

While the primary focus of this role is translation and localization, you may occasionally support core retail communications during peak periods, coverage gaps, or special projects.
  • Create and execute comprehensive and compelling communication strategies for stores and retail leadership, supporting clarity and alignment across the business.
  • Provide expert guidance on messaging, timing, methods, and communication vehicles to maximize impact.
  • Serve as a gatekeeper by evaluating communication requests across departments to ensure they are necessary and aligned with organizational priorities.

What You’ll Bring

  • Four or more years of professional translation and localization experience.
  • Full professional fluency in Spanish and English, both written and spoken, with demonstrated experience translating, editing, proofreading, and adapting business content in both languages.
  • Strong knowledge of linguistic quality assurance, cultural adaptation, and maintaining consistent tone, style, and technical terminology across languages.
  • Experience using Content Management Systems, Translation Management Systems, translation-memory tools, or similar translation technologies.
  • Strong project-management and organizational skills, with the ability to prioritize a high volume of requests and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent listening and collaboration skills, with a commitment to understanding business-partner and audience needs.
  • Sound judgment and critical-thinking skills, including the ability to solve problems independently, navigate ambiguity, and recognize when to escalate concerns.
  • Flexibility and resilience when managing changing priorities, time-sensitive requests, and evolving business needs.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Acrobat and Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • A degree in translation, communications, linguistics, business, or a related field is preferred.
  • Professional certification in translation or localization is preferred.
  • Experience in retail communications, professional communications, or a retail environment is preferred.
  • Experience with Articulate Storyline, Articulate Rise, Vyond, Adobe Creative Suite, closed-captioning tools, audio-editing software, AI voiceover tools, or XLIFF files is a plus.
  • Experience with Retail Zipline or learning-management systems is a plus.
  • A proactive approach, openness to feedback, and commitment to continuous learning and improvement.

What You’ll Get:

The annual base salary range for this position is $86,105.00 - $114,570.00 The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, which may include, as applicable, the applicant’s qualifications for the position; years of relevant experience; specific and unique skills; level of education attained; certifications or other professional licenses held; other legitimate, non-discriminatory business factors specific to the position; and the geographic location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will perform the job. Individuals employed in this position may also be eligible to earn bonuses. This job will be posted for a minimum of five days.

jobs.description:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That’s the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Job Category

Claim

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$104,000.00 - $171,700.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Major Case Specialist, Excess Casualty, you are responsible for investigating, evaluating, reserving, negotiating, and resolving the office and/or department's most complex, high-exposure, and highest-severity injury and/or property damage claims within appropriate authority and oversight. You will serve as an expert technical resource to claim professionals, business partners, customers, and other stakeholders.

As of the date of this posting, Travelers anticipates that the posting will remain open until October 30th, 2026.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage and oversee an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles high complexity injury and/or property damage claims which includes coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Conduct detailed investigations to gather evidence, assess liability and determine extent of damages and establish appropriate reserves.
  • Evaluate claim information and documentation to make informed decisions regarding coverage and resolutions.
  • Engage in negotiations with claimants, legal representatives, and other parties to achieve fair and equitable resolutions.
  • Develop and execute advanced resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Prepare and present detailed reports on claim status, trends and outcomes to senior management.
  • Work closely with legal, underwriting, and other departments to ensure coordinated claim handling.
  • Partner with Counsel to develop, direct, and execute litigation management strategies.
  • Maintain comprehensive and accurate records of all claim activities, communications, and decisions.
  • Identify areas in which we can improve or enhance current best practices and offer creative solutions.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers’ requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • May require travel, including overnight stays, to attend mediations, trials, arbitration, etc.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor’s Degree.
  • Five plus years of complex, bodily injury claim and litigation experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management and estimating software, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to understand, synthesize, interpret, and convey complex information in a simplified manner to multiple stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to make independent decisions and handle complex claims, evaluate severe losses, and negotiate settlements strategically.
  • Exceptional customer service skills; demonstrated ability to manage relationships with key stakeholders while delivering a consistently positive experience.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Expert-level negotiation and conflict resolution skills with the ability to apply strategic claim handling practices.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Expert level knowledge of insurance principles, policy language, exclusions, and ISO forms with thorough understanding of business line products.
  • Strong understanding of state and federal insurance regulations, fair claims practices legislation, and legal requirements, with the ability to apply this knowledge to complex claims.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Four years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members – including spouses, domestic partners, and children – are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

ICF's Disaster Management Division seeks a Senior Director, Housing Implementation (Sector Lead) to direct a major sector within the HUD Line of Business, with accountability for business growth, delivery quality, financial performance, and people leadership across ICF's housing implementation portfolio. This Remote U.S. senior leadership role guides single-family housing recovery programs, construction management and resilient housing initiatives for state, local, territorial, utility, and developer clients.


The Sector Lead establishes the strategy and direction for the housing implementation practice in alignment with Line of Business and Division strategic plans. The role leads through an experienced management team rather than through direct project delivery and holds three interlocking accountabilities: growing the sector’s book of business, managing sector staff for high performance, and ensuring consistent delivery across all projects in the portfolio.


This is an opportunity for an experienced disaster recovery, grant management, operations, and housing leader to shape a business-critical sector, build trusted client relationships, develop leadership talent, ensure operational excellence across project teams, and deliver sustained growth and quality across a complex national portfolio.


Responsibilities:

Sector Strategy and Market Position

  • Establish multi-year sector strategy and annual operating goals using housing expertise, HUD policy and funding direction, market trends, competitive intelligence, and company priorities.
  • Anticipate and address complex housing implementation challenges, including changes in CDBG-DR program design, procurement practices, delivery models, and resilience funding.
  • Strengthen ICF’s market position as a thought leader by representing the company with clients, industry groups, and conferences and contributing to Line of Business and Division planning.

Business Development and Growth

  • Lead sector growth from opportunity identification through capture, teaming, proposal strategy, pricing, and bid/no-bid recommendations in partnership with Line of Business, account, and business development leaders.
  • Achieve $40 million in annual sales and maintain a qualified pipeline of at least $100 million, with disciplined quarterly review of coverage, quality, risk, and conversion assumptions.
  • Build senior client relationships, influence key decisions, and expand cross-sector and cross-Line of Business opportunities by connecting clients with ICF’s full capabilities.

Portfolio, Financial, and Delivery Oversight

  • Own sector financial performance, including $30 million in recognized annual revenue, $40 million in contract awards, a $100 million qualified pipeline, profitability, margin, utilization, and backlog burn.
  • Direct portfolio delivery through Project Managers and senior managers, establishing consistent standards, controls, quality benchmarks, staffing, and early intervention for projects that are off plan.
  • Balance client satisfaction, execution, innovation, profitability, and risk while ensuring compliance with CDBG-DR regulations, locality specific program policies and procedures, 2 CFR 200 and other state-specific financial and procurement requirements, applicable relocation requirements, building codes, and other client-specific requirements.

People Leadership and Talent Development

  • Lead the sector through subordinate managers and senior managers, with accountability for workforce planning, hiring, staffing, bench management, performance, engagement, and succession depth.
  • Develop leadership talent through mentoring, Impact Conversations, internal mobility, and clear alignment between individual roles, the sector strategy, and business goals.
  • Create an inclusive, high-performing environment and provide calm, decisive leadership during challenges, constraints, and post-disaster surge conditions.

Cross-Organizational Leadership

  • Lead collaboration across sector and Line of Business boundaries, removing barriers to sharing staff, capabilities, and client relationships.
  • Champion ICF’s strategy, mission, and direction while fostering timely decision-making, agility, and an entrepreneurial mindset.
  • Engage stakeholders in critical cross-organizational decisions to resolve staffing, resource, and client-ownership issues and achieve aligned outcomes.

Measures of Success

  • Achieve annual revenue, sales, pipeline, profitability, qualification discipline, and win-rate goals established in the approved operating plan.
  • Deliver consistent quality demonstrated through client satisfaction, strong CPARS and past-performance ratings, on-time and on-budget execution, and no material compliance findings.
  • Advance talent and organizational outcomes through retention, internal promotion, engagement, succession depth, cross-sector collaboration, and strategic initiative leadership.

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in disaster recovery, housing, or community development programs, including substantial CDBG-DR housing implementation experience.
  • 5+ years leading through subordinate managers, with demonstrated accountability for business results and staff performance.
  • 5+ years of demonstrated knowledge of HUD CDBG-DR and CDBG-MIT regulatory frameworks, 2 CFR 200, and housing program delivery models, including single-family rehabilitation and reconstruction, affordable housing development, and buyout-adjacent housing programs.
  • 2+ years of demonstrated business development experience, including capture leadership and proposal strategy for competitive state and local procurements.
  • 2+ years of experience managing a portfolio with profit and loss responsibility of $20 million or more in annual revenue.
  • Willing and able to travel by air and vehicle, with anticipated travel up to 50% (TBD).

  • Recognized external presence in the disaster recovery housing field through publications, conference speaking, or industry working groups.
  • Experience leading organizations through structural or operating-model change.

jobs.description:
WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The Manager, Artist Agreements & Clearances is a cross-company role responsible for securing and managing artist agreements, releases, and content clearances in support of production and distribution across the Recording Academy and its affiliates. In this position, you will be a key liaison between internal stakeholders, artists, managers, labels, publishers, and legal teams, supporting events, series, exhibits, GRAMMY Studios programming, and expanding organizational objectives. You are a detail-oriented professional with a genuine passion for music and the music industry. You excel at building and maintaining strong relationships, can balance creative needs with legal and company requirements, and are calm under pressure. You have a collaborative spirit and service mentality.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Artist Releases & Agreements

  • Draft, negotiate, execute, and manage artist agreements and releases across all Recording Academy and affiliate productions, ensuring timely execution for live and pre-recorded content.
  • Maintain organized records of all agreements, including rights granted, restrictions, and obligations.
  • Partner with internal stakeholders to ensure content usage plans and artist negotiations are accurately reflected in contractual terms.

Sync and Misc. Clearances

  • Secure synchronization rights and related clearances for music and content use across all Recording Academy and affiliate platforms.
  • Coordinate with record labels, publishers, PROs, and other rights holders to obtain necessary licenses.
  • Track and manage rights by territory, media, term, and usage to ensure compliance.
  • Oversee the license lifecycle, including payments, amendments, extensions, expirations, and archiving
  • Troubleshoot and resolve clearance issues under tight production timelines.
  • Support additional clearance needs, including artwork, likeness, podcast, and other media usage.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work with internal stakeholders early in the process to assess and address clearance, release, and agreement needs.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for all artist-related contractual and clearance matters.
  • Clearly communicate requirements, risks, and timelines to internal and external stakeholders.

Process & Systems Management

  • Refine workflows for outreach, negotiations, contract execution, and rights tracking.
  • Maintain and improve systems for documenting, tracking, and reporting rights and permissions.
  • Keep standardized clearance process resources current and accessible.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve efficiency, and mitigate risk.

Risk Management & Compliance

  • Ensure content is cleared prior to distribution across all platforms.
  • Flag risks and escalate issues appropriately.
  • Stay current on music rights, licensing practices, and industry standards.

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s Degree required.
  • 5+ years’ experience in music business affairs, content clearance, and music publishing.
  • Paralegal experience and/or the ability to draft and review content licensing agreements and negotiate terms with knowledge of how smaller negotiations affect big-picture relationships.
  • Established relationships with record labels, music publishers, and artist management.
  • Proficiency in Spanish and/or Portuguese preferred.
  • Exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and comprehensive follow-through.
  • Flexibility to succeed in a fast-paced production environment with tight deadlines.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects proactively and independently while providing cross-company support.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time.

SALARY AND BENEFITS

The starting salary for this position is $64,400 to $70,800 per year, benchmarked against industry standards. Salaries for positions required to be in specific geographic locations reflect the corresponding labor market.

The actual offer extended will depend on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and the role's requirements. Positions working 20+ hours per week also receive our comprehensive benefits package (with medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, generous paid time off, and more). Click here for an overview of our company benefits.

Explore our career opportunities to join a team that values creativity, innovation, and diversity.

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. Hi, thanks for checking out our job board!
If you're an entrepreneurial-minded builder who loves to work with great people to solve wicked problems that have a meaningful impact, read on to see if this position might be a good fit for you!

WHO WE ARE

Outdoor Afro celebrates and inspires Black connections and leadership in nature. Our network also connects Black people with our lands, water, and wildlife through outdoor education, recreation, and conservation. Examples of Outdoor Afro’s year-round activities range from fishing, hiking, biking, kayaking, gardening, skiing and more! Visit: to learn more.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Strategic Development & Partnerships Director oversees the strategy and operational excellence of Outdoor Afro’s partnerships and development efforts. In addition to driving revenue generation and partnership opportunities, the role emphasizes building strong departmental processes, managing donor relations technology, streamlining grant administration, and ensuring alignment between development operations and organizational goals development goals of the organization.

Who You Are

  • You're a seasoned mentor, having guided your teams to excellence and ensuring they reach their full potential.
  • Entrepreneurial at heart, you're adept at shaping policies and strategies from the ground up while thriving in dynamic environments.
  • A strategic partnership aficionado, you blend process efficiency with genuine relationship-building, understanding the twin pillars of successful fundraising.
  • Your personal outdoor experiences align with our mission, emphasizing the importance of Black connections with nature and advocating for equitable access.
  • Data-driven, you see the overarching picture, and value analytics just as much as interpersonal connections in driving development success.
  • An operations enthusiast, you're always seeking ways to refine processes and heighten efficiency.
  • Trust is your watchword, and you cherish every relationship – from major donors to volunteers, understanding the intricate value of each.
  • Passionate about technology, you harness donor management tools to streamline operations and extract meaningful insights.
  • An empathetic leader, you motivate with understanding and collaboration, fostering an environment where every voice matters.
  • Adaptable and proactive, you revel in change, always ready to evolve for the organization's betterment.
  • Ever-curious, you're consistently exploring new trends, tools, and strategies in nonprofit operations and fundraising.

Fundraising and External Relationship Development

  • Collaborate closely with the CEO and Executive Director to shape and continuously refine long-term fundraising strategies, ensuring they align with the organization's overarching goals and set the groundwork for sustained funding sources.
  • Dive deep into the nuances of the fundraising process, leveraging data analytics and internal feedback to identify areas for improvement, and ensuring continuous enhancement of departmental operations.
  • Progressively take on a pivotal role in donor relationship management, eventually becoming the primary lead, allowing the organization's Founder to focus on high-level strategic endeavors and broad organizational vision.
  • Foster and nurture existing funder relationships, using advanced donor management tools to ensure consistent, impactful interactions and expanded recurring revenue streams.
  • Draw from data insights within donor relation platforms to discern vital trends, uncover fresh opportunities, and effectively guide and support donor engagements.
  • Oversee grant compliance and reporting, while coordinating with internal team members to ensure that grant utilization aligns seamlessly with available operational resources and organizational goals.
  • Lead the planning and execution of fundraising events, ensuring that event logistics harmoniously integrate with development objectives, while also ensuring that fundraising initiatives benefit from the most effective operational strategies and tools available.

Development Operations

  • Strengthen and optimize the business development department operations, processes, procedures, and infrastructure.
  • Oversee the implementation and management of donor relations software (e.g., Salesforce) to enhance donor engagement and improve data insights.
  • Evaluate and recommend technologies, tools, and platforms that can streamline development and fundraising operations.
  • Develop or refine development policies and procedures to ensure best practices. Create and continually refine fundraising SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the development department.
  • Collaborate with the CEO and senior management on financial planning, budgeting, cash flow, and other operational matters.
  • Coordinate closely with other departments to ensure seamless alignment of strategies and initiatives.

Cross Functional Collaboration & Partnership Management

  • Partner with the program team to integrate fundraising initiatives with organizational programs and events - serving as the primary partner owner for the organization.
  • Manage regular reporting on partner needs, and deliverables; elevate issues to the Executive Team.
  • Serve as the primary Outdoor Afro representative and point of contact for partners, donors and the internal team driving all communications and follow-up items - sharing widely with the team as necessary.
  • Work with other departments to ensure that fundraising strategies are synchronized with organizational capabilities, resources, and timelines.
  • Oversee the day to day operational management of the Outdoor Afro’s partner relationships, ensuring donor and partner retention annually.
  • Develop strong relationships with corporate partner representatives.
  • Apply a customer centric approach to strategically approach partnership goals, ensuring alignment with Outdoor Afro’s mission.
  • Serve as an internal partner representative for the larger Outdoor Afro team to identify partner needs, deliverables and regular communications
  • Escalate potential conflicts of interest or issues to the Outdoor Afro Executive Team in a timely fashion as needed.

Leadership & Strategy

  • Participate in, and plan strategy meetings with the CEO and executive management team regarding exigent communications, partnerships, and large events.
  • Supervise fund development staff and consultants; develop individual goals, provide ongoing feedback, one-on-one meetings and conduct performance assessments
  • Actively participate in and provide leadership for strategic plan implementation in collaboration with the CEO and key staff. Coach staff as they implement strategic initiatives pertaining to fund development and partnership strategies.
  • Maintain continuous lines of communication within the Outdoor Afro HQ staff; identify and implement solutions to key issues; keep the CEO informed of critical issues and identify solutions.
  • Provide organizational leadership, insight, and expertise to the CEO and senior management on financial planning, budgeting, cash flow and other policy matters.
  • Provide leadership to the Board of Directors and relevant committees to communicate critical fund development matters. Write reports, including quarterly reports to the Board of Directors and its various operating committees.

Skills & Experience

  • Bachelor's Degree in a related field such as Nonprofit Management, Business Administration, Marketing, Public Relations, or another relevant area.
  • Master's Degree (Preferred but not mandatory): Advanced degrees like an MBA, Master's in Nonprofit Management, or a related discipline a plus.
  • 8-10 years in fund and/or business development roles, w/ significant portion of time spent in leadership or managerial positions. Candidates with corporate sales, account management and corporate partnership development are encouraged to apply.
  • Demonstrated experience optimizing development department operations, including refining processes, implementing new technologies, and managing donor relations software.
  • Proven track record of successful fundraising, including cultivating and maintaining relationships, securing major gifts, planning fundraising events, and grant writing.
  • Demonstrated experience managing projects and tracking key performance indicators; experience using project management software such as Asana.
  • Advanced skills in the G-Suite and/or MS Office. Experience managing donor relations software (CRM), Salesforce, or similar software is required.

Core Competencies

  • Leadership & Strategic Vision: Guides, inspires, & develops teams to align with departmental and organizational objectives. Envisions short and long-term fundraising goals in harmony with organization's mission.
  • Operational & Data Mastery: Understands how to streamline business processes for efficiency and effectiveness while harnessing insights from donor relations software to inform strategies.
  • Partnership & Relationship Building: Excels in building & maintaining strong ties with diverse stakeholders, from corporate partners to community organizations. Understands nonprofit and corporate dynamics, and bridges communication gaps effectively.
  • Technical Proficiency & Grant Management: Familiar with tools like Salesforce and the intricacies of grant sourcing, application, compliance, and reporting.
  • Budget Oversight & Project Management: Plans & manages budgets for organizational growth and adeptly oversees multiple projects for timely completion.
  • Communication & Collaborative Mindset: Clearly articulates ideas & strategies to all stakeholders and works closely with other departments, aligning fundraising with broader strategies.
  • Problem-Solving & Adaptability: Identifies challenges & devises solutions in evolving environments, and pivots strategies responsively to changes.
  • Ethical Standards & Continuous Learning: Upholds professionalism, ethics, & confidentiality while staying updated on best practices in philanthropy and nonprofit management.

Right now, someone is scrolling through their phone while working out how next year can look different from this one. They have a plan, and the right credit card could be a real step toward it. Whether Mission Lane shows up at that moment, in a way that makes sense for where they are, depends on how well our paid campaigns are built, optimized, and scaled. As our Manager, Paid Acquisition & Investment, you are the trusted expert who runs the campaigns that put us in front of them at the right time, for the right reasons.

In your first year, you will take autonomous ownership of our paid channels, translating high-level strategy into flawless, reliable execution. Campaigns go live perfectly aligned with strategic intent, budgets are managed with precision, and the cost of bringing in each approved customer consistently hits target. Mission Lane is in a stable, exciting phase of growth, making this a great moment to lead the execution of our paid media engine. You’ll do that by:

  • Serving as the Subject Matter Expert (SME) and independently owning campaign execution across Meta, Google, TikTok, and Snapchat, from complex builds through launch and advanced optimization.

  • Driving a rigorous testing roadmap, running sophisticated A/B tests on behalf of the marketing team and translating complex data into actionable, strategic decisions.

You’ll thrive in this role if:

  • You know the platform levers like the back of your hand: You are an expert in bidding strategies, ad formats, audience targeting, and identifying exactly what to adjust when performance shifts.
  • You are a highly trusted operator: You consistently run channels end-to-end, require minimal oversight, and flawlessly execute on overarching marketing strategies.
  • Budget management is second nature: You check pacing and variance as a daily habit, and you have a proven history of managing specific budgets to hit strict CAC targets.
  • Quality acquisition drives you: Acquiring the right customers matters to you just as much as acquiring them efficiently, and you instinctively reach for ROAS or an LTV:CAC view to dictate your optimizations.
  • You launch with uncompromising precision: Setup always matches strategic intent, rigorous QA happens before go-live, and defects are virtually nonexistent.

Mission Lane has cumulatively raised over $600 million of equity from leading investors, including Invus Opportunities, QED Investors, LL Funds, funds affiliated with Oaktree Capital Management, and other leading investors.

· Own P&C actuarial and regulatory reporting, including reserve analyses, actuarial opinions, and supporting memoranda; monitor relevant developments and ensure timely, accurate, compliant, decision-useful reporting.

· Engage Pricing Committees, the CFO, the Chief Risk Officer, and other senior stakeholders through timely, decision-useful portfolio insights, clear performance reporting, actionable recommendations, and effective enterprise partnerships.

· Build and lead an accountable, high-performing actuarial organization with strong capabilities, clear decision rights, technical standards, disciplined analysis, constructive challenge, continuous improvement, integrity, and succession depth.

· Applies deep P&C or specialty insurance expertise across pricing, reserving, reinsurance, in-force performance, loss drivers, and portfolio risk.

· Uses strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills to translate complex actuarial analysis into clear, actionable insights and disciplined decisions.

· Communicates actuarial judgments, uncertainty, and recommendations credibly to executives, governance committees, boards, auditors, regulators, and technical and nontechnical stakeholders.

· Builds trusted, action-oriented partnerships across functions while constructively challenging assumptions and maintaining actuarial independence.

jobs.excerpt: Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO) About the RoleWe are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.
jobs.description:
Position:Chief Financial Officer (CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and commercially strategic Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to lead the financial strategy, financial performance, capital management, investment finance, treasury, reporting, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investment organization.

The CFO will serve as a key member of the executive leadership team and strategic advisor to the CEO/President and Board, providing leadership across financial planning, insurance accounting, capital and solvency management, investment portfolio performance, asset-liability management, treasury, risk, regulatory reporting, and corporate development.

The successful candidate will combine deep financial expertise with strong commercial and investment acumen and will be capable of operating in a highly regulated financial-services environment.

Key Responsibilities

1. Financial Strategy & Executive Leadership

Develop and execute the organization's overall financial strategy.

Advise the CEO, President, and Board on financial performance, capital allocation, investment strategy, and enterprise value creation.

Translate corporate strategy into financial plans, budgets, forecasts, and measurable objectives.

Lead financial decision-making across insurance, investment, and corporate operations.

Establish strong financial governance and accountability across the organization.

2. Financial Planning, Budgeting & Performance

Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-term financial planning.

Develop financial models and scenario analyses to support strategic decisions.

Monitor revenue, profitability, expenses, capital efficiency, and operating performance.

Establish financial KPIs and executive dashboards.

Identify opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and shareholder returns.

3. Insurance Finance & Performance

Oversee financial management of insurance operations, including premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, and underwriting performance.

Monitor key insurance financial metrics including loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting profitability.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk teams to assess financial performance and emerging exposures.

Ensure appropriate financial treatment and reporting of insurance liabilities and reserves.

Support pricing, product profitability, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions from a financial perspective.

4. Investment Finance & Portfolio Management

Provide financial oversight of the organization's investment portfolio and investment activities.

Partner with the CIO/Chief Investment Officer and Investment Committee on portfolio strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, realized/unrealized gains, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted returns.

Evaluate investment opportunities and strategic asset-allocation decisions.

Ensure investment activities are aligned with the organization's liabilities, liquidity requirements, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.

5. Capital, Solvency & Balance Sheet Management

Lead capital planning and balance-sheet optimization.

Monitor solvency, capital adequacy, liquidity, leverage, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize the organization's capital structure and return on capital.

Assess the financial impact of major business, investment, and insurance decisions on capital requirements.

Work closely with Risk and Actuarial functions on capital and solvency assessments.

6. Asset-Liability Management (ALM)

Provide executive financial oversight of asset-liability management.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support development of ALM strategies and balance-sheet optimization initiatives.

Ensure appropriate financial stress testing and scenario analysis.

7. Treasury & Liquidity

Oversee treasury, cash management, liquidity planning, and banking relationships.

Maintain adequate liquidity to meet claims, operating obligations, investment commitments, and strategic requirements.

Optimize cash deployment and short-term investment strategies.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

Establish robust treasury policies and controls.

8. Regulatory & Financial Reporting

Ensure accurate, timely, and transparent financial reporting to the Board, shareholders, regulators, and other stakeholders.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and consolidated financial statements.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Lead relationships with external auditors, regulators, actuarial advisers, tax advisers, and other professional stakeholders.

Maintain strong financial controls and governance frameworks.

9. Risk Management & Financial Controls

Establish effective financial risk-management frameworks.

Monitor exposure to market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, operational, interest-rate, and foreign-exchange risks.

Strengthen internal controls, financial policies, and governance processes.

Work closely with the CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and other executives to manage enterprise-wide financial risks.

Ensure appropriate stress testing and contingency planning.

10. Reinsurance & Capital Optimization

Provide financial oversight of reinsurance strategy and economics.

Evaluate the financial and capital implications of reinsurance arrangements.

Monitor reinsurance recoverables, counterparty exposure, and profitability.

Support optimization of risk transfer, capital efficiency, and balance-sheet resilience.

11. Corporate Development & Strategic Investments

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, strategic investments, joint ventures, and business expansion opportunities.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and investment cases.

Assess potential M&A opportunities and their impact on capital, solvency, earnings, and shareholder value.

Support negotiations with investors, financial institutions, and strategic partners.

12. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, banks, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Communicate financial performance, capital strategy, investment results, and business outlook to key stakeholders.

Support investor presentations, Board materials, and strategic financial communications.

13. Finance Transformation & Technology

Modernize finance systems, reporting infrastructure, ERP platforms, and financial analytics.

Improve automation, data quality, forecasting, and management reporting.

Establish real-time visibility into financial, insurance, investment, and risk performance.

Drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

14. Leadership & Talent Development

Lead Finance, FP&A, Treasury, Accounting, Financial Reporting, Tax, and related functions.

Build a high-performing and commercially focused finance organization.

Develop finance leadership talent and succession plans.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and business partnership.

Key Performance Indicators

The CFO will be accountable for:

Revenue and earnings growth

Operating and net profitability

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Combined ratio / underwriting profitability

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow management

Balance-sheet optimization

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and financial reporting quality

Cost of capital

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant executive leadership.

Previous experience as CFO, Group CFO, Finance Director, VP Finance, Deputy CFO, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, asset management, investment management, banking, pensions, financial services, or a related regulated financial institution.

Strong understanding of insurance financial statements, investment portfolios, capital management, and regulatory requirements.

Proven experience managing complex balance sheets, liquidity, capital, and financial performance.

Strong experience working with Boards, regulators, auditors, investors, rating agencies, and senior executives.

Demonstrated experience in financial strategy, investment analysis, and capital allocation.

Preferred Experience

Experience as Group CFO within a diversified insurance or financial-services group.

Experience across both insurance and investment/asset-management businesses.

Experience with life insurance, general insurance, health insurance, pensions, or reinsurance.

Exposure to institutional investment portfolios and alternative investments.

Experience with M&A, strategic investments, capital raising, restructuring, or corporate transformation.

Experience operating across multiple jurisdictions or regulated markets.

Experience interacting with insurance regulators and rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is an advantage.

Relevant insurance, actuarial, investment, or risk-management qualifications are advantageous.

Core Competencies

Insurance Finance

Corporate Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Risk Management

Regulatory Reporting

Insurance Accounting

M&A & Corporate Development

Capital Allocation

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Financial Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially minded, and financially rigorous

Highly analytical and investment-oriented

Experienced in highly regulated environments

Strong in capital and balance-sheet management

Comfortable engaging with Boards, regulators, investors, and rating agencies

Able to balance growth, profitability, liquidity, capital, and risk

An effective strategic partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, and Chief Actuary

Strong in complex financial decision-making

A transformational finance leader capable of building high-performing teams

Compensation

A competitive executive compensation package comprising base salary, performance-based incentives, executive benefits, and other benefits commensurate with experience and market benchmarks.

Team: Sales / Solution Engineering

Mindset:Own the technical win.

About Nametag

Nametag is a category leader in identity verification, security, and account protection. We sell into security-conscious enterprises with complex environments, and high technical standards. Our Solutions Engineers are trusted technical partners to both customers and Account Executives—and are accountable for proving value, not just explaining it.

We value intellectual curiosity, collaboration, and a strong sense of responsibility in protecting enterprise security.

About the Role

We’re hiring an Enterprise Solutions Engineer to own the technical motion in complex enterprise deal cycles. This role partners directly with Account Executives to drive new business and expansion, assisting with discovery, shaping technical strategy, and running proofs-of-concept that align to the buyer’s security, identity, and implementation criteria.

This is not a demo jockey role. You are responsible for the technical win—from first technical conversation through POC success and into a clean, confident handoff to post-sales. You’ll stay engaged through implementation to ensure what was sold is what gets delivered, on time and against the buyer’s stated objectives.

Responsibilities

  • Partner closely with Account Executives to drive the technical validation for enterprise new business and expansion opportunities.
  • Lead deep technical discovery to understand customer identity architecture, security posture, and success criteria.
  • Own and execute enterprise-grade demos andproof-of-concept, clearly tied to documented success criteria reflecting customer requirements around relevant use cases,, risk factors, and decision criteria.
  • Articulate Nametag’s value in the context of IAM, authentication flows, and account protection—not just product features.
  • Serve as the primary technical adviser during the sales cycle, building trust with security, IT, and identity stakeholders.
  • Define clear technical success criteria and acceptance standards for each deal.
  • Own thehandover to post-sales, ensuring Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, and Technical Customer Engineering teams have full context.
  • Provide continuity and technical oversight during implementation to ensure onboarding stays aligned with what was sold and agreed.
  • Surface product gaps, competitive insights, and recurring objections to Product and Leadership.
  • Support renewals and expansions as necessary by re-engaging on architecture changes, new use cases, integration opportunities, and evolving security requirements.

Tech You’ll Work With

  • Identity and access management platforms: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Auth0, Ping, Duo
  • Authentication and federation standards: SAML, OIDC, OAuth, SSO, MFA
  • Enterprise IT and workflow systems: ServiceNow, custom internal platforms
  • REST APIs, webhooks, and modern SaaS architectures
  • Cloud environments and enterprise security tooling
  • Customer demo, POC, and evaluation environments

Qualifications

Work Authorization (Required): Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without current or future need for visa sponsorship. This is a firm requirement. The technical qualifications below are guidelines.

  • 5+ years experience in Pre-sales Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or Technical Consulting in B2B SaaS.
  • Strong background in IAM, cybersecurity, or enterprise infrastructure.
  • Hands-on experience with SAML SSO, identity federation, and enterprise authentication flows.
  • Proven track record running successful enterprise POCs and technical evaluations.
  • Comfortable engaging with senior technical buyers (Security, IAM, IT Architecture).
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills—able to explain complex systems clearly and credibly.
  • Bonus: Experience supporting post-sale implementations or working closely with Customer Success teams.

Who Will Succeed in This Role If

  • You take personal ownership of the technical win.
  • You think demos should prove outcomes, not just show features.
  • You’re comfortable pushing back when a POC is poorly scoped or misaligned.
  • You care deeply about clean handoffs and long-term customer success.
  • You enjoy complex environments where trust, clarity, and execution matter.

Why Join

You’ll work on high-impact enterprise deals where technical credibility is decisive. You’ll partner closely with Sales, Product, and Customer Success leadership, influence how we sell and onboard at scale, and help define Nametag’s technical reputation in the market.

Culture & Perks

At Nametag, we believe trust starts with how we treat each other. We're a remote-first team that values autonomy, inclusivity, and collaboration, with regular in-person time to stay connected and innovate together.

  • Remote-first: Work from anywhere in the US. Our team spans Seattle, San Francisco, Ann Arbor, Denver, New York City, and beyond.
  • Off-sites: We bring the team together once per quarter for in-person collaboration, often off-site in new places.
  • Flexible schedules: Work in your own time zone; we align key meetings across a shared window.

We Offer

  • Competitive salary at $225,000 OTE with a 77/23 split
  • Meaningful equity ownership
  • Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
  • Flexible paid time off
  • Quarterly team off-sites and travel support
  • New computer hardware and equipment
  • An inclusive environment where your voice has impact and your work drives change
