Head of Performance

Launch With Us | Remote-first (UK), optional London office in Camden | Competitive salary + performance bonus

Most agencies have great operators. We want the person who turns them into a growth engine.

At Launch With Us, we manage £25M+ in annual paid media across Meta, Google and TikTok for founder-led ecom brands in drinks, food, beauty, wellness and pet. We take them from £2–3M in revenue to £8M, £10M and beyond.

Media and creative sit in one team, which is a big part of why Meta ranks us the UK’s number one Independent Meta Agency Group, as part of the wider Soar Group. We’ve grown 120% year on year for two years running, to 20+ operators. Now we’re building the leadership layer for our next stage, and this is its most important seat.

The role

You’ll own client outcomes across every brand we work with, on every channel and in every pod. You’ll report directly to our Founder, and our Paid Social, Paid Search and Creative Strategy Leads will report to you.

You won’t run a portfolio. You’ll set the strategy every portfolio runs on.

Your core job is to build the Launch With Us growth engine. That means taking how our best operators grow brands by instinct and codifying it into a model every pod can run, covering offer, conversion, creative and distribution.

What you’ll own

Client outcomes. You’ll own retention, MRR expansion and the share of clients hitting their growth target across the whole book. You’ll also be executive sponsor for our key founder relationships.

The outcome model. You’ll build the forecasting and target-setting system every account runs on, turn it into an SOP, train the team on it, and help shape what our service delivers as standard.

Creative as a growth lever. You’ll get media and creative planning, testing and reporting as one. With the Creative Strategy Lead, you’ll make creative hit-rate a performance metric.

Leadership. You’ll coach three leads, and through them a team of 15+, into confident department leaders. You’ll own hiring and build the bench beneath them.

Agency growth. You’ll sit on the leadership team, help set commercial objectives, and bring rigour to pitches so the brands we win are brands we can grow.

Requirements

What you’ll bring

  • You’ve taken seven-figure ecom brands to eight figures, with 5+ years in performance or growth on the agency or DTC side.
  • You have deep fluency in testing, scaling, attribution, funnels and CRO across Meta, TikTok and search. You can audit an account in 30 minutes and name the one constraint holding it back.
  • You have real creative strategy experience. You know a great brief when you see one, and you judge creative on commercial potential, not taste.
  • You think in a founder’s P&L, not in platform ROAS: CAC, MER, contribution margin, LTV and payback.
  • You’ve managed managers and written models teams actually follow. You remove steps rather than add them.
  • You have founder-level presence and you’re comfortable with ambiguity.

Bonus points if you’ve worked both agency and brand side, have depth in retention, CRO or offer strategy, and treat AI, Triple Whale and Shopify as second nature.

Benefits

What you’ll get

  • 25 days’ leave plus Christmas Eve, New Years Eve, and your birthday off
  • Up to 30 days a year working abroad
  • Private health insurance after 6 months, life insurance and a healthcare cash plan
  • Company pension
  • Performance bonus, annual pay reviews and a structured progression plan
  • Ongoing training, monthly incentives and our Kudos reward scheme

Our values: Extreme Ownership · Radical Curiosity · Kind Candour · Outcome Obsessed

If you’ve grown seven-figure brands yourself and you get energy from building leaders and systems that outlast you, this is where your impact compounds. Apply now.

Clinical Supervisor - CT - LPC or LCSW


**MUST be credentialed or willing to be credentialed at the following location with the specific license type: LPC or LCSW**


Can supervise fully remote from any location within the state of CT; however, must reside permanently within the state of CT


Thriveworks is currently seeking Licensed Clinicians to provide clinical supervision and telehealth sessions with patients in Connecticut.


A mix of telehealth sessions and face-to-face sessions with patients is available at the following locations:

  • Milford, CT
  • Manchester, CT

About the job

Thriveworks is a mental health care company founded by clinicians in 2008 and still led by them today. With 340+ locations and a nationwide hybrid care model, we serve over 175,000 clients annually through more than 1.7 million sessions, and we're growing. In addition to working directly with clients, we partner with health systems and primary care providers because we believe mental health is inseparable from physical health. As a clinician-led organization, we're built to support the people who do this work with the tools, community, and stability you need to build a career that lasts.


About the Role

We’re hiring licensed clinicians to provide compassionate, evidence-based care to our more than 175,000 clients across the country. You may be a good fit for this role if you’re:


  • Independently licensed and living in Connecticut— LPC or LCSW
  • Consistently available to clients
  • A behavioral health generalist who is open to treating a variety of clients, including couples and children
  • Invested in helping your clients achieve measurable progress
  • Confident working with modern clinical technology, including telehealth and EHR tools
  • A good teammate — we’re building a clinical community and value positive contributors

Key Responsibilities

  • Provision of supervision to a minimum of six (6) resident clinicians. Provision of weekly group supervision. Provision of individual supervision to each resident clinician for every 10 clinical hours. This would equate to a minimum of 7 hours/week for a supervisor, which varies depending on the Resident caseload size.
  • Willing to maintain a clinical caseload of seeing clients with at least 10 hours of availability per week (not a supervision-only position)
  • Willingness to provide documentation oversight
  • Coaching on the professional and clinical development of the resident clinician
  • Completion of weekly documentation as evidence of supervision sessions.
  • Completion of coaching documentation regarding any disciplinary or performance concerns.
  • Collaboration with the Regional Clinical Director regarding any performance issues.

Supervisor Requirements for LPC or LCSW in CT

LPC Requirements:

  • Must be a licensed professional counselor, in good standing, licensed pursuant to chapter 383a

LCSW Requirements:

  • Must be a licensed clinical social worker, in good standing, licensed pursuant to chapter 383b

Supervision Compensation.

  • For Clinical Caseload: Clinician will receive Fee For Service rates with bonus potential (ex. 90837 could be $55.85 to $64.79 depending on caseload)
  • For Supervision: Provider will be compensated at a rate of seventy dollars and sixty-seven ($70.67) per Individual Supervision session. In the event that the 90837-session code compensation is greater than the individual supervision rate, the 90837 rate (vs code) will be used. The provider will receive a code to document their supervision hours and will be required to complete the recording documentation of such supervision.

How We Support You

We handle the administrative work so you can focus on what you do best: providing exceptional care. jobs.excerpt: OverviewThe Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.
jobs.description:
Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries (LMICs). We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, Ebola, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are also investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: www.clintonhealthaccess.org

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

CHAI’s Market Shaping Team Overview

The CHAI Market Shaping Team (MST) is responsible for envisioning, executing, and monitoring market shaping interventions aimed at improving access to health commodities for LMICs. MST shapes markets across the full product continuum, from R&D and regulatory strategy through manufacturing, procurement, country introduction, adoption, and scale-up. Interventions include target product profile development, pooled procurement, demand forecasting, negotiation of access terms, and supply chain optimization. Where a specific barrier requires it, CHAI structures risk-sharing instruments — advance market commitments, volume guarantees, product subsidies, procurement and payment guarantees, and working capital facilities — matched to that barrier and stage of the product lifecycle. Equally, MST works on the demand side to convert improved access terms into uptake, partnering with governments and country teams to build the evidence and policy case for adoption, secure guideline inclusion and financing, plan product introduction and scale-up, and strengthen the workforce, supply chain, and service delivery capacity needed to reach patients. This work also generates the demand signals and volume forecasts that underpin MST’s supply-side negotiations.

MST collaborates closely with internal and external stakeholders to maximize the public health impact of a proposed intervention and ensure alignment with current and future policy goals. MST also works to build stronger relationships with manufacturers and distributors to devise and execute sustainable solutions for improved access to health commodities. Examples of the types of market shaping efforts CHAI has been involved with include the following:

  • New agreement secures historic US$1 price for HIV self-test
  • Global partnership to make available 120M affordable, quality COVID-19 rapid tests for low- and middle-income countries
  • Innovative agreement launches affordable, optimal second-line HIV treatment in LMICs
  • Breakthrough agreement will reduce costs and increase access to diagnostic technology for LMICs
  • New high-quality antiretroviral therapy to be launched in South Africa, Kenya, and over 90 LMICs at reduced price
  • Unitaid, CHAI, and Wits RHI enter into a landmark agreement with Dr. Reddy’s to make HIV prevention tool lenacapavir affordable in LMICs

Position Overview

CHAI’s Market Shaping Team is seeking an Associate to support CHAI’s market shaping strategies across programmatic areas, including supporting two key related projects being led by the MST Women’s and Newborn Health (WNH) and Diagnostics sub-teams:

  • Developing a market access strategy for a portfolio of preeclampsia- and maternal anemia-related commodities to accelerate their validation, affordability, and introduction into antenatal care across LMICs.
  • Developing a market access strategy for a portfolio of artificial intelligence (AI)-supported diagnostics, including AI-enabled point-of-care ultrasound (AI-POCUS) and other tools to transform diagnostic capability in LMICs.

We are seeking a highly motivated, entrepreneurial individual with outstanding analytical capabilities, problem-solving ability and communication skills. The individual must be comfortable synthesizing large amounts of quantitative and qualitative data into thoughtful recommendations. They must also be able to function independently, balance multiple priorities simultaneously, and work effectively across a range of stakeholders in a multicultural environment. CHAI places great value on the following personal qualities: resourcefulness, humility, responsibility, tenacity, independence, energy, and work ethic.

The Associate will report to the project leads for these respective WNH and AI diagnostics projects. Preference is for this role to be based in a CHAI program country, subject to MST, country team leadership approval and ability to obtain work authorization; US-based candidates will also be considered. This role will require up to 25% travel.

Responsibilities

The Associate will support these projects by driving forward the rigorous market analyses required to thoughtfully design and implement strategies to support investment decisions by suppliers, country programs, donors, and other key stakeholders to secure access to these commodities for LMICs. Responsibilities include:

  • Landscaping and analysing suppliers of priority commodities for LMICs — including cultivating relationships with new and existing suppliers and distributors, conducting due diligence, and analysing market share, pricing, timelines for product development and regulatory approvals, manufacturing capacity, and access strategies — to identify opportunities to enhance affordability, availability, and sustainability of essential commodities in LMICs
  • Developing demand forecasts and uptake models for new and existing commodities to inform access pricing strategies and supplier negotiations
  • Executing costing and impact analysis for new models of financing, procurement, and distribution, including all-inclusive pricing, equipment leasing, pooled procurement, and tender optimization
  • Analysing country introduction and scale-up requirements, including cost, budget impact, and financing options, to support government adoption decisions and country readiness planning
  • Preparing presentations, reports, investment cases, and other analyses to inform global policy and increase the evidence base for interventions; presenting findings of analyses to internal and external audiences
  • Collaborating with internal stakeholders — including CHAI country, program, and cross-cutting teams — as well as external partners — including donors, governments, suppliers, and global partners — to support the design and execution of supply- and demand-side interventions
  • Developing market analytic frameworks, tools, and templates and serving as a market analytics resource across MST projects
  • Supporting business development efforts by contributing to proposal writing and donor engagement
  • Maintaining effective relationships with senior-level stakeholders across CHAI and partner organizations
  • Executing other responsibilities as needed by the team

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree and 4+ years of relevant experience in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment (e.g., management consulting, industry, global health, government, or multilateral organizations)
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and quantitative modelling skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare compelling presentations and written reports and present effectively to both internal and external stakeholders, including donors and more senior-level individuals
  • Demonstrated ability to think strategically, handle ambiguity, and work in a fast-paced, multicultural, remote environment
  • Ability to drive forward assigned workstreams effectively (e.g., through thoughtful work planning, priority setting, stakeholder engagement, etc.)
  • Ability to build collaborative relationships with internal and external stakeholders, including more senior-level individuals
  • High level of proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word
  • Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time
  • English language fluency, both written and verbal

Advantages

  • Experience in AI, global health, and/or maternal and newborn health
  • Knowledge of market dynamics in low- and middle-income countries
  • Familiarity with innovative financing mechanisms and public-private partnerships
  • Experience working remotely with decentralized teams
  • Additional language skills

jobs.description:
Our Client, an international e-commerce company with a strong presence in the USA, is looking for a creative and driven Amazon Product Development Manager to help the company launch new, competitive products under its growing brand portfolio. In this role, you'll be responsible for turning niche ideas into differentiated product concepts that stand out on Amazon both visually and functionally.

You'll research existing products in a given niche, identify opportunities for improvement, and develop enhanced product ideas supported by compelling Amazon-ready visuals. Your concepts will be tested in blind focus groups against current best-sellers to determine their potential. This is a high-impact role that blends market research, creative thinking, and visual presentation.

Key Responsibilities:

  • You'll receive product or niche directions from the company, outlining the type of product the company is interested in. Your first task will be to thoroughly research the niche. This includes analyzing current competitors, Amazon listings, product reviews, YouTube content, and using tools like ChatGPT to gather insights and identify opportunities.
  • Using what you've learned, you'll come up with one or more creative ways to improve upon what already exists in the market. This could be through a better design, additional function, improved materials or components, smarter packaging, a new size or color, or any other meaningful improvement. Your goal is to create a product with added value that can compete without raising the cost significantly.
  • Once your idea is ready, you'll create a concept for an Amazon main image that visually showcases the product and its value. This starts with a basic sketch or mockup, which you'll turn into a high-quality image using tools like Photoshop, AI generators, competitor references, or even 3D modeling. You can design it yourself or work with freelancers if needed.
  • After your image is ready, you'll compare it side-by-side with the main images of the top three best-sellers in the same niche to see if your product visually stands out and offers a more appealing choice to customers.
  • Finally, you'll submit the concept and final image(s) to the company. The company will run a blind test with focus groups, comparing your image to the competitors. If your concept scores well, the company knows that is headed in the right direction.
  • You are encouraged to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and collaborate with us throughout the process to deliver the strongest possible product concepts.

Requirements:

  • Experience with Amazon product research, private label development, or FBA.
  • Strong ability to analyze market gaps and customer needs.
  • Creative thinker with a good sense for product trends and differentiation.
  • Proficiency in tools like Photoshop, Canva, or AI design tools.
  • Ability to manage concept creation, either independently or with freelancers.
  • Comfort with reviewing and comparing Amazon listings and images.
  • Experience with 3D modeling or product packaging design would be a plus.

What We Offer:

  • Remote work and flexible hours.
  • Competitive and timely salary.
  • Opportunity to lead the early-stage development of new Amazon products.
  • Creative freedom and ownership over product concept development.
  • Ability to work with a small, agile team that values innovation.
  • Make a visible impact - your ideas directly influence what we launch.

You work closely with the analytics team: you don’t have to build the data models yourself, but you must read them, spot what is wrong and say what to change. AI at BambooHR

jobs.title: Manager, Performance Marketing
jobs.excerpt: About Eleanor Health Eleanor Health is rethinking addiction by treating it as a chronic condition and building an integrated care model that expands access to effective, whole-person treatment to drive sustained recovery.
jobs.description:
About Eleanor Health

Eleanor Health is rethinking addiction by treating it as a chronic condition and building an integrated care model that expands access to effective, whole-person treatment to drive sustained recovery. Our goal is to improve upon earlier generations of opioid and substance use disorder treatment to create more accessible clinic- and community-based care.

Eleanor Health and its associated health care providers deliver best-in-class substance use disorder care utilizing Medication-Assisted Therapy (MAT), behavioral health therapy, care management, and social support and wrap services. As a multi-site, outpatient treatment organization, Eleanor delivers accessible, evidence-based, and excellent clinical care, supported by innovative technology.

If you are passionate about growing your career in a business that makes a difference, we seek highly skilled, motivated, and compassionate individuals who take responsibility and adapt quickly to change to join our deeply committed and collaborative team.

About the Role

Every month, thousands of people decide they are ready to do something about their substance use. They search, they scroll, they stream, they click, they call, they fill out a form. This role exists to make sure that as many of them as possible find us in more places than a search results page, and that it costs less to reach them each quarter.

This is a paid media role, and it is not a paid search role. Google Ads and Microsoft Ads are our largest channels today, and a dedicated specialist runs them day to day. This role exists to build and scale everything around that foundation: affiliate, programmatic and streaming audio, Meta, and Reddit. We are hiring for depth in those channels, along with the website experimentation that turns more traffic into more members.

Where we are

We have built a real foundation over the past two years. Paid cost per new member has been reduced by more than half. Conversion tracking is clean and includes offline conversion data, so campaigns optimize toward people who actually enter care rather than toward form fills. Campaign structure has been rebuilt, landing page experience has improved substantially, and bid strategy and targeting have moved from manual management to value-based approaches.

This is a performance marketing function with good bones, clear measurement, and meaningful results already behind it.

Where we are going

Three priorities define the next phase of the work.

  • First — Paid channel diversification. Paid search carries too much of the load today. We need to build and prove affiliate, programmatic and streaming audio, Meta, and Reddit, and to test others worth testing, so growth does not depend on a single auction that gets more expensive as we scale. Each new channel earns its budget by proving member-level economics, not lead volume.
  • Second — Testing rigor. Our experimentation program is young, and there is substantial gain available from running it properly: structured A/B testing on landing pages and creative, and disciplined testing of newer bid strategies and campaign types, including AI Max.
  • Third — Website conversion. The website is the front door for every channel. Landing pages, forms, and the online self-scheduling experience decide how much of the traffic we buy turns into a lead, and every point of lift improves every channel at once.

The channels

The channels in scope are Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, affiliate, programmatic and streaming audio, and Meta and Reddit. A paid search specialist runs the day-to-day on Google and Microsoft. This role leads the rest, builds the strategy across all five, and decides where each dollar goes.

How the funnel is shared

Marketing does not own the entire path on its own. This role owns the path from first impression to a submitted lead or call: the channels, the landing pages, the forms, and the online self-scheduling experience. From there, our Access team is the first human point of contact for every prospective member who reaches out, by phone, by web form, or through online self-scheduling. They handle insurance verification, appointment scheduling, pre-visit support, and follow-up when someone misses an appointment. The Access team reports separately to the Chief Marketing Officer, alongside this role rather than within it.

The lifecycle communications that carry a prospective member from inquiry to first visit, including confirmations, reminders, pre-visit content, and no-show recovery, are owned by the Organic & AI Acquisition team, which also owns the content behind them. This role partners with that team and with Access, because paid cost per new member depends on what happens after the lead. A standing intake funnel review brings all three together.

What this role is accountable for

The primary measure is paid cost per new member, and it is deliberately end-to-end: spend divided by members who complete a first visit, not by leads generated. It does not improve by producing more form fills. It improves when more of the people we reach actually enter care.

Alongside it sit website-visitor-to-lead conversion, owned outright by this role, and the mix of paid acquisition itself: the share of members coming from channels beyond paid search, and each new channel's cost against a defined target before it earns more budget. Lead-to-member conversion is owned by Access and the lifecycle function, and blended cost per acquisition across all channels, paid and non-paid together, sits with the Chief Marketing Officer.

What You'll Do

Paid Media Strategy & Performance

  • Own paid cost per new member as a quarterly target, understanding that monthly variance in this category is largely seasonal rather than performance-driven
  • Own budget pacing and allocation across all five channels, shifting investment toward what is working
  • Lead paid channel diversification: build, test, and scale affiliate, programmatic and streaming audio, Meta, and Reddit, with a defined budget, success criteria, and scale-or-stop decision for each
  • Be hands-on in the newer channels: build campaigns, manage partners and platforms, and optimize against member-level outcomes rather than platform-reported leads
  • Manage programmatic and streaming audio partners as an informed client, including planning, creative requirements, measurement, and incrementality
  • Direct the paid search specialist on Google and Microsoft: set priorities, review work, and stay close enough to the accounts to audit the work independently
  • Design and run structured tests of newer bid strategies and campaign types, including AI Max, with clear success criteria defined before launch
  • Plan for seasonality: demand and cost per click vary substantially by month in addiction treatment, and the annual plan should reflect that rather than assume a flat target
  • Maintain offline conversion tracking and value-based bidding wherever a channel supports it, so campaigns optimize toward members rather than leads
  • Ensure all paid activity meets LegitScript certification and platform policy requirements for addiction treatment advertising. Meta, Reddit, and programmatic partners each apply their own restrictions

Affiliate & Partner Channels

  • Build and manage the affiliate program: recruit and vet partners, set terms, track quality, and cut what does not produce members
  • Structure affiliate and partner compensation in partnership with Legal and Compliance, including EKRA and Anti-Kickback requirements
  • Hold every partner to member-level quality rather than lead volume, and to our advertising and privacy standards

Website Conversion & Experimentation

  • Own website-visitor-to-lead conversion as a primary accountability
  • Build and run a disciplined experimentation program: written hypotheses, pre-declared success measures, and documented readouts including the tests that lose
  • Prioritize the test roadmap by expected impact rather than by ease or preference
  • Own the online self-scheduling experience and the forms that lead into it
  • Partner with the content specialist and design partners on landing page builds and publishing
  • Partner with the Organic & AI Acquisition team on page changes that affect both conversion and discoverability

Funnel Performance & Measurement

  • Maintain a view of the funnel from first impression to submitted lead, and know at all times which step is weakest
  • Establish and maintain a conversion baseline for every step, with methodology agreed with our data and analytics consultant
  • Report cost per new member and member quality by channel, including channels where tracking is imperfect, and use incrementality tests where attribution alone cannot answer the question
  • Participate in the standing intake funnel review with Access and the lifecycle owner, bringing the paid and website perspective
  • Maintain clean attribution between paid and non-paid sources
  • Report performance monthly against target, and explain variance without being asked

Team & Vendor Management

  • Direct the paid search and paid media specialists: set expectations in writing, hold a consistent feedback cadence, and develop them deliberately
  • Manage affiliate networks, programmatic and audio partners, and other channel vendors as an informed client
  • Maintain a current quarterly plan for the function showing priorities, expected impact, owners, and timelines

You'll Be a Good Fit If You:

  • Are equally comfortable setting strategy and doing the work. This is a small team, and everyone on it executes
  • Have built a channel from zero: launched it, measured it honestly, and either scaled it or shut it down
  • Get genuinely excited by a half-point conversion lift, because you know what it compounds to across every channel
  • Think in terms of members rather than leads, and have turned down a cheap-lead tactic because you knew what happened downstream
  • Are comfortable where attribution is messy, as in affiliate, audio, and programmatic, and still hold every channel to member-level economics
  • Are curious about channels you have not run yet, and rigorous about how you test them
  • Work well inside a shared accountability, where the number depends on teams you do not manage and the only way through is a real working relationship
  • Are rigorous about testing: the hypothesis comes first, and the losses get reported
  • Find the constraints of regulated healthcare marketing energizing rather than frustrating
  • Can say what your team is not doing this quarter, and why
  • Approach the work with compassion, knowing that a faster, clearer path to care is sometimes the difference between someone entering treatment and giving up

Skills and Competencies:

  • Experience — roughly 5+ years in performance or acquisition marketing, with at least two managing a substantial paid media budget
  • Channel expertise — hands-on expertise in at least three of the five channels we run: Google Ads, Microsoft Ads, affiliate, programmatic and streaming audio, and Meta and Reddit. Real depth in at least one of affiliate, programmatic and streaming audio, Meta, or Reddit, and ideally two, is essential. Paid search is covered by a specialist, so strong search skills alone are not what we are hiring for
  • Channel building — a record of launching a paid channel from zero and scaling it on member-level or customer-level economics rather than platform-reported conversions
  • Paid search literacy — enough working knowledge of Google and Microsoft Ads to direct and audit a specialist
  • Conversion optimization — demonstrated experience running a structured experimentation program, not just making site changes
  • Measurement — comfort building and defending your own reporting, measuring to the end of the funnel rather than to the lead, and handling imperfect attribution in affiliate, audio, and programmatic. Familiarity with incrementality testing
  • Management — experience directing specialists, contractors, or vendors. Experience managing at least one direct report is a plus
  • Judgment — sound decision-making in a space with hard compliance constraints around patient privacy, partner compensation, and advertising policy
  • Operating rigor — can prioritize under constraint and hold a plan while conditions change

Helpful but not required:

  • Healthcare, behavioral health, or other regulated-category marketing experience
  • LegitScript certification experience or familiarity with addiction treatment advertising policy
  • Experience running an affiliate program on a network or platform
  • Experience with a customer data platform or call tracking tooling
  • Experience working alongside a contact center or intake team on shared conversion targets
  • Multi-state or multi-market experience

What This Role Is Not:

We would rather be clear now than waste your time.

  • Not a paid search role. Google and Microsoft Ads are our largest channels today, and a specialist runs them. This role is hired to build the channels around them.
  • Not an organic, content, or brand role. Organic search, AI visibility, reputation, and brand sit with a peer function.
  • Not a lifecycle or CRM role. Lifecycle marketing and intake conversion sit with the Organic & AI Acquisition team, which owns the content behind them.
  • Not a purely strategic seat. There is real hands-on work here, and someone looking to direct rather than build would not enjoy it.
  • Not a role where you can hand the thinking to an agency. Partners and vendors execute; this role sets direction and owns the result.

Compensation & Benefits

The target compensation range for this position is $105,000-115,000. The actual compensation offered depends on a variety of factors, which may include, as applicable, the applicant’s qualifications for the position; years of relevant experience; specific and unique skills; level of education attained; certifications or other professional licenses held; other legitimate, non-discriminatory business factors specific to the position; and the geographic location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will perform the job.

Eleanor Health offers a generous benefits package to full-time employees, which includes:

  • Generous Paid Time Off (prorated for new employees) - unplug, relax, and recharge!
    • 12 Vacation days
    • 12 Wellness (Sick) days
    • 3 Floating holidays
    • 9 Company-observed holidays
    • Jury Duty, Voting Leave, and other forms of paid time off may be available
  • Eleanor-paid medical and dental insurance plans, with affordable vision coverage -We are a health first company, and we strive to make our plans affordable and accessible.
  • 401(k) plan with 3% match - We are excited to be able to support the long-term financial well-being of our team in a way that reinforces Eleanor’s commitment to equity.
  • Short-term disability - We understand that things happen, we want you to feel comfortable to take time to get better.
  • Long Term Disability - Picks up where Short Term Disability leaves off (employee paid).
  • Life Insurance - Both Eleanor and employee-paid options are available.
  • Family Medical Leave -Eleanor Health’s Paid Family & Medical Leave (“PFML”) is designed to provide flexibility and financial peace of mind for approved family and medical reasons such as the birth, adoption, or fostering of a child, and for serious health conditions that you or a family member/significant other might be facing.
  • Wellness Perks & Benefits -Mental Health is important to us and we want our employees to have the accessibility you deserve to talk things through, zen with a mindfulness app, or seek assistance from health advocates
    • Mindfulness App Reimbursement
    • EAP with eight face-to-face sessions
    • Virtual health and wellness visits covered by our medical plan.

Join the VRChat Team

VRChat offers a first-of-its-kind, game-changing platform that provides an endless collection of social VR experiences and gives the power of creation to its robust community. With over 250,000 worlds and growing, VRChat’s vision is to allow users to bring their imaginations to life and help shape the metaverse anywhere in the world on any device. VRChat has raised $100M to date with the support of investors, Makers Fund, Anthos Capital and HTC.

We have a great team which includes people from: Netflix, Twitter, Meta, Microsoft, Roblox, Google, Amazon, Unity, Spotify, Discord, Uber, eBay, Robinhood, Twitch, Zynga and TikTok. Come and join the mission!

Job Overview

    Help VRChat build and sustain a small, exceptionally strong team. You'll lead a focused People function and work directly with leaders and managers to turn clear expectations into effective performance, development, and accountability practices. This is a hands-on leadership role: you'll build on existing infrastructure and partner closely with the recruiting lead.

    We’re looking for a builder who combines strategic judgment with practical delivery, moves comfortably between strategy and hands-on work, and builds only the process the business needs. If you’re energized by leading high-impact environments and care deeply about building inclusive, community-aligned cultures, this role was built for you.

Job & Team Impact

    As Head of People, you’ll shape how VRChat attracts, develops, and retains the talent that makes our mission possible. You’ll be a trusted partner to the CEO and business leaders, a coach to managers, and a champion for the people and culture that make VRChat distinct.

Duties & Responsibilities

  • Partner with senior leaders to strengthen leadership alignment, decision-making, and accountability. Challenge constructively, clarify decision rights, and move decisively once alignment is reached

  • Translate People priorities into practical deliverables with clear owners, milestones, and proactive communication of risks and trade-offs

  • Lead and develop the People team with clear priorities, support, and tools. Model calm, respectful leadership under pressure and handle sensitive matters with discretion, impartiality, and evidence-based judgment

  • Build trust in People as an approachable, reliable partner to employees and managers, with dependable core operations and onboarding

  • Run a practical performance-calibration and manager-accountability process that helps leaders recognize strong performance, identify gaps, support development, and address persistent underperformance promptly and fairly. Leaders own performance decisions; People equips, coaches, and challenges them

  • Coach managers through difficult feedback, employee relations issues, and organizational changes, balancing clear business expectations with fairness, sound judgment, and employee dignity

  • Use engagement, attrition, and performance insights to surface emerging organizational risks and capability gaps proactively, with practical recommendations and clear decisions for leadership

  • Lead the development and operation of leveling and compensation practices, including equity philosophy and communication to candidates and employees, in partnership with executive leadership and Finance

  • Use automation and AI where they demonstrably improve People operations, reduce manual work, or improve employee experience, with appropriate safeguards for sensitive employee data and human judgment

  • Partner closely with the recruiting lead on workforce planning, quality of hire, leveling, and candidate experience. Own the ongoing onboarding and employee lifecycle, using recruiting-to-ramp feedback to improve handoffs

  • Sustain and evolve VRChat's inclusive, remote-first culture across a globally distributed and diverse workforce

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own the experience for your product as well as its roadmap and competitive positioning, and you will collaborate with company leadership on setting your product's goals. You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.

Product Managers are the bridge that connects R&D to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

The role

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you'll own the Grafana Labs offerings that run outside our standard multi-tenant SaaS. That includes Grafana Federal Cloud, for organizations that need FedRAMP-authorized observability: US federal agencies; state, local, and education (SLED) customers; and commercial companies that sell FedRAMP offerings of their own. It also includes Grafana Cloud Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC), which delivers the full Grafana Cloud experience while the customer pays the infrastructure bill directly to their cloud provider, saving them significantly at scale.

Your mission is to make Grafana Labs the obvious choice for organizations that can't use standard SaaS because of compliance, data, or cost-at-scale constraints. Deployment choices change the product: features that are simple in standard SaaS can be hard, expensive, or impossible in a regulated or customer-owned environment. You’ll be responsible for adapting existing Grafana Cloud capabilities to these environments, deciding which features come in, which wait, and which stay out, and occasionally building something specific to BYOC or Federal Cloud. You'll also help shape which deployment models we offer next.

Along the way, you’ll use AI tools daily to speed up research, analyze product signals, and develop positioning, applying strong judgment to the results.

As the Staff Product Manager for Enterprise Deployment Solutions, you will:

jobs.description:
As the Product Manager for the Roadmap Track, you will own the long-term features, core game loops, and retention systems that keep Sunshine Island, our flagship casual farming title, growing.

Our product team operates in two specialized execution tracks: Strategic Roadmap (deep features, long-term systems) and LiveOps (recurring events, monetization, D2C growth). You will lead the Roadmap Track in a close PM/PJM pair, partnering directly with a dedicated Project Manager (PJM) who manages day-to-day agile mechanics and operational scheduling. This structure frees you to focus on product direction, new mechanics, and the impact of what we build. You work with a complete feature team of dedicated engineers, designers, economy designers, artists, and data analysts, bringing new mechanics to a mature game.

This position is ideal for a data-driven Product Manager who thinks in roadmaps, stays close to the market to see what works, comes up with their own ideas for new mechanics, and wants to have a measurable impact on retention and long-term revenue.

YOUR MISSION

  • Roadmap & Feature Ownership: Own the Roadmap Track backlog and quarterly plan. Keep existing features and systems healthy (progression, content updates, guilds, tournaments) while prioritizing and sequencing larger releases that move our KPIs.

  • New Mechanics & Market Insight: Stay close to the market: play and analyze games in the genre, see what works, and come up with your own ideas for new mechanics that make the game better in its genre. Game designers own the detailed feature design, and you bring the ideas, the evidence, and the KPI goals.

  • Retention & Early Game: Own first-session and early-game retention (FTUE, unlock pacing, onboarding) and the path from new player to veteran, working with analysts on cohorts and A/B tests.

  • Progression & Content: Shape progression and content cadence with economy designers (content waves, level cap, progression speed), so players keep finding new things to do from the first session to veteran play.

  • KPI Ownership & Testing: Own the roadmap KPIs: D7 and early retention, veteran DAU and ARPDAU of high-level players, and progression speed. Define success metrics up front and read A/B tests and cohorts together with the data analysts.

  • Delivery & Collaboration: Partner with your track PJM on sprint scoping and release scheduling and act as the central product anchor for the feature team. Drive multi-phase features from goal to release, with clear scope and learnings per phase. You report to the Director of LiveOps and work day to day with the game's Product Owner.

YOUR PROFILE

  • 4–6 years as a Product Manager or Game PM in mobile F2P gaming (casual, farming, simulation, or city-builder experience preferred).

  • Proven Live Game Experience: Demonstrated experience running a live game and thinking in roadmaps: prioritizing, sequencing, and delivering large features, and weighing trade-offs between them.

  • Market-Informed Mindset: Plays and analyzes games in the genre, has a strong pulse on what works, and turns it into ideas for new mechanics. Comfortable with retention and monetization metrics (D7, ARPDAU, LTV, churn).

  • Player & Systems Understanding: Understanding of what keeps players engaged over time: progression, onboarding, long-term retention systems, and how economy and content pacing work together.

  • Cross-Functional Communicator: Skilled at aligning and inspiring cross-functional teams (Art, Tech, Design, Analytics) through clear commercial reasoning without needing direct line management.

  • Agile & Operationally Minded: Highly organized, calm under live operational pressure, and accustomed to working alongside PJMs in SCRUM/Kanban frameworks.

  • Time Zone: Located within +/- 3 hours of CEST for real-time collaboration in our remote-first setup.

  • AI-Savvy or Curious: Comfortable using AI tools in your daily work, or keen to learn. We use AI across production and expect you to try it.

WHAT WE OFFER

  • Direct ownership of the product direction and long-term growth of a high-scale mobile title generating millions in revenue.

  • A complete feature team and a close partnership with a dedicated PJM, who handles operational overhead so that you stay focused on product strategy and impact.

  • A mature, remote-first studio culture that values autonomy, data-driven decisions, and sustainable execution.

  • A competitive compensation package, personal development budget, and flexible working conditions.

Job Summary

At Fuze Health, we put patients first and tirelessly address the most pressing needs in healthcare. We empower millions to digitally connect with care providers, essential health resources and needed treatments – and enable care providers, employers, health plans and life sciences companies to meaningfully enhance quality, outcomes and value. Together, we have the shared vision, advanced capabilities and talented teams to deliver next-generation solutions that patients and healthcare partners need today and into the future.



Job Description

The Senior Manager, Pharmacy Operations at FuzeRx is a senior operational leadership role responsible for driving operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and performance across multiple pharmacy fulfillment sites within a designated region of the US. This role sits within the Pharmacy Operations job family and is accountable for translating company strategy into scalable, high-performing regional operations while developing strong site-level leadership.


As a Senior Manager, Pharmacy Operations, you will lead and develop a team of Pharmacy Fulfillment Managers, partnering closely with Pharmacy Operations, Clinical, Talent Acquisition, HR, Logistics, and other cross-functional leaders to optimize performance across the fulfillment network. This role requires strategic thinking, strong operational judgment, and the ability to drive measurable improvements in patient experience, safety, quality, cost, and delivery performance while maintaining rigorous compliance in a highly regulated environment. You will play a critical role in scaling operations, implementing company-wide initiatives, and building the processes, tools, and leadership capabilities needed to support sustainable growth.


Key Responsibilities:


  • Lead regional operational strategy, execution, and performance across multiple pharmacy fulfillment sites, ensuring alignment with company objectives and broader operational priorities
  • Drive regulatory compliance and operational readiness in accordance with applicable federal and state pharmacy regulations, payer requirements, and internal quality standards
  • Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of Pharmacy Fulfillment Managers, building leadership capabilities, establishing performance expectations, and supporting succession planning
  • Establish and scale standardized processes, tools, and resources that improve site-level execution, operational consistency, and long-term performance
  • Define, monitor, and improve key operational metrics across safety, quality, cost, productivity, and delivery timeliness, fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement
  • Apply Lean, Kaizen, and other process improvement methodologies to identify inefficiencies, eliminate waste, and optimize end-to-end pharmacy fulfillment workflows

  • Serve as a senior escalation point for significant site-level operational events, leading issue resolution, risk mitigation, and recovery efforts to maintain safe, reliable, and uninterrupted service
  • Establish and oversee audit, quality assurance, and compliance review processes to maintain inspection readiness and uphold regulatory and operational standards
  • Lead the regional implementation of corporate initiatives, ensuring site readiness, stakeholder alignment, effective change management, and consistent execution
  • Support new site launches, operational transitions, expansions, and restructuring initiatives to enable scalable growth and maintain continuity of pharmacy services

Required Experience & Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, Pharmacy Operations, Supply Chain, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in fulfillment, healthcare, pharmacy, or operations leadership, including responsibility for multi-site operations
  • Demonstrated success leading high-volume fulfillment operations, healthcare services, or pharmacy operations in a performance-driven environment
  • Experience managing teams in highly regulated, compliance-driven environments, with a strong understanding of operational controls, quality standards, and risk management
  • Proven track record of developing leaders, managing diverse teams, and driving accountability and performance across multiple sites
  • Strong analytical and financial acumen, including experience using operational data, financial metrics, and P&L insights to guide decision-making and improve business performance
  • Proficiency with analytical and reporting tools such as Excel, Tableau, Looker, or similar platforms
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, influence stakeholders at multiple levels, and translate strategic priorities into effective operational execution
  • Strong problem-solving, communication, and change-management skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and resolve complex operational challenges
  • Experience implementing process improvements that enhance efficiency, quality, compliance, and service delivery in a dynamic operating environment

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Master’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Healthcare Leadership, or a related field
  • 3+ years of regional or multi-site pharmacy leadership experience
  • Lean Six Sigma, APICS, or other relevant operations, supply chain, or quality certifications
  • Deep knowledge of pharmacy fulfillment workflows, inventory management, courier logistics, and end-to-end pharmacy operations
  • Experience scaling operations in high-growth environments, including site launches, organizational transitions, or network expansion
  • Demonstrated success leading continuous improvement initiatives using Lean, Kaizen, or other operational excellence methodologies
  • Experience partnering across Pharmacy Operations, Clinical, Logistics, Recruiting, HR, and other business functions to deliver measurable operational outcomes
  • Experience developing standardized operating models, performance management frameworks, and scalable processes across distributed teams



Additional Information

Physical requirements for this role include the ability to work at a computer terminal with monitor, keyboard and mouse for extended periods of time, stoop, bend, and reach for equipment and supplies, make frequent repetitive motions required to operate a computer that include the wrists, hands and fingers, and lift, carry, push, pull, and move light objects up to 20 pounds. The role also requires the ability to effectively communicate through verbal interactions, discern auditory information, and visually perceive details to perform essential job functions.


This position requires occasional travel therefore you must be able to sit for extended periods of time on airplanes and/or in vehicles, lift and carry luggage independently, navigate long distances through airports and other travel locations independently, and adjust to different time zones and climates.

The Clinical Systems and Informatics (CSI) team is a Trillium Health Partners (THP) Program that successfully implemented Epic as the hospital’s integrated Hospital Information System (HIS) in October 2020. The CSI team is within the Quality, Risk, and Practice Division and focuses on bridging the gap between technology and process through a Quintuple AIM framework with a focus on system, user, and patient-based outcomes, within the resources available.

Reporting to the Manager, Projects and Partnerships, this position plays an integral role in the development, implementation and adoption of health care information technologies amongst clinicians across Trillium Health Partners (THP). Job Description | Head of Risk, Audit & Compliance

1. Position Details

Position

﻿

Head of Risk, Audit and Compliance

Department

﻿

Risk, Audit and Compliance

Job Level

﻿

Head of Department (HOD)

Reporting To

﻿

Board of Directors or Managing Director, as determined by the Company's governance structure

Direct Reports

﻿

Risk, Internal Audit and Compliance personnel, as determined by the approved organisational structure

Geographical Scope

﻿

Company-wide - Head Office and all branches

Employment Type

﻿

Full-time

2. Role Overview

The Company is seeking a strategic, analytical, and execution-oriented Head of Risk, Audit & Compliance to strengthen enterprise-wide risk management, internal audit, regulatory compliance, and governance across the organisation.

The role holder will provide leadership in identifying and managing material business risks, independently assessing the effectiveness of internal controls, monitoring compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, and providing assurance to Management and the Board on the Company's governance and control environment.

The position will cover all business functions, departments, systems, and branches, including operational, financial, strategic, regulatory, technology, fraud, reputational, and other enterprise risks. It is not limited to credit risk, credit assessment, loan approvals, or credit compliance.

A key priority will be to establish a proactive and disciplined control environment in which risks are identified early, accountability is clearly assigned, audit findings are addressed within agreed timelines, and compliance obligations are consistently met.

The successful candidate will work closely with the Managing Director, HODs, branch management, and other stakeholders to strengthen business controls while maintaining the independence required to provide objective assurance. The role holder will also engage the Board or its designated committee on material risks, significant audit findings, regulatory breaches, and unresolved control weaknesses.

This is a high-impact HOD role requiring strong professional judgement, integrity, analytical capability, and the ability to translate risk, audit, and compliance findings into practical actions that protect the Company's assets, reputation, regulatory standing, and long-term sustainability.

3. Key Roles & Responsibilities

A. Enterprise Risk Management

  • Develop, implement, and maintain the Company's enterprise risk management framework, policies, procedures, and risk assessment methodologies.

  • Identify, assess, and monitor strategic, operational, financial, regulatory, legal, fraud, reputational, technology, cybersecurity, data privacy, business continuity, and third-party risks across Head Office and all branches.

  • Maintain a comprehensive enterprise risk register, ensuring material risks have defined owners, assessments, mitigation plans, monitoring mechanisms, and escalation thresholds.

  • Establish risk appetite measures, key risk indicators, risk-rating criteria, and escalation protocols for approval through the appropriate governance channels.

  • Conduct periodic enterprise-wide risk assessments and risk and control self-assessments to identify material exposures, control gaps, and emerging risks.

  • Monitor changes in the business environment, products, processes, systems, regulatory requirements, and operating model that may introduce new or increased risks.

  • Advise Management on the risk implications of significant business decisions, strategic initiatives, new products, material contracts, and operational changes.

  • Monitor risk mitigation plans and hold business owners accountable to agreed actions and deadlines.

  • Coordinate business continuity and disaster recovery risk assessments with the relevant functional owners.

  • Develop risk dashboards and management reports highlighting material exposures, emerging trends, overdue mitigations, and matters requiring escalation.

  • Promote risk ownership across the organisation, ensuring that HODs and branch managers remain accountable for risks arising within their respective areas.

  • Provide practical recommendations that strengthen controls without creating unnecessary operational bottlenecks or compromising customer service.

B. Internal Audit and Independent Assurance

  • Develop and maintain a risk-based internal audit plan covering the Company's material business functions, processes, systems, and branches.

  • Submit the annual internal audit plan and material changes to the appropriate Board or designated committee for approval, in line with the Company's governance arrangements.

  • Conduct or oversee independent audits, operational reviews, and control assessments to evaluate the effectiveness of governance, risk management, and internal controls.

  • Execute scheduled and surprise audits of branches, Head Office departments, business processes, financial transactions, records, and systems, based on approved audit priorities.

  • Review the adequacy of controls over procurement, expenditure, payroll, assets, reconciliations, approvals, records management, system access, and other material business processes.

  • Assess adherence to approved policies, delegated authorities, operational procedures, contractual obligations, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

  • Evaluate the reliability, completeness, and integrity of financial and operational records, management reports, and supporting documentation.

  • Assess the effectiveness of controls designed to prevent or detect fraud, unauthorised transactions, conflicts of interest, misuse of Company resources, and other irregularities.

  • Prepare objective, evidence-based audit reports setting out findings, risk implications, root causes, recommendations, responsible action owners, and agreed timelines.

  • Classify findings according to approved risk-rating criteria and promptly escalate critical findings to the appropriate Management or Board forum.

  • Maintain an audit findings tracker and independently verify that corrective actions have been implemented and are operating effectively.

  • Monitor recurring findings, overdue actions, and unresolved material weaknesses, escalating persistent non-compliance to the appropriate governance level.

  • Maintain adequate audit working papers, evidence, and documentation in accordance with applicable professional standards and Company requirements.

  • Protect the independence and objectivity of Internal Audit, ensuring that the function does not audit its own work or assume operational responsibility for the controls it assesses.

C. Regulatory Compliance and Corporate Governance

  • Establish and maintain a company-wide compliance framework covering applicable legal, statutory, regulatory, licensing, and internal policy obligations.

  • Maintain a compliance obligations register and regulatory calendar, with clear accountability for submissions, renewals, reporting deadlines, and other required deliverables.

  • Monitor applicable local laws, regulations, regulatory guidance, and licence conditions relevant to the Company's business and regulatory status.

  • Coordinate compliance assessments across Head Office and branches and monitor the implementation of required controls.

  • Advise Management and relevant functional leaders on regulatory changes, compliance risks, and required corrective actions.

  • Oversee compliance monitoring relating to applicable data protection, customer protection, anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing, anti-bribery and corruption, record retention, and other relevant obligations.

  • Coordinate regulatory inspections, reviews, information requests, and submissions, working with the relevant internal functions and professional advisers as necessary.

  • Maintain records of regulatory correspondence, findings, commitments, remediation plans, and supporting evidence.

  • Review Company policies, procedures, and internal governance standards periodically to identify gaps, inconsistencies, or outdated requirements.

  • Monitor adherence to the Company's Code of Conduct, conflict-of-interest requirements, whistleblowing arrangements, and other applicable governance standards.

  • Promote employee and management awareness of relevant compliance obligations through appropriate communication and training initiatives.

  • Escalate actual or potential material regulatory breaches promptly through the approved reporting channels.

  • Monitor the closure of compliance gaps and validate that corrective actions address the underlying causes.

D. Fraud Prevention, Investigations and Incident Management

  • Establish and maintain appropriate arrangements for identifying, reporting, assessing, and responding to suspected fraud, theft, corruption, misconduct, and material control breaches.

  • Coordinate or oversee investigations into reported irregularities in accordance with approved investigation procedures and appropriate independence requirements.

  • Ensure investigations are conducted objectively, confidentially, and on the basis of verifiable evidence.

  • Coordinate the preservation and review of relevant documents, transaction records, system logs, access records, and other evidence.

  • Prepare investigation reports setting out verified facts, findings, potential exposure, root causes, control weaknesses, and recommended actions.

  • Escalate material incidents and suspected misconduct promptly to the appropriate Management or Board authority.

  • Work with Human Resources, Legal, Finance, IT, and relevant business leaders where investigations require cross-functional support.

  • Maintain a central register of incidents, investigations, outcomes, recoveries, and preventive or corrective actions.

  • Identify recurring incident patterns and recommend improvements to processes, supervision, access controls, approvals, and employee awareness.

  • Monitor implementation of agreed preventive measures and assess whether they reduce the likelihood of recurrence.

  • Ensure investigations support fair and evidence-based decision-making without prejudging disciplinary, employment, legal, or other outcomes reserved for authorised decision-makers.

E. Internal Controls, Operational Assurance and Business Process Improvement

  • Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls across all material business functions and branches.

  • Review segregation of duties, maker-checker arrangements, approval limits, reconciliations, access rights, exception handling, and supervisory controls.

  • Assess whether approved policies, procedures, and delegated authorities are consistently implemented across the organisation.

  • Identify control gaps, process inefficiencies, unauthorised workarounds, and weaknesses that expose the Company to financial loss, non-compliance, or operational disruption.

  • Review controls over procurement, expenditure, payroll, asset management, vendor engagements, records management, and other material processes.

  • Assess controls over information systems, cybersecurity, data access, information handling, and technology-enabled business processes in collaboration with the relevant technical owners.

  • Evaluate the adequacy of controls over outsourced services, third-party engagements, and other external dependencies.

  • Recommend practical improvements that strengthen accountability, protect Company resources, and improve operational efficiency.

  • Work with process owners to clarify control requirements, responsibilities, documentation standards, and evidence of compliance.

  • Independently verify that implemented corrective actions address identified root causes and improve control effectiveness.

  • Maintain clear boundaries between independent assurance and operational ownership of business processes.

F. Management, Board Reporting and Risk Intelligence

  • Prepare periodic enterprise risk reports highlighting material exposures, risk trends, incidents, mitigation progress, and matters requiring Management attention.

  • Present internal audit results, significant findings, recurring weaknesses, and overdue corrective actions to the appropriate Management and Board forums.

  • Prepare compliance reports showing the status of applicable obligations, outstanding deliverables, identified breaches, regulatory engagements, and remediation actions.

  • Provide timely notification of critical incidents, suspected material fraud, significant compliance breaches, and critical control failures.

  • Translate technical findings into clear business implications, potential financial exposure, operational consequences, and recommended management actions.

  • Maintain accurate and current risk registers, audit trackers, compliance records, and investigation documentation.

  • Develop dashboards that support monitoring of risk exposure, audit coverage, compliance performance, and closure of corrective actions.

  • Provide quarterly and annual summaries of the Company's risk profile, audit results, compliance status, and control environment, or at the frequency approved by the relevant governance forum.

  • Ensure that reports are supported by reliable evidence, clearly identify accountability, and distinguish confirmed findings from matters still under investigation.

  • Monitor the timely implementation of Management and Board decisions relating to material risk, audit, and compliance matters.

G. Business Risk Oversight and Strategic Advisory

  • Provide independent risk and control advice to Management on business initiatives, new products, material operational changes, and strategic decisions.

  • Assess enterprise-level risks arising from business growth, branch expansion, changes in customer channels, new technology, and third-party arrangements.

  • Monitor relevant credit-related exposures from an enterprise risk perspective without assuming responsibility for day-to-day credit assessment, approvals, credit administration, or collections.

  • Work with functional leaders to assess operational risks affecting customer service, business continuity, data integrity, financial performance, and regulatory standing.

  • Provide risk-based input into policies, procedures, delegated authorities, and governance arrangements.

  • Challenge practices that create material risk, weaken internal controls, or expose the Company to avoidable loss or regulatory action.

  • Recommend proportionate risk mitigation measures that support sustainable growth and protect the Company's assets and reputation.

  • Promote a forward-looking approach to risk management, including the assessment of emerging risks and the potential impact of significant business changes.

  • Support Management in prioritising risk mitigation resources according to materiality, likelihood, potential impact, and the Company's approved risk appetite.

H. Regulatory Engagement, Assurance Coordination and External Relationships

  • Coordinate relevant engagement with regulators and other oversight bodies within the scope of the role and the Company's approved governance arrangements.

  • Support the preparation of accurate and timely responses to regulatory requests, inspections, and compliance reviews.

  • Coordinate with external auditors, independent assurance providers, and professional advisers on matters relating to risk, audit, and compliance.

  • Track external audit findings, regulatory observations, and agreed remediation commitments, ensuring accountability and timely follow-up.

  • Maintain appropriate records of regulatory correspondence, external assurance reports, and management responses.

  • Ensure that regulatory and external assurance issues are escalated to the appropriate internal authorities.

  • Collaborate with Legal and relevant subject-matter experts when specialist interpretation or advice is required.

  • Maintain professional relationships with external stakeholders while protecting the Company's confidentiality, interests, and governance requirements.

I. People Leadership and Functional Effectiveness

  • Provide strategic and operational leadership to the Risk, Internal Audit and Compliance function.

  • Establish clear responsibilities, work plans, performance expectations, and accountability mechanisms for direct reports.

  • Lead, coach, and develop team members to strengthen technical competence, professional judgement, and delivery standards.

  • Establish functional KPIs, review mechanisms, and development priorities aligned with the Company's enterprise objectives.

  • Ensure that departmental resources are allocated according to risk exposure, audit priorities, and compliance requirements.

  • Promote professional integrity, independence, confidentiality, and evidence-based decision-making across the function.

  • Strengthen collaboration with HODs, branch managers, and other stakeholders while maintaining the independence of assurance activities.

  • Identify capability gaps and coordinate relevant professional development and training.

  • Manage departmental budgets, tools, and external service providers within approved limits.

  • Foster a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and proactive risk identification.

  • Monitor departmental performance and implement corrective actions where delivery falls below agreed standards.

5. Qualifications & Experience

Academic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Risk Management, Accounting, Finance, Auditing, Business Administration, Law, or a related field.

  • A relevant postgraduate qualification in Risk Management, Finance, Business Administration, Governance, or a related discipline will be an added advantage.

  • Professional qualifications in internal audit, risk management, accounting, compliance, or related disciplines will be an advantage.

Professional Experience

  • At least 8-10 years of relevant progressive experience in enterprise risk management, internal audit, regulatory compliance, governance, or assurance.

  • Demonstrated experience in a senior management or leadership role with responsibility for risk oversight, audit delivery, compliance monitoring, or internal controls.

  • Experience developing and implementing enterprise risk frameworks, risk registers, risk-based audit plans, compliance programmes, and management reporting arrangements.

  • Demonstrated capability in conducting or overseeing branch audits, operational reviews, control assessments, and investigations.

  • Experience monitoring regulatory obligations, managing compliance issues, and coordinating corrective actions.

  • Experience engaging senior Management, Boards, external auditors, and regulatory authorities.

  • Strong understanding of applicable legal and regulatory requirements relevant to the Company's business and regulatory status.

  • Experience in microfinance, microcredit, digital lending, financial services, or another regulated, multi-branch business will be strongly preferred.

  • Demonstrated experience improving internal controls, addressing recurring audit findings, and strengthening accountability across business functions.

  • Experience leading and developing multidisciplinary teams and managing competing operational and assurance priorities.

6. Leadership & Behavioral Competencies

Strategic and Risk-Based Thinking

  • Connects risk management, audit, and compliance priorities to enterprise strategy and business sustainability.

  • Identifies material and emerging risks and prioritises them according to exposure, likelihood, and potential impact.

  • Balances the need for effective controls with operational efficiency and commercial objectives.

Execution and Results Orientation

  • Translates risk, audit, and compliance priorities into clear work plans, measurable targets, and disciplined execution.

  • Demonstrates ownership and accountability for deliverables, reporting deadlines, and follow-up actions.

  • Drives timely resolution of material findings and persistent control weaknesses.

Integrity and Professional Independence

  • Demonstrates high ethical standards, objectivity, and sound professional judgement.

  • Is willing to challenge decisions or practices that expose the Company to material risk.

  • Maintains confidentiality and protects the independence of assurance activities.

Analytical Decision-Making and Problem-Solving

  • Uses evidence, data, and structured analysis to assess risks and determine appropriate responses.

  • Identifies root causes rather than addressing only the symptoms of control failures.

  • Recommends practical, proportionate, and sustainable solutions.

Leadership and Team Development

  • Builds a capable, accountable, and technically competent team.

  • Sets clear expectations, provides constructive feedback, and addresses underperformance.

  • Develops professional capability and promotes continuous improvement.

Stakeholder Management and Collaboration

  • Builds effective working relationships with the Board, Management, HODs, branch leaders, and relevant external stakeholders.

  • Influences stakeholders to address control weaknesses and meet agreed obligations.

  • Communicates sensitive findings and complex risk matters clearly and professionally.

Adaptability and Resilience

  • Operates effectively in a fast-paced, multi-branch business environment.

  • Manages competing priorities while maintaining quality, independence, and professional standards.

  • Responds constructively to changing risks, regulatory developments, and business requirements.

Accountability and Ethical Leadership

  • Promotes transparency, ownership, and responsible decision-making.

  • Encourages early reporting of incidents, errors, and control weaknesses.

  • Reinforces a culture in which accountability and corrective action are valued.

7. Industry and Business Environment

The ideal candidate will have experience in one or more of the following environments:

  • Microfinance and microcredit institutions.

  • Digital credit providers and digital lending businesses.

  • Banks and other financial services institutions.

  • Fintech organisations operating in lending, payments, or related financial services.

  • Regulated businesses with complex operational processes, multiple branches, or geographically distributed teams.

  • Other organisations with established enterprise risk, internal audit, compliance, and governance requirements.

Candidates with direct experience overseeing enterprise risk, internal audit, and regulatory compliance within a multi-branch financial services environment will be particularly relevant to the role.

Experience operating within the applicable regulatory environment and engaging relevant regulatory and assurance stakeholders will be an advantage.
